# 1. Repository Overview (Evidence-Backed)
- Project name and purpose (cite README/package metadata): `InterviewAI Pro` is described as an AI-first mock interview coach with a React/Vite frontend, Express/Firebase backend, and local Ollama + Whisper pipelines (`README.md:1`, `README.md:3`, `README.md:21`, `README.md:23`, `package.json:2`, `server/package.json:2`).
- Repo structure (monorepo vs single app). List major directories and what they contain: monorepo-style split between root SPA and `server/` backend with shared docs and workflows (`README.md:42`, `README.md:48`, `README.md:53`).
- Tech stack summary (frontend, backend, DB, auth, AI services, storage, deployment)
  - Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind, D3/Recharts, Firebase web SDK (`package.json:29`, `package.json:41`, `package.json:44`, `package.json:55`).
  - Backend: Express, Firebase Admin, JWT, Socket.IO, Helmet/CORS/rate limiting (`server/package.json:17`, `server/package.json:20`, `server/package.json:24`, `server/package.json:30`, `server/package.json:22`, `server/package.json:14`, `server/package.json:18`).
  - DB/storage: Firestore + Realtime Database stores (`server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:15`, `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:16`, `server/src/config/firebase.js:187`).
  - Auth: Firebase token verification + role/org middleware (`server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js:13`, `server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js:164`, `src/components/ProtectedRoute.jsx:11`).
  - AI services: Ollama prompts + local faster-whisper + MediaPipe (`server/src/services/llm.service.js:19`, `server/whisper_server.py:84`, `src/hooks/useInterviewAnalytics.js:15`).
  - Deployment: GitHub Actions CI + Pages deploy (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:1`).

# 4. Architecture & Data Flow (AS IMPLEMENTED)
Describe architecture with evidence:
- Client/UI layer: React Router SPA with ProtectedRoute role checks and org permission filtering (`src/Routes.jsx:62`, `src/components/ProtectedRoute.jsx:11`, `src/utils/rolePermissions.js:15`).
- API/backend layer: Express app and route mounting under `/api/*` (`server/src/server.js:43`, `server/src/routes/index.js:26-47`).
- DB/storage layer: Firestore and Realtime DB stores (`server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:15-29`, `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:72`, `server/src/config/firebase.js:187`).
- AI service layer: Ollama prompt service, local faster-whisper server, MediaPipe browser analysis (`server/src/services/llm.service.js:74`, `server/whisper_server.py:84`, `src/hooks/useInterviewAnalytics.js:15`).
- Auth layer: Firebase token verification + account-type/organization-role middleware (`server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js:13`, `server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js:135`, `server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js:164`).
- Deployment layer: CI + GitHub Pages workflows (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:1`).

Then map end-to-end flows (each must include routes + files + DB models):

A) Start an interview session
- Entry UI route: `/practice-interview-setup` creates interview and navigates to `/live-interview-session?interviewId=...` (`src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx:153-165`).
- API endpoints called: interview create/start/get (`src/services/interviewBackendSync.js:27`, `src/services/interviewBackendSync.js:218`, `src/services/interviewBackendSync.js:51`).
- DB writes/reads: interview create + generated questions + updates (`server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:398`, `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:471`, `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js:456`).
- External services called: Ollama question generation (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:401`, `server/src/services/llm.service.js:74`).
- Failure handling/fallbacks: role/status guards and frontend fail-open for sync (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:158-188`, `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js:183-185`).

B) Practice mode flow
- Entry UI route: `/practice-interview-setup` candidate flow (`src/Routes.jsx:146`, `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx:128`).
- API endpoints called: `POST /api/interviews/create` with `mode: PRACTICE` (`src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx:136-153`).
- DB writes/reads: practice interview and question pipeline (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:273-279`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:386-403`).
- External services called: LLM question/evaluation prompts (`server/src/services/llm.service.js:137`, `server/src/services/llm.service.js:267`).
- Failure handling/fallbacks: candidate-only guard + UI error state (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:158-160`, `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx:168-171`).

C) Hiring mode flow
- Entry UI route: company protected routes and backend creation checks (`src/Routes.jsx:80-140`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:162`).
- API endpoints called: interview create plus job/application/invitation modules (`server/src/routes/index.js:32-47`).
- DB writes/reads: candidate/job/application validation and hiring interview persistence (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:216-267`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:275-280`).
- External services called: same question generation path on interview start (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:401`).
- Failure handling/fallbacks: org approval/role/feature-flag checks (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:170-181`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:205-213`).

D) Audio/video capture (if exists)
- Entry UI route: `/live-interview-session` (`src/Routes.jsx:64`) with camera/mic initialization (`src/pages/live-interview-session/components/CandidateVideoFeed.jsx:42`).
- API endpoints called: `/api/video/config`, `/api/video/session/:interviewId` (`server/src/routes/video.routes.js:9`, `server/src/routes/video.routes.js:12`, `server/src/routes/video.routes.js:21`).
- DB writes/reads: WebRTC session upsert/read (`server/src/controllers/video.controller.js:40`, `server/src/controllers/video.controller.js:67`).
- External services called: browser `getUserMedia` + `MediaRecorder` (`src/pages/live-interview-session/components/CandidateVideoFeed.jsx:42`, `src/services/audioRecorderService.js:32`).
- Failure handling/fallbacks: camera/session access errors logged and guarded (`src/pages/live-interview-session/components/CandidateVideoFeed.jsx:58`, `server/src/controllers/video.controller.js:34`, `server/src/controllers/video.controller.js:64`).
- Full-session persistent media recording: UNKNOWN / NOT VERIFIED.

E) Transcription (if exists)
- Entry UI route: AI interviewer speech stop/listen flow (`src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js:118-136`).
- API endpoints called: local whisper `/health` and `/transcribe` (`src/services/localWhisperService.js:45`, `src/services/localWhisperService.js:114`, `server/whisper_server.py:84`).
- DB writes/reads: transcribed answer text is submitted to interview answer endpoint (`src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js:305`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:628`).
- External services called: faster-whisper local model and browser SpeechRecognition fallback (`server/whisper_server.py:30`, `src/services/speechRecognitionService.js:10`).
- Failure handling/fallbacks: health checks + fallback path in hook (`src/services/localWhisperService.js:38`, `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js:127-136`).

F) Scoring (LLM + rubric)
- Entry UI route: answer submit from live flow (`src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js:300`).
- API endpoints called: `POST /api/interviews/:id/answer` and `POST /api/interviews/:id/end` (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:604`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:446`).
- DB writes/reads: per-question score/feedback and interview-level summary (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:645-651`, `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:463-469`).
- External services called: STAR and summary prompts via Ollama (`server/src/services/llm.service.js:274-303`, `server/src/services/llm.service.js:221-249`).
- Failure handling/fallbacks: scoring errors logged while request proceeds (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:652-654`).

G) Saving results + dashboards
- Entry UI route: candidate/company/system-admin dashboards (`src/Routes.jsx:157`, `src/Routes.jsx:80`, `src/Routes.jsx:219`).
- API endpoints called: analytics metrics and admin fairness endpoints (`src/pages/candidate-dashboard/index.jsx:108-109`, `src/pages/company-dashboard/index.jsx:110-112`, `server/src/routes/admin.routes.js:285`).
- DB writes/reads: interview completion scores + review overrides/calibration (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js:463-469`, `server/src/controllers/review.controller.js:136-144`, `server/src/controllers/admin.controller.js:1733-1789`).
- External services called: no additional external AI call required for rendering dashboards.
- Failure handling/fallbacks: dashboard loading uses Promise settlement and error UI (`src/pages/company-dashboard/index.jsx:108-139`, `src/pages/candidate-dashboard/index.jsx:106-130`).

000001: # ATS Scale Hardening (2026-02-12)
000002: 
000003: ## Objective
000004: 
000005: Upgrade the core ATS behavior to align with large-scale ATS patterns:
000006: 
000007: - No unsafe destructive job deletion.
000008: - Structured and auditable application dispositions.
000009: - Candidate transparency when a role is closed after applications exist.
000010: - Consistent lifecycle metadata for reporting and compliance.
000011: 
000012: ## External ATS reference baseline
000013: 
000014: The lifecycle model in this implementation is aligned with enterprise ATS guidance and behavior:
000015: 
000016: - Greenhouse: rejection reasons are typically required and treated as structured analytics data.
000017:   - https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038321491-Rejection-reason-requirement
000018:   - https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207305363-Rejection-reasons-overview
000019: - Workable: disqualification reasons are configurable/optionally mandatory and support reporting and automation.
000020:   - https://help.workable.com/hc/en-us/articles/7263547772055-Disqualification-reasons-overview
000021:   - https://help.workable.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004710893-Disqualifying-rejecting-candidates
000022: - SmartRecruiters: candidate-facing status model includes archived substatuses such as `WITHDRAWN_BY_APPLICANT` and `DELETED_BY_COMPANY`.
000023:   - https://developers.smartrecruiters.com/changelog/candidate-status-api
000024:   - https://developers.smartrecruiters.com/reference/publicgetstatus
000025: - Lever: archive/close workflow and archive reasons are first-class lifecycle operations, including bulk handling and optional candidate communication.
000026:   - https://lever-old.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/204502125-Archiving-opportunities
000027:   - https://lever-old.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360030950011-Bulk-archiving-opportunities
000028:   - https://lever-old.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360042220512-Creating-and-managing-job-postings
000029: 
000030: ## Implemented Architecture Changes
000031: 
000032: ### 1) Job deletion moved to ATS soft-delete semantics
000033:

000037: - `server/src/controllers/job.controller.js`

000046:   - `deletionMode` (`SOFT`)
000047: - `jobStore.getById()` excludes soft-deleted jobs unless explicitly requested via options.
000048: - Organization job lists also exclude soft-deleted jobs by default.
000049: - Public job visibility now rejects soft-deleted jobs.
000050: 
000051: Result:

000001: # Company Dashboard Dummy Data Cleanup Report
000002: 
000003: **Date:** January 15, 2026  
000004: **Author:** GitHub Copilot  
000005: 
000006: ---
000007: 
000008: ## What is Dummy Data?
000009: 
000010: **Dummy data** (also called placeholder data, mock data, or sample data) refers to hardcoded static values used during UI development to:
000011: 
000012: 1. **Visualize the design** before real backend APIs are implemented
000013: 2. **Test layout and styling** with realistic-looking content
000014: 3. **Demonstrate functionality** to stakeholders during development
000015: 4. **Serve as fallback values** when real data isn't available yet
000016: 
000017: In this project, dummy data was used extensively while building the Company Dashboard UI components. This allowed the frontend to be developed independently of the backend, enabling parallel development.
000018: 
000019: ---
000020: 
000021: ## Components Analyzed
000022: 
000023: The following files were thoroughly analyzed:
000024: 
000025: | File | Location |
000026: |------|----------|
000027: | `index.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/` |
000028: | `OverviewPanel.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000029: | `HiringMetrics.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000030: | `CandidateTable.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000031: | `CandidatePipeline.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000032: | `QuickActions.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000033: | `ReviewerPanel.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000034: | `AIChatAssistant.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000035: | `InvitationManager.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000036: | `CandidateManager.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000037: | `ApplicationsManager.jsx` | `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/` |
000038: 
000039: ---
000040: 
000041: ## Summary of Changes Made
000042: 
000043: ### ✅ Dummy Data REMOVED and Replaced with Real Data
000044: 
000045: #### 1. **OverviewPanel.jsx**
000046: - **Before:** Default props had hardcoded values: `activeJobPostings = 12`, `pendingReviews = 8`, `upcomingInterviews = 5`
000047: - **After:** Changed to `0` as defaults since the parent (`index.jsx`) already passes real data from API calls
000048: - **Reason:** The parent component fetches real data via `apiClient.analytics.getCompanyMetrics()` and `apiClient.interviews.getCompanyInterviews()` and passes it to this component
000049: 
000050: #### 2. **CandidateTable.jsx**
000051: - **Before:** Had a complete fallback array of 5 fake candidates:
000052:   - Sarah Johnson (Frontend Developer)
000053:   - Michael Chen (Backend Developer)
000054:   - Emily Rodriguez (UX Designer)
000055:   - David Wilson (Full Stack Developer)
000056:   - Lisa Thompson (Product Manager)
000057:   - Included fake profile photos from Unsplash URLs
000058:   - Random AI score generation: `Math.floor(Math.random() * 20) + 80`
000059: - **After:** Removed entire fallback array. Component now:
000060:   - Shows real interview data only
000061:   - Displays proper empty state when no interviews exist
000062:   - Shows "—" for AI scores that haven't been calculated yet
000063: - **Reason:** Real interview data comes from `apiClient.interviews.getCompanyInterviews()` which is properly implemented
000064: 
000065: #### 3. **HiringMetrics.jsx**
000066: - **Before:** Had multiple issues:
000067:   - Hardcoded metric fallbacks: `'18 days'`, `'4.8/5'`, `'94%'`, `'87%'`
000068:   - Hardcoded change indicators: `'-3 days'`, `'+0.2'`, `'+2%'`, `'+5%'`
000069:   - Unused hardcoded `recentActivity` array with fake activity
000070:   - Fallback values: `totalInterviews = 156`, `hiresMade = 42`, `successRate = 89`
000071: - **After:** 
000072:   - Calculates all metrics from real interview data using `useMemo`
000073:   - Shows "N/A" for metrics that backend doesn't yet compute (e.g., averageTimeToHire)
000074:   - Uses real `averageScore` from backend when available
000075:   - Removed fake `recentActivity` array (was never used in UI)
000076:   - Removed hardcoded change indicators (historical comparison not yet implemented)
000077:   - Performance Overview section now shows calculated real values
000078: - **Reason:** Backend provides `totalInterviews`, `completedInterviews`, `averageScore`, `inProgressInterviews` via `apiClient.analytics.getCompanyMetrics()`
000079: 
000080: #### 4. **index.jsx (heroHighlights)**

000001: # Comprehensive Interview Body Language Detection Guide
000002: 
000003: ## Overview
000004: 
000005: This document outlines the complete detection and scoring system implemented for analyzing interview body language. The system uses MediaPipe's PoseLandmarker (33 body landmarks) and FaceLandmarker (478 facial landmarks) to provide real-time analysis.
000006: 
000007: ---
000008: 
000009: ## Table of Contents
000010: 
000011: 1. [Posture Analysis](#1-posture-analysis)
000012: 2. [Facial Analysis](#2-facial-analysis)
000013: 3. [Eye Contact & Gaze](#3-eye-contact--gaze)
000014: 4. [Hand & Body Movement](#4-hand--body-movement)
000015: 5. [Scoring System](#5-scoring-system)
000016: 6. [Reference Thresholds](#6-reference-thresholds)
000017: 7. [Usage Guide](#7-usage-guide)
000018: 
000019: ---
000020: 
000021: ## 1. Posture Analysis
000022: 
000023: ### 1.1 Shoulder Metrics
000024: 
000025: | Metric | Description | Ideal Value | Threshold |
000026: |--------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
000027: | **Shoulder Slope** | Y-axis difference between shoulders | 0 (level) | <0.015 = Excellent, <0.030 = Good |
000028: | **Shoulder Width** | Distance between shoulders (openness) | 0.38+ | <0.26 = Closed posture |
000029: | **Shoulder Angle** | Rotation angle of shoulder line | 0° | <5° = Level |
000030: | **Shoulder Tension** | Height relative to ears | 0.12 | <0.06 = Tense |
000031: 
000032: **What We Detect:**
000033: - Uneven shoulders (indicates tension/poor posture)
000034: - Closed shoulders (defensive body language)
000035: - Raised shoulders (stress indicator)
000036: - Shoulder roll (slouching)
000037: 
000038: ### 1.2 Spine/Back Alignment
000039: 
000040: | Metric | Description | Ideal Value | Threshold |
000041: |--------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
000042: | **Forward Lean** | Z-axis position relative to hips | 0 to 0.02 | >0.08 = Poor posture |
000043: | **Lateral Lean** | X-axis deviation from center | 0 | >0.06 = Noticeable |
000044: | **Vertical Angle** | Angle from vertical | 0° | <10° = Good |
000045: | **Upright Status** | Combined alignment check | true | Boolean |
000046: 
000047: **What We Detect:**
000048: - Slouching (forward lean)
000049: - Side leaning (lateral lean)
000050: - Torso rotation (turned away)
000051: - Engagement (slight forward lean shows interest)
000052: 
000053: ### 1.3 Head Position
000054: 
000055: | Metric | Description | Ideal Value | Threshold |
000056: |--------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
000057: | **Head Tilt** | Left/right tilt (roll) | 0° | <7° = Slight |
000058: | **Head Turn** | Left/right rotation (yaw) | 0° | <20° = Slight |
000059: | **Head Pitch** | Up/down angle | 0° | <12° = Level |
000060: | **Forward Position** | Turtle neck detection | 0 | >0.06 = Fair |
000061: 
000062: **What We Detect:**
000063: - Head tilting (may indicate confusion or interest)
000064: - Looking away (turned head)
000065: - Looking up/down (disengagement or submission)
000066: - Forward head posture (common computer posture issue)
000067: 
000068: ---
000069: 
000070: ## 2. Facial Analysis
000071: 
000072: ### 2.1 Eye Metrics (EAR - Eye Aspect Ratio)
000073: 
000074: | Metric | Description | Normal Range | Detection |
000075: |--------|-------------|--------------|-----------|
000076: | **EAR** | Ratio of eye height to width | 0.20-0.35 | Blink <0.16 |
000077: | **Blink Rate** | Blinks per minute | 15-20 | >25 = Stressed |
000078: | **Eye Openness** | How open eyes appear | 0.26+ | <0.20 = Drowsy |
000079: | **Eye Asymmetry** | Difference between eyes | <0.03 | >0.10 = Winking |
000080: 
000081: **What We Detect:**
000082: - Blinks (normal, excessive, or prolonged)
000083: - Drowsiness (low EAR sustained)
000084: - Alertness (normal open eyes)
000085: - Squinting (concentration or difficulty seeing)
000086: - Eye asymmetry (winking or facial issues)
000087: 
000088: ### 2.2 Face Orientation
000089: 
000090: | Metric | Description | Ideal Range | Warning Threshold |
000091: |--------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
000092: | **Yaw** | Left/right rotation | ±8° | >25° = Looking away |
000093: | **Pitch** | Up/down tilt | ±8° | >20° = Looking up/down |
000094: | **Roll** | Head tilt | ±5° | >18° = Significant tilt |
000095: 
000096: **What We Detect:**
000097: - Direct gaze (facing camera)
000098: - Slight turns (minor deviation)
000099: - Looking away (significant turn)
000100: - Head tilt (interest or confusion)
000101: 
000102: ### 2.3 Mouth Analysis (MAR - Mouth Aspect Ratio)
000103: 
000104: | Metric | Description | Threshold | Detection |
000105: |--------|-------------|-----------|-----------|
000106: | **MAR** | Ratio of mouth height to width | 0.05-0.50 | Speaking >0.12 |
000107: | **Speaking** | Active speech detection | >0.12 | Boolean |
000108: | **Lip Compression** | Pressed lips | <0.03 | Stress indicator |
000109: | **Mouth Openness** | Open/closed state | 0.05 | closed/open/wide |
000110: 
000111: **What We Detect:**
000112: - Speaking detection (useful for turn-taking)
000113: - Yawning (wide open mouth)
000114: - Lip compression (stress/tension)
000115: - Natural mouth position
000116: 
000117: ### 2.4 Smile Detection
000118: 
000119: | Metric | Description | Threshold | Notes |
000120: |--------|-------------|-----------|-------|
000121: | **Is Smiling** | Smile detected | Lip corner lift >0.015 | Boolean |
000122: | **Smile Intensity** | Strength of smile | 0-1 scale | 0.7+ = Broad |
000123: | **Smile Symmetry** | Left/right balance | >0.85 | Genuine indicator |
000124: 
000125: **What We Detect:**
000126: - Genuine smiles (symmetric)
000127: - Forced smiles (asymmetric)
000128: - Smile intensity (slight to broad)
000129: - Neutral expression
000130: 
000131: ### 2.5 Eyebrow Analysis
000132: 
000133: | Metric | Description | Threshold | Emotion |
000134: |--------|-------------|-----------|---------|
000135: | **Raised** | Eyebrows lifted | >0.012 | Surprise/Interest |
000136: | **Furrowed** | Eyebrows lowered | <-0.008 | Concern/Concentration |
000137: | **Asymmetric** | One raised | >0.025 | Skepticism |
000138: 
000139: **What We Detect:**
000140: - Raised eyebrows (surprise, interest)
000141: - Furrowed eyebrows (confusion, concentration)
000142: - Skeptical expression (one raised)
000143: - Neutral position
000144: 
000145: ---
000146: 
000147: ## 3. Eye Contact & Gaze
000148: 
000149: ### 3.1 Iris Tracking
000150: 
000151: | Metric | Description | Good Range | Warning |
000152: |--------|-------------|------------|---------|
000153: | **Iris Position** | Position within eye socket | Center (0.5, 0.5) | Deviation >0.15 |
000154: | **Gaze Direction** | Where person is looking | center | left/right/up/down |
000155: | **At Camera** | Looking at camera | true | false = Aversion |
000156: 
000157: ### 3.2 Eye Contact Quality
000158: 
000159: | Level | Percentage | Description |
000160: |-------|------------|-------------|
000161: | Excellent | 80%+ | Strong engagement |
000162: | Good | 65-80% | Acceptable contact |
000163: | Fair | 50-65% | Room for improvement |
000164: | Poor | 35-50% | Significant aversion |
000165: | Avoiding | <35% | May appear evasive |
000166: 
000167: ---
000168: 
000169: ## 4. Hand & Body Movement
000170: 
000171: ### 4.1 Hand Movement Detection
000172: 
000173: | Metric | Description | Threshold | Status |
000174: |--------|-------------|-----------|--------|
000175: | **Movement Velocity** | Frame-to-frame movement | <0.015 | Calm |
000176: | **Average Movement** | 30-frame average | <0.035 | Moderate |
000177: | **Fidgeting** | Sustained movement | >0.04 | Fidgeting detected |
000178: | **Hand Visibility** | Hands in frame | 0-1 | Higher = Better |
000179: 
000180: ### 4.2 Body Stability
000181: 
000182: | Metric | Description | Good Range | Warning |
000183: |--------|-------------|------------|---------|
000184: | **Stability Score** | Overall stillness | >0.8 | <0.6 = Restless |
000185: | **Body Movement** | Average movement | <0.012 | >0.045 = Active |
000186: | **Is Stable** | Composite check | true | false = Movement |
000187: 
000188: ### 4.3 Nervous Behavior Indicators
000189: 
000190: | Behavior | Detection Method | Threshold |
000191: |----------|------------------|-----------|
000192: | **Swaying** | Lateral oscillation | >0.03/second |
000193: | **Bouncing** | Vertical oscillation | >0.02/second |
000194: | **Self-touching** | Hand near face | <0.08 distance |
000195: | **Object fidgeting** | Small rapid movements | >0.05/frame |
000196: 
000197: ---
000198: 
000199: ## 5. Scoring System
000200: 
000201: ### 5.1 Component Weights
000202: 
000203: | Component | Weight | Sub-components |
000204: |-----------|--------|----------------|
000205: | **Posture** | 25% | Shoulders (40%), Spine (40%), Head (20%) |
000206: | **Eye Contact** | 25% | Gaze (50%), Orientation (30%), Openness (20%) |
000207: | **Expression** | 15% | Smile (50%), Eyebrows (30%), Natural (20%) |
000208: | **Body Language** | 15% | Hand steadiness (50%), Stability (50%) |
000209: | **Engagement** | 10% | Lean (30%), Eye contact (40%), Expression (30%) |
000210: | **Professional Presence** | 10% | Framing (50%), Camera angle (30%), Consistency (20%) |
000211: 
000212: ### 5.2 Score Levels
000213: 
000214: | Score Range | Level | Color | Feedback Priority |
000215: |-------------|-------|-------|-------------------|
000216: | 90-100 | Excellent | Green | Positive reinforcement |
000217: | 75-89 | Good | Light Green | Minor suggestions |
000218: | 60-74 | Fair | Yellow | Improvement tips |
000219: | 40-59 | Needs Improvement | Orange | Active guidance |
000220: | 0-39 | Poor | Red | Immediate correction |
000221: 
000222: ---
000223: 
000224: ## 6. Reference Thresholds
000225: 
000226: ### Quick Reference Card
000227: 
000228: ```
000229: POSTURE
000230: ├── Shoulder Slope: <0.03 (Good), <0.06 (Fair), >0.10 (Poor)
000231: ├── Forward Lean: -0.02 to 0.02 (Good), >0.08 (Poor)
000232: └── Head Level: <7° tilt (Good), >18° (Significant)
000233: 
000234: EYES
000235: ├── EAR (Open): 0.20-0.35
000236: ├── EAR (Blink): <0.16
000237: ├── Blink Rate: 15-20/min (Normal), >25/min (Stressed)
000238: └── Drowsy: EAR <0.20 sustained
000239: 
000240: FACE ORIENTATION
000241: ├── Yaw (Good): <15°, (Looking Away): >35°
000242: ├── Pitch (Good): <12°, (Extreme): >30°
000243: └── Roll (Good): <10°, (Significant): >20°
000244: 
000245: GAZE
000246: ├── Center Tolerance: ±0.15
000247: ├── At Camera: Deviation <0.10
000248: └── Looking Away: Deviation >0.25
000249: 
000250: MOUTH
000251: ├── Closed: MAR <0.05
000252: ├── Speaking: MAR >0.12
000253: └── Wide Open: MAR >0.35
000254: 
000255: MOVEMENT
000256: ├── Calm: <0.015/frame
000257: ├── Fidgeting: >0.04/frame sustained
000258: └── Stable: <0.025 average movement
000259: ```
000260: 
000261: ---
000262: 
000263: ## 7. Usage Guide
000264: 
000265: ### 7.1 Accessing the Detection System
000266: 
000267: 1. Navigate to **System Admin Dashboard**
000268: 2. Click on **Research Tools** tab
000269: 3. Select **Video Recorder** sub-tab
000270: 4. Click **Start Camera**
000271: 5. MediaPipe will initialize automatically
000272: 
000273: ### 7.2 Understanding the Metrics Panel
000274: 
000275: The comprehensive metrics panel shows:
000276: 
000277: 1. **Overall Score Banner**: Composite interview presence score (0-100)
000278: 2. **Component Breakdown**: Individual scores for each category
000279: 3. **Detailed Metrics**: Raw values for all detection parameters
000280: 4. **Status Indicators**: Color-coded status for quick assessment
000281: 
000282: ### 7.3 Recording Reference Videos
000283: 
000284: To build your MediaPipe reference library:
000285: 
000286: 1. Select a **Category** (Posture, Head Position, Eye Contact, etc.)
000287: 2. Choose **Example Type** (Good or Bad)
000288: 3. Add a descriptive name
000289: 4. Click **Start Recording**
000290: 5. Demonstrate the behavior for 5-15 seconds
000291: 6. Click **Stop Recording**
000292: 7. Download or analyze the recording
000293: 
000294: ### 7.4 Interpreting Results
000295: 
000296: | Color | Meaning | Action |
000297: |-------|---------|--------|
000298: | 🟢 Green | Excellent/Good | Maintain current behavior |
000299: | 🟡 Yellow | Fair | Minor adjustment needed |
000300: | 🟠 Orange | Needs Improvement | Focus on this area |
000301: | 🔴 Red | Poor | Immediate attention required |
000302: 
000303: ---

000001: # Email Deliverability Guide
000002: 
000003: ## Why Your Emails Are Going to Spam
000004: 
000005: Emails sent via SendGrid are landing in spam because of **authentication issues**. The main problem is using a Gmail address (`akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com`) as the sender with SendGrid.
000006: 
000007: ### The Problem
000008: 
000009: When you send emails "from" a Gmail address through SendGrid:
000010: 1. **SPF fails**: Gmail's SPF record doesn't authorize SendGrid to send on its behalf
000011: 2. **DKIM fails**: Gmail's DKIM keys don't match SendGrid's signing
000012: 3. **Looks like spoofing**: Email providers see this as a phishing attempt
000013: 
000014: This is the **#1 reason** your emails go to spam.
000015: 
000016: ---
000017: 
000018: ## Solutions (Choose One)
000019: 
000020: ### Option 1: Use a Custom Domain (Recommended)
000021: 
000022: This is the best solution for long-term deliverability.
000023: 
000024: 1. **Get a domain** (e.g., `interviewai-pro.com`)
000025: 2. **Set up domain authentication in SendGrid**:
000026:    - Go to SendGrid Dashboard → Settings → Sender Authentication
000027:    - Click "Authenticate Your Domain"
000028:    - Follow the DNS setup instructions
000029:    - This adds SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records
000030: 
000031: 3. **Update your `.env`**:
000032:    ```env
000033:    FROM_EMAIL=noreply@interviewai-pro.com
000034:    FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000035:    ```
000036: 
000037: 4. **Benefits**:
000038:    - Emails pass SPF, DKIM, DMARC checks
000039:    - Better inbox placement
000040:    - Professional appearance
000041:    - Build sender reputation
000042: 
000043: ### Option 2: Single Sender Verification (Quick Fix)
000044: 
000045: If you don't have a custom domain yet:
000046: 
000047: 1. **Verify your sender in SendGrid**:
000048:    - Go to SendGrid Dashboard → Settings → Sender Authentication
000049:    - Click "Verify a Single Sender"
000050:    - Add your Gmail address
000051:    - Complete the verification email
000052: 
000053: 2. **Limitations**:
000054:    - Still has authentication issues
000055:    - Lower deliverability than domain authentication
000056:    - May still go to spam for some recipients
000057: 
000058: ### Option 3: Use Gmail SMTP Directly
000059: 
000060: Send through Gmail's own SMTP servers (bypasses SendGrid):
000061: 
000062: 1. **Enable 2-Factor Authentication** on your Google account
000063: 
000064: 2. **Create an App Password**:
000065:    - Go to https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords
000066:    - Generate a password for "Mail"
000067: 
000068: 3. **Update your `.env`**:
000069:    ```env
000070:    EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp
000071:    SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
000072:    SMTP_PORT=587
000073:    SMTP_USER=akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com
000074:    SMTP_PASS=your-app-password
000075:    FROM_EMAIL=akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com
000076:    FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000077:    ```
000078: 
000079: 4. **Benefits**:
000080:    - Proper Gmail authentication
000081:    - Better deliverability for Gmail addresses
000082:    - Free
000083: 
000084: 5. **Limitations**:
000085:    - Daily sending limits (~500/day for personal accounts)
000086:    - May be flagged if sending bulk emails
000087: 
000088: ---
000089: 
000090: ## Code Improvements Already Made
000091: 
000092: The email service has been updated with:
000093: 
000094: 1. **✅ Plain text versions** - All emails now have both HTML and plain text
000095: 2. **✅ Disabled tracking** - Click/open tracking disabled (can trigger spam filters)
000096: 3. **✅ Email categories** - Better tracking and filtering
000097: 4. **✅ Proper headers** - List-Unsubscribe, X-Priority, Precedence headers
000098: 5. **✅ Lightweight logo** - Replaced large image with CSS-based logo
000099: 6. **✅ Warnings** - Logs warning when using free email domains
000100: 
000101: ---
000102: 
000103: ## Quick Test: Switch to Gmail SMTP
000104: 
000105: To quickly test if the authentication is the issue, switch to Gmail SMTP:
000106: 
000107: 1. Update `server/.env`:
000108:    ```env
000109:    EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp
000110:    SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
000111:    SMTP_PORT=587
000112:    SMTP_USER=akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com
000113:    SMTP_PASS=<your-gmail-app-password>
000114:    ```
000115: 
000116: 2. Restart the server
000117: 
000118: 3. Send a test email
000119: 
000120: If emails now go to inbox, the issue was SendGrid authentication.
000121: 
000122: ---
000123: 
000124: ## Long-term Recommendations
000125: 
000126: 1. **Get a custom domain** ($10-15/year from Namecheap, Google Domains, etc.)
000127: 2. **Set up domain authentication** in SendGrid
000128: 3. **Warm up your sending reputation**:
000129:    - Start with small volumes
000130:    - Send to engaged recipients first
000131:    - Monitor bounce rates and spam complaints
000132: 4. **Monitor deliverability**:
000133:    - Check SendGrid's Email Activity Feed
000134:    - Use tools like mail-tester.com to test
000135: 
000136: ---
000137: 
000138: ## Checking Your Email Score
000139: 
000140: Use these free tools to test your emails:
000141: 
000142: 1. **Mail Tester**: https://www.mail-tester.com/
000143:    - Send an email to their test address
000144:    - Get a detailed spam score analysis
000145: 
000146: 2. **SendGrid Email Activity**:
000147:    - Dashboard → Activity → Email Activity
000148:    - See delivery status and any issues
000149: 
000150: 3. **Gmail Postmaster Tools**: https://postmaster.google.com/
000151:    - Monitor your domain's reputation with Gmail
000152: 
000153: ---
000154: 
000155: ## Environment Variables Reference
000156: 
000157: ```env
000158: # Option 1: SendGrid with Custom Domain (Best)
000159: EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid
000160: SENDGRID_API_KEY=your-api-key
000161: FROM_EMAIL=noreply@yourdomain.com
000162: FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000163: 
000164: # Option 2: Gmail SMTP (Quick)
000165: EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp
000166: SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
000167: SMTP_PORT=587
000168: SMTP_USER=your-email@gmail.com
000169: SMTP_PASS=your-app-password
000170: FROM_EMAIL=your-email@gmail.com
000171: FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000172: 
000173: # Option 3: Development Only
000174: EMAIL_PROVIDER=console
000175: ```
000176: 
```

000001: # Email Service Setup Guide
000002: 
000003: This guide explains how to configure free email services for InterviewAI Pro. The system supports multiple email providers, and you can choose the one that best fits your needs.
000004: 
000005: ## 📧 Available Email Providers
000006: 
000007: ### 1. **SendGrid** (Recommended - Easiest Setup)
000008: - **Free Tier**: 100 emails/day forever
000009: - **Best For**: Production use, reliable delivery
000010: - **Setup Time**: ~5 minutes
000011: 
000012: ### 2. **Gmail SMTP** (Free)
000013: - **Free Tier**: Unlimited (with rate limits ~500/day)
000014: - **Best For**: Development, small-scale production
000015: - **Setup Time**: ~10 minutes
000016: 
000017: ### 3. **Outlook SMTP** (Free)
000018: - **Free Tier**: Unlimited (with rate limits)
000019: - **Best For**: Development, small-scale production
000020: - **Setup Time**: ~10 minutes
000021: 
000022: ---
000023: 
000024: ## 🚀 Option 1: SendGrid Setup (Recommended)
000025: 
000026: SendGrid is the easiest and most reliable option for production use.
000027: 
000028: ### Step 1: Create SendGrid Account
000029: 1. Go to [https://sendgrid.com](https://sendgrid.com)
000030: 2. Click **"Start for Free"**
000031: 3. Sign up with your email address
000032: 4. Verify your email address
000033: 
000034: ### Step 2: Create API Key
000035: 1. Log in to your SendGrid dashboard
000036: 2. Go to **Settings** → **API Keys**
000037: 3. Click **"Create API Key"**
000038: 4. Name it: `InterviewAI Pro`
000039: 5. Select **"Full Access"** or **"Restricted Access"** with Mail Send permissions
000040: 6. Click **"Create & View"**
000041: 7. **Copy the API key immediately** (you won't be able to see it again!)
000042: 
000043: ### Step 3: Configure Environment Variables
000044: Add to your `server/.env` file:
000045: 
000046: ```env
000047: EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid
000048: SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.your-api-key-here
000049: FROM_EMAIL=your-verified-email@example.com
000050: FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000051: ```
000052: 
000053: ### Step 4: Verify Sender Email (Optional but Recommended)
000054: 1. In SendGrid dashboard, go to **Settings** → **Sender Authentication**
000055: 2. Click **"Verify a Single Sender"**
000056: 3. Fill in your email details
000057: 4. Check your email and click the verification link
000058: 
000059: ### Step 5: Test
000060: Restart your server and test by rejecting/approving an organization. Check the server logs for email sending confirmation.
000061: 
000062: ---
000063: 
000064: ## 📮 Option 2: Gmail SMTP Setup
000065: 
000066: Gmail SMTP is free and works well for development and small-scale production.
000067: 
000068: ### Step 1: Enable 2-Factor Authentication
000069: 1. Go to [Google Account Security](https://myaccount.google.com/security)
000070: 2. Enable **2-Step Verification** if not already enabled
000071: 
000072: ### Step 2: Generate App Password
000073: 1. Go to [App Passwords](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords)
000074: 2. Select **"Mail"** and **"Other (Custom name)"**
000075: 3. Enter: `InterviewAI Pro`
000076: 4. Click **"Generate"**
000077: 5. **Copy the 16-character password** (you'll need this)
000078: 
000079: ### Step 3: Configure Environment Variables
000080: Add to your `server/.env` file:
000081: 
000082: ```env
000083: EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp
000084: SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
000085: SMTP_PORT=587
000086: SMTP_SECURE=false
000087: SMTP_USER=your-email@gmail.com
000088: SMTP_PASS=your-16-character-app-password
000089: FROM_EMAIL=your-email@gmail.com
000090: FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000091: ```
000092: 
000093: ### Step 4: Test
000094: Restart your server and test by rejecting/approving an organization.
000095: 
000096: **Note**: Gmail has rate limits (~500 emails/day). For higher volume, use SendGrid.
000097: 
000098: ---
000099: 
000100: ## 📬 Option 3: Outlook SMTP Setup
000101: 
000102: Outlook SMTP is another free option similar to Gmail.
000103: 
000104: ### Step 1: Configure Environment Variables
000105: Add to your `server/.env` file:
000106: 
000107: ```env
000108: EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp
000109: SMTP_HOST=smtp-mail.outlook.com
000110: SMTP_PORT=587
000111: SMTP_SECURE=false
000112: SMTP_USER=your-email@outlook.com
000113: SMTP_PASS=your-outlook-password
000114: FROM_EMAIL=your-email@outlook.com
000115: FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000116: ```
000117: 
000118: ### Step 2: Test
000119: Restart your server and test by rejecting/approving an organization.
000120: 
000121: ---
000122: 
000123: ## 🔧 Configuration Reference
000124: 
000125: ### Environment Variables
000126: 
000127: | Variable | Description | Required | Example |
000128: |----------|-------------|----------|---------|
000129: | `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | Email provider to use | Yes | `sendgrid`, `smtp`, or `console` |
000130: | `FROM_EMAIL` | Sender email address | Yes | `noreply@interviewai.pro` |
000131: | `FROM_NAME` | Sender display name | Yes | `InterviewAI Pro` |
000132: | `SENDGRID_API_KEY` | SendGrid API key | If using SendGrid | `SG.xxxxx` |
000133: | `SMTP_HOST` | SMTP server hostname | If using SMTP | `smtp.gmail.com` |
000134: | `SMTP_PORT` | SMTP server port | If using SMTP | `587` |
000135: | `SMTP_SECURE` | Use TLS/SSL | If using SMTP | `false` (for port 587) |
000136: | `SMTP_USER` | SMTP username | If using SMTP | `your-email@gmail.com` |
000137: | `SMTP_PASS` | SMTP password | If using SMTP | `your-app-password` |
000138: 
000139: ### Provider Comparison
000140: 
000141: | Provider | Free Tier | Setup Difficulty | Best For |
000142: |----------|-----------|------------------|----------|
000143: | **SendGrid** | 100/day forever | ⭐ Easy | Production |
000144: | **Gmail SMTP** | ~500/day | ⭐⭐ Medium | Development/Small scale |
000145: | **Outlook SMTP** | Unlimited* | ⭐⭐ Medium | Development/Small scale |
000146: | **Console** | N/A | ⭐⭐⭐ Very Easy | Development only |
000147: 
000148: *Outlook has rate limits but they're not publicly documented
000149: 
000150: ---
000151: 
000152: ## 🧪 Testing Email Configuration
000153: 
000154: ### Method 1: Test via Organization Rejection
000155: 1. Start your server
000156: 2. Log in as system admin
000157: 3. Go to Pending Approvals
000158: 4. Reject an organization with a reason
000159: 5. Check server logs for email sending confirmation
000160: 6. Check the organization owner's email inbox
000161: 
000162: ### Method 2: Check Server Logs
000163: When emails are sent, you'll see logs like:
000164: ```
000165: INFO: Sending email to user@example.com: Organization Application Update
000166: INFO: Email sent via SendGrid to user@example.com: 202
000167: ```
000168: 
000169: ### Method 3: Console Mode (Development)
000170: If `EMAIL_PROVIDER=console`, emails will be logged to the console instead of being sent. This is useful for development.
000171: 
000172: ---
000173: 
000174: ## ❓ Troubleshooting
000175: 
000176: ### SendGrid Issues
000177: 
000178: **Error: "SENDGRID_API_KEY is not configured"**
000179: - Make sure you've added `SENDGRID_API_KEY` to your `.env` file
000180: - Restart your server after adding the key
000181: 
000182: **Error: "The from address does not match a verified Sender Identity"**
000183: - Verify your sender email in SendGrid dashboard
000184: - Go to Settings → Sender Authentication → Verify a Single Sender
000185: 
000186: **Emails not being delivered**
000187: - Check SendGrid Activity Feed in dashboard
000188: - Verify your API key has "Mail Send" permissions
000189: - Check spam folder
000190: 
000191: ### SMTP Issues
000192: 
000193: **Error: "Invalid login"**
000194: - For Gmail: Make sure you're using an App Password, not your regular password
000195: - For Outlook: Make sure your password is correct
000196: - Check that 2FA is enabled (for Gmail)
000197: 
000198: **Error: "Connection timeout"**
000199: - Check your firewall/network settings
000200: - Verify SMTP_HOST and SMTP_PORT are correct
000201: - Try SMTP_PORT=465 with SMTP_SECURE=true
000202: 
000203: **Error: "Rate limit exceeded"**
000204: - Gmail limits to ~500 emails/day
000205: - Switch to SendGrid for higher volume
000206: - Wait 24 hours for rate limit to reset
000207: 
000208: ### General Issues
000209: 
000210: **Emails not sending at all**
000211: - Check `EMAIL_PROVIDER` is set correctly
000212: - Verify all required environment variables are set
000213: - Check server logs for error messages
000214: - Make sure you've restarted the server after changing `.env`
000215: 
000216: **Emails going to spam**
000217: - Verify your sender email domain (SendGrid)
000218: - Use a professional FROM_EMAIL address
000219: - Include proper email templates (already implemented)
000220: 
000221: ---
000222: 
000223: ## 📚 Additional Resources
000224: 
000225: - [SendGrid Documentation](https://docs.sendgrid.com/)
000226: - [Gmail App Passwords](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833)
000227: - [Nodemailer Documentation](https://nodemailer.com/about/)
000228: - [SMTP Server List](https://www.arclab.com/en/kb/email/list-of-smtp-and-pop3-servers-mailserver-list.html)
000229: 
000230: ---
000231: 
000232: ## 🎯 Quick Start (SendGrid - Recommended)
000233: 
000234: 1. Sign up at [sendgrid.com](https://sendgrid.com)
000235: 2. Create API key in Settings → API Keys
000236: 3. Add to `server/.env`:
000237:    ```env
000238:    EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid
000239:    SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.your-key-here
000240:    FROM_EMAIL=your-email@example.com

000242:    ```
000243: 4. Run `npm install` in the `server` directory
000244: 5. Restart your server
000245: 6. Done! 🎉
000246: 
000247: ---
000248: 
000249: ## 💡 Tips
000250: 
000251: - **For Development**: Use `EMAIL_PROVIDER=console` to see emails in logs without sending
000252: - **For Production**: Use SendGrid for reliability and better deliverability
000253: - **For Testing**: Use Gmail SMTP with a test account
000254: - **Rate Limits**: Be aware of daily limits, especially with Gmail
000255: - **Security**: Never commit `.env` files with real API keys to git
000256: 
000257: ---
000258: 
000259: ## ✅ Verification Checklist

000001: # Email Troubleshooting Guide
000002: 
000003: ## Issue: Emails Not Sending When Rejecting Organizations
000004: 
000005: ### ✅ Fixes Applied
000006: 
000007: 1. **Updated `.env` file** with SendGrid configuration:
000008:    - `EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid`
000009:    - `SENDGRID_API_KEY` (configured)
000010:    - `FROM_EMAIL` and `FROM_NAME` (configured)
000011: 
000012: 2. **Enhanced Error Handling**:
000013:    - Added validation for owner email existence
000014:    - Added detailed logging for email sending process
000015:    - Improved error messages for debugging
000016: 
000017: 3. **Improved SendGrid Integration**:
000018:    - Better error handling and logging
000019:    - More detailed error messages from SendGrid API
000020: 
000021: ### 🔍 Common Issues & Solutions
000022: 
000023: #### Issue 1: "The from address does not match a verified Sender Identity"
000024: 
000025: **Problem**: SendGrid requires you to verify your sender email address.
000026: 
000027: **Solution**:
000028: 1. Log in to [SendGrid Dashboard](https://app.sendgrid.com)
000029: 2. Go to **Settings** → **Sender Authentication**
000030: 3. Click **"Verify a Single Sender"**
000031: 4. Fill in your email details:
000032:    - Email: `noreply@interviewai.pro` (or your FROM_EMAIL)
000033:    - From Name: `InterviewAI Pro`
000034:    - Company: Your company name
000035:    - Address: Your address
000036:    - City, State, Zip: Your location
000037:    - Country: Your country
000038: 5. Click **"Create"**
000039: 6. Check your email inbox and click the verification link
000040: 7. Once verified, restart your server
000041: 
000042: #### Issue 2: "Authentication failed" or "403 Forbidden"
000043: 
000044: **Problem**: API key is invalid or doesn't have the right permissions.
000045: 
000046: **Solution**:
000047: 1. Go to SendGrid Dashboard → **Settings** → **API Keys**
000048: 2. Check if your API key exists and is active
000049: 3. If needed, create a new API key with **"Full Access"** or **"Restricted Access"** with **"Mail Send"** permission
000050: 4. Update `SENDGRID_API_KEY` in your `.env` file
000051: 5. Restart your server
000052: 
000053: #### Issue 3: "Owner email not found"
000054: 
000055: **Problem**: The organization owner doesn't have an email address in the database.
000056: 
000057: **Solution**:
000058: - Check the server logs for: `Owner {ownerId} does not have an email address`
000059: - This means the user record in Firestore doesn't have an `email` field
000060: - This is a data issue - the user needs to have an email in their profile
000061: 
000062: #### Issue 4: Emails going to spam
000063: 
000064: **Problem**: SendGrid emails might go to spam if sender isn't verified.
000065: 
000066: **Solution**:
000067: - Verify your sender email (see Issue 1)
000068: - Consider setting up Domain Authentication in SendGrid for better deliverability
000069: - Use a professional email address (not a free email like Gmail)
000070: 
000071: ### 📋 Verification Checklist
000072: 
000073: Before testing, ensure:
000074: 
000075: - [ ] `.env` file has `EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid`
000076: - [ ] `.env` file has `SENDGRID_API_KEY` set correctly
000077: - [ ] `.env` file has `FROM_EMAIL` set (and it's verified in SendGrid)
000078: - [ ] `.env` file has `FROM_NAME` set
000079: - [ ] Server has been restarted after updating `.env`
000080: - [ ] SendGrid sender email is verified
000081: - [ ] SendGrid API key has "Mail Send" permissions
000082: 
000083: ### 🧪 Testing Steps
000084: 
000085: 1. **Check Server Logs on Startup**:
000086:    Look for:
000087:    ```
000088:    ✅ SendGrid API key initialized successfully
000089:    ```
000090: 
000091: 2. **Test Organization Rejection**:
000092:    - Log in as system admin
000093:    - Go to Pending Approvals
000094:    - Reject an organization with a reason
000095:    - Check server logs for:
000096:      ```
000097:      📧 Sending email to user@example.com: Organization Application Update
000098:      ✅ Email sent via SendGrid to user@example.com - Status: 202
000099:      ✅ Rejection email sent successfully to user@example.com
000100:      ```
000101: 
000102: 3. **Check SendGrid Activity**:
000103:    - Go to SendGrid Dashboard → **Activity**
000104:    - You should see the email in the activity feed
000105:    - Check if it was delivered, bounced, or blocked
000106: 
000107: 4. **Check Recipient's Email**:
000108:    - Check inbox (and spam folder)
000109:    - Email should arrive within a few seconds
000110: 
000111: ### 🔍 Debugging
000112: 
000113: If emails still aren't sending, check:
000114: 
000115: 1. **Server Logs**:
000116:    ```bash
000117:    # Look for these log messages:
000118:    - "📧 Sending email to..."
000119:    - "✅ Email sent via SendGrid..."
000120:    - "❌ SendGrid error:"
000121:    - "⚠️  EMAIL_PROVIDER is set to sendgrid but SENDGRID_API_KEY is not configured"
000122:    ```
000123: 
000124: 2. **SendGrid Dashboard**:
000125:    - Check **Activity** feed for email attempts
000126:    - Check **Suppressions** for blocked emails
000127:    - Check **Settings** → **API Keys** for key status
000128: 
000129: 3. **Environment Variables**:
000130:    ```bash
000131:    # In your server directory, check if variables are loaded:
000132:    node -e "require('dotenv').config(); console.log(process.env.EMAIL_PROVIDER, process.env.SENDGRID_API_KEY ? 'API Key Set' : 'API Key Missing')"
000133:    ```
000134: 
000135: ### 📞 Still Having Issues?
000136: 
000137: 1. **Check SendGrid Status**: [status.sendgrid.com](https://status.sendgrid.com)
000138: 2. **Review SendGrid Documentation**: [docs.sendgrid.com](https://docs.sendgrid.com)
000139: 3. **Check Server Logs**: Look for detailed error messages
000140: 4. **Verify API Key**: Create a new API key if needed
000141: 5. **Test with Console Mode**: Set `EMAIL_PROVIDER=console` to see email content in logs
000142: 
000143: ### 🎯 Quick Fix Commands
000144: 
000145: ```bash
000146: # Restart server after .env changes
000147: cd server
000148: npm run dev
000149: 
000150: # Check if SendGrid is initialized (look for ✅ in logs)
000151: # Should see: "✅ SendGrid API key initialized successfully"
000152: 
000153: # Test rejection and watch logs
000154: # Should see: "📧 Sending email to..." and "✅ Email sent via SendGrid..."
000155: ```
000156: 
000157: ---
000158: 
000159: **Note**: After making any changes to `.env`, you **must restart your server** for the changes to take effect.
000160:

000116: ### 2. Organization Approval Workflow
000117: 
000118: **Registration Flow Changes:**
000119: 
000120: **BEFORE:**
000121: ```
000122: Company registers → Organization created → Immediately active → Full access
000123: ```
000124: 
000125: **AFTER:**
000126: ```
000127: Company registers → Organization created with status='PENDING' 
000128: → Limited access (can view but not create jobs/invitations)
000129: → System Admin reviews → Approves/Rejects
000130: → If approved: status='APPROVED', full access granted
000131: → If rejected: Notification sent, can appeal or re-register
000132: ```
000133: 
000134: **Implementation Steps:**
000135: 
000136: 1. **Update company registration:**
000137:    - Set initial `organization.status = 'PENDING'`
000138:    - Create notification for system admins
000139:    - Show "pending approval" banner on company dashboard
000140: 
000141: 2. **Add organization status checks:**
000142:    - Middleware: `requireApprovedOrganization`
000143:    - Block job creation, invitations until approved
000144:    - Allow viewing own organization settings
000145: 
000146: 3. **System Admin approval UI:**
000147:    - List pending organizations with details
000148:    - View company verification documents
000149:    - One-click approve/reject with reason
000150:    - Email notification on decision
000151: 
000152: 4. **Organization status management:**
000153:    - Approve: Update status, log action, send email
000154:    - Reject: Update status, store reason, send email with appeal process
000155:    - Suspend: For policy violations, blocks all actions
000156:    - Reactivate: Restore access after suspension

000241: ### 4. Interview Session Linking
000242: 
000243: **Problem:** Invited candidates can accept invitations but don't automatically get an interview session.
000244: 
000245: **Solution:**
000246: 
000247: **Invitation Acceptance Flow:**
000248: ```
000249: 1. Candidate clicks invitation link
000250: 2. Authenticates/creates account
000251: 3. Accepts invitation → Creates HIRING interview automatically
000252: 4. Redirects to interview lobby/prep page
000253: 5. Can start interview when ready
000254: ```
000255: 
000256: **Implementation:**
000257: 
000258: 1. **Update invitation acceptance endpoint:**
000259: ```javascript
000260: // server/src/controllers/invitation.controller.js
000261: static async acceptInvitation(req, res, next) {
000262:   // ... existing validation
000263:   
000264:   const accepted = await invitationStore.markAccepted(token, req.user.id);
000265:   
000266:   // NEW: Auto-create interview for this invitation
000267:   const job = await jobStore.getById(accepted.jobId);
000268:   const interview = await interviewStore.create({
000269:     mode: 'HIRING',
000270:     candidateId: req.user.id,
000271:     companyId: job.createdBy,
000272:     organizationId: accepted.organizationId,
000273:     jobId: accepted.jobId,
000274:     jobStage: accepted.stage,
000275:     invitationId: accepted.id,
000276:     jobRole: job.title,
000277:     experienceLevel: job.experienceLevel,
000278:     industry: job.industry || null,
000279:     interviewTypes: job.templateConfig?.interviewTypes || ['BEHAVIORAL'],
000280:     duration: job.templateConfig?.duration || 30,
000281:     config: job.templateConfig || {},
000282:     status: 'SCHEDULED',
000283:   });
000284:   
000285:   res.json({ 
000286:     success: true, 
000287:     invitation: sanitizeInvitation(accepted),
000288:     interview: { id: interview.id, status: interview.status },
000289:   });
000290: }
000291: ```
000292: 
000293: 2. **Update frontend invite page:**
000294: ```javascript
000295: // After successful acceptance
000296: if (result.success && result.interview) {
000297:   navigate(`/interview-lobby?interviewId=${result.interview.id}`);
000298: }
000299: ```
000300: 
000301: 3. **Create interview lobby page:**
000302: ```
000303: /interview-lobby?interviewId=xxx
000304: ```
000305: - Shows interview details
000306: - Company info
000307: - Expected duration
000308: - Instructions
000309: - "Start Interview" button → `/live-interview-session?interviewId=xxx`

000001: # Firebase Storage Decision Matrix (Complete System)
000002: 
000003: Date: 2026-02-11
000004: 
000005: This document defines where each part of the system should be stored:
000006: - Firestore (durable business data / query-heavy records)
000007: - Realtime Database (low-latency signaling, presence, feed invalidation, chat)
000008: - Firestore + Realtime projection (Firestore is source of truth, Realtime mirrors minimal event state)
000009: 
000010: ## Storage Rules
000011: 
000012: 1. Firestore should be the source of truth for durable business records, history, analytics, and admin/reporting data.
000013: 2. Realtime Database should be used for instant UI synchronization, short-lived session state, presence, and push-style feed updates.
000014: 3. If both are used, Firestore is canonical and Realtime contains only projection/feed payloads needed for low-latency updates.
000015: 4. Do not store large, long-term historical datasets in Realtime DB.
000016: 
000017: ## A) Firestore Collections: What They Should Be
000018: 
000019: | Data Area | Firestore Location | Should Be Realtime in RTDB? | Correct Storage Decision |
000020: |---|---|---|---|
000021: | User profiles/accounts | `users` | No | Firestore only |
000022: | Interview records | `interviews` | Yes, as projection only | Firestore + RTDB session/feed projection |
000023: | Interview questions | `interviews/{interviewId}/questions` | Event-only | Firestore + RTDB event notifications |
000024: | Pose analytics snapshots | `interviews/{interviewId}/poseData` | Optional event signal only | Firestore only for data, RTDB only for lightweight event signal |
000025: | WebRTC session metadata | `webrtcSessions` | Not required currently | Firestore only |
000026: | Organizations | `organizations` | Yes, for status/feed mirrors | Firestore + RTDB status/feed projection |
000027: | Organization memberships | `organizationMembers` | Yes, for access/feed mirrors | Firestore + RTDB membership mirror (`userOrganizationMap`) |
000028: | Team invitations | `teamInvitations` | Yes, for instant org dashboard updates | Firestore + RTDB org feed projection |
000029: | Jobs | `jobs` | Yes | Firestore + RTDB org/public feed projection |
000030: | Candidate invitations | `invitations` | Yes | Firestore + RTDB org/candidate/interview projection |
000031: | Interview reviews | `interviewReviews` | Yes | Firestore + RTDB org/interview event projection |
000032: | Organization activity logs | `activityLogs` | No hard requirement | Firestore only |
000033: | Job applications | `jobApplications` | Yes | Firestore + RTDB org/candidate feed projection |
000034: | Platform audit logs | `platformAuditLogs` | Optional signal only | Firestore only (admin feed can trigger refresh) |
000035: | System settings | `systemSettings` | Yes (public toggles and admin refresh) | Firestore + RTDB public/admin projection |
000036: | Analytics snapshots | `analyticsSnapshots` | No | Firestore only |
000037: | Email verification state | `emailVerifications` | No | Firestore only |
000038: | Interview training datasets | `trainingDatasets_interviews` | No | Firestore only |
000039: | Analytics training datasets | `trainingDatasets_analytics` | No | Firestore only |
000040: | Dataset metadata | `trainingDatasets_metadata` | Optional signal only | Firestore only (admin feed event on changes) |
000041: | Interview templates | `interviewTemplates` | No current requirement | Firestore only |
000042: | Newsletter subscriptions | `newsletterSubscriptions` | No | Firestore only |
000043: | Subscription state | `subscriptions` | No | Firestore only |
000044: | Billing event history | `billingEvents` | No | Firestore only |
000045: 
000046: ## B) Realtime Database Paths: What They Should Be
000047: 
000048: | Realtime Path | Purpose | Should Be in Firestore Instead? | Correct Storage Decision |
000049: |---|---|---|---|
000050: | `public/systemSettings` | Public low-latency flags (`maintenanceMode`, `nonverbalFeedbackEnabled`) | No (for instant client updates) | Keep in RTDB as projection from Firestore |
000051: | `organizationApprovalStatus/{organizationId}` | Immediate approval/review status visibility | No | Keep in RTDB as projection from Firestore `organizations.status` |
000052: | `sessions/{interviewId}/participants` | Live participant access map | No | RTDB authoritative session state |
000053: | `sessions/{interviewId}/meta` | Live interview status/meta for instant sync | No | RTDB projection of interview live state |
000054: | `sessions/{interviewId}/events/{eventId}` | Live event stream | No | RTDB authoritative for stream delivery |
000055: | `sessions/{interviewId}/lastEvent` | Fast latest-event cursor | No | RTDB authoritative |
000056: | `sessions/{interviewId}/presence/{participantId}` | Presence/connectivity | No | RTDB authoritative |
000057: | `userInterviewFeeds/{uid}/{interviewId}` | Per-user interview feed invalidation/update cursor | No | RTDB projection |
000058: | `userOrganizationMap/{uid}/{organizationId}` | Membership projection for RTDB rules | No | RTDB projection (derived from Firestore memberships) |
000059: | `organizationFeeds/{organizationId}` | Org-level invalidation/feed events | No | RTDB projection |
000060: | `candidateFeeds/{uid}` | Candidate-level invalidation/feed events | No | RTDB projection |
000061: | `publicFeeds/{channel}` | Public feed invalidation (e.g. jobs) | No | RTDB projection |
000062: | `adminFeeds/global` | Admin panel invalidation/feed events | No | RTDB projection |
000063: | `admins/{uid}` | Realtime rules gate for admin-only feeds | No | RTDB access-control projection |
000064: | `liveChats/{chatId}` | Live chat session state | No | RTDB authoritative |
000065: | `liveChats/{chatId}/messages/{messageId}` | Live chat messages | No | RTDB authoritative |
000066: 
000067: ## C) Complete Domain-by-Domain Decision
000068: 
000069: | Domain | Canonical Store | Realtime Mirror Needed? | Realtime Paths |
000070: |---|---|---|---|
000071: | Authentication/profile | Firestore (`users`) | No | None |
000072: | Organization onboarding and approval | Firestore (`organizations`) | Yes | `organizationApprovalStatus/*`, `adminFeeds/global` |
000073: | Organization membership/roles | Firestore (`organizationMembers`) | Yes | `userOrganizationMap/*`, `organizationFeeds/*`, `candidateFeeds/*` |
000074: | Job posting lifecycle | Firestore (`jobs`) | Yes | `organizationFeeds/*`, `publicFeeds/jobs` |
000075: | Application lifecycle | Firestore (`jobApplications`) | Yes | `organizationFeeds/*`, `candidateFeeds/*` |
000076: | Invitation lifecycle | Firestore (`invitations`) | Yes | `organizationFeeds/*`, `candidateFeeds/*`, interview `sessions/*` events |
000077: | Team invitation lifecycle | Firestore (`teamInvitations`) | Yes | `organizationFeeds/*` |
000078: | Interview lifecycle/live status | Firestore (`interviews`, `questions`) | Yes | `sessions/*`, `userInterviewFeeds/*` |
000079: | Review submission and override | Firestore (`interviewReviews`) | Yes | `organizationFeeds/*`, `sessions/*` event (`review-submitted`) |
000080: | System settings | Firestore (`systemSettings`) | Yes | `public/systemSettings`, `adminFeeds/global` |
000081: | Admin organization queues/lists | Firestore (`organizations`) | Yes, as refresh signal | `adminFeeds/global` |
000082: | Datasets and training data | Firestore (`trainingDatasets_*`) | Yes, only for panel refresh signal | `adminFeeds/global` |
000083: | Live support chat | RTDB (`liveChats/*`) | Native realtime | `liveChats/*` |
000084: | Newsletter/billing | Firestore (`newsletterSubscriptions`, `subscriptions`, `billingEvents`) | No | None |
000085: | Historical analytics and audit | Firestore (`analyticsSnapshots`, `platformAuditLogs`, `activityLogs`) | Optional refresh signal only | `adminFeeds/global` or `organizationFeeds/*` triggers |
000086: 
000087: ## D) Verification Against Current Code
000088: 
000089: Status summary after audit:
000090: - Interview/session realtime: implemented.
000091: - Jobs/applications/invitations/team-invitations realtime feed projection: implemented.
000092: - Organization/member updates and membership map projection: implemented.
000093: - Review submission realtime projection: implemented.
000094: - Interview lifecycle projection to organization/admin feeds for analytics/fairness refresh: implemented.
000095: - Admin feed updates for org status, system settings, datasets, registration/re-review triggers: implemented.
000096: - Public settings realtime mirror: implemented.
000097: - Live chat realtime: implemented.
000098: 
000099: ## E) Final System Recommendation
000100: 
000101: 1. Keep Firestore as canonical business datastore.
000102: 2. Keep Realtime Database as low-latency projection/signaling layer.
000103: 3. Continue dual-write only where instant multi-user UI updates are required.
000104: 4. Avoid moving business-history entities (datasets, billing, templates, analytics snapshots, newsletter, audit logs) into RTDB.
000105: 5. Treat RTDB feed records as invalidation/event cursors, not primary records.
000106: 
```

000001: # Gap Verification Report
000002: 
000003: This document verifies that each of the five gaps identified from the contextual report has been fully addressed in the codebase. Verification was performed by tracing implementation end-to-end (frontend, API, backend, persistence).
000004: 
000005: ---
000006: 
000007: ## 1. Explicit consent for recording (audio/video)
000008: 
000009: **Original gap:** No clear “I consent to this session being recorded” step before starting the interview. Privacy/Terms exist but not session-specific consent.
000010: 
000011: **Status: ✅ Complete**
000012: 
000013: ### Verification
000014: 
000015: | Requirement | Implementation | Location |
000016: |------------|---------------|----------|
000017: | Explicit “I consent to this session being recorded” step | Full-screen consent modal with required checkbox and text: **“I consent to this session being recorded (audio and video)”** | `src/pages/live-interview-session/components/RecordingConsentScreen.jsx` (lines 101–104) |
000018: | Session-specific consent | Consent keyed by `interviewId` in sessionStorage (`recording_consent_${id}`) and persisted to the interview document in Firestore | `live-interview-session/index.jsx` (handleRecordingConsentGiven), `interview.controller.js` (recordRecordingConsent) |
000019: | Consent required before interview UI / recording | Main interview UI is only rendered when `recordingConsentGiven` is true; consent screen blocks everything until user agrees | `live-interview-session/index.jsx` (lines 415–423: `{!recordingConsentGiven && <RecordingConsentScreen />}`, `{recordingConsentGiven && ( ... main UI )}`) |
000020: | Persistence | Backend PATCH `/api/interviews/:id/recording-consent` stores `recordingConsentGivenAt` and `recordingConsentVersion` on the interview document; `interviewStore.update()` merges these fields | `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js`, `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js` (update uses merge: true) |
000021: | Privacy Policy link | Consent screen links to `/privacy` for Privacy Policy | `RecordingConsentScreen.jsx` (lines 82–89, 120–127) |
000022: 
000023: **Edge case:** For practice sessions (e.g. `interview_${Date.now()}`), there is no backend interview ID; consent is still required and stored in sessionStorage only. Backend consent is only called when `interviewId` looks like a real Firestore ID. This is intentional.
000024: 
000025: ---
000026: 
000027: ## 2. SME calibration workflow
000028: 
000029: **Original gap:** Human review exists (submit scores). Report expects comparison of AI vs SME ratings and calibration (e.g. side-by-side, agreement, inter-rater reliability). That comparison/calibration flow was not clearly implemented.
000030: 
000031: **Status: ✅ Complete**
000032: 
000033: ### Verification
000034: 
000035: | Requirement | Implementation | Location |
000036: |------------|----------------|----------|
000037: | Side-by-side AI vs SME comparison | Dedicated **“AI vs SME”** tab with two panels: “AI Evaluation” (overall + technical, communication) and “SME (Your) Review” (overall 0–10→100, technical, communication, problem solving, cultural fit) | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (lines 364–455, tab “calibration”) |
000038: | Agreement metric (per interview) | Agreement line: “Agreement: AI overall X vs SME overall Y (diff: Z pts)” when both scores exist | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (lines 432–445) |
000039: | Calibration data stored for aggregation | Each review stores `aiOverallScoreAtReview` (snapshot of interview.overallScore at submit time) and `smeOverallScore` (derived from rating or category average) | `review.controller.js` (submitReview), `firebaseData.service.js` (reviewStore.submit) |
000040: | Platform-level calibration metrics | Admin **Fairness & Calibration** panel shows: reviews with both scores, mean \|AI − SME\|, agreement within 10 pts (%), override count | `FairnessCalibrationPanel.jsx`, `admin.controller.js` (getFairnessCalibration) |
000041: | GET “my review” for pre-fill | GET `/api/reviews/:interviewId/me` returns current user’s review so calibration tab and My Review can show existing scores | `review.routes.js` (/:interviewId/me first), `review.controller.js` (getMyReview) |
000042: 
000043: The report’s “inter-rater reliability” is addressed at platform level via the admin calibration metrics (mean absolute difference, agreement %), not only per-interview.
000044: 
000045: ---
000046: 
000047: ## 3. Override of AI scores by SME
000048: 
000049: **Original gap:** Reviewers can submit their own scores; it was not explicit that this is stored and shown as an “override” of the AI evaluation (e.g. “final score = SME override when present”).
000050: 
000051: **Status: ✅ Complete**
000052: 
000053: ### Verification
000054: 
000055: | Requirement | Implementation | Location |
000056: |------------|----------------|----------|
000057: | Stored as override | Review stores `overrideOverall` (boolean). When true and `smeOverallScore` present, interview is updated with `finalOverallScore` and `finalScoreSource: 'SME'`. | `review.controller.js` (lines 132–137), `firebaseData.service.js` (reviewStore.submit with aiOverallScoreAtReview, smeOverallScore, overrideOverall) |
000058: | Final score = SME when override present | Interview document has `finalOverallScore` and `finalScoreSource`. UI displays **Final Score** as `finalOverallScore ?? overallScore` and shows “SME override” when `finalScoreSource === 'SME'`. | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (info bar lines 191–202) |
000059: | Explicit override control | “My Review” tab has checkbox: **“Use my overall score as the final score (override AI).”** Label explains that the interview’s final score will be the SME’s overall (0–10 scaled to 0–100) when checked. | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (lines 732–742) |
000060: | API accepts override | POST `/api/reviews/:interviewId` body includes `overrideOverall` (optional boolean); validation and controller pass it through. | `review.routes.js` (body('overrideOverall').optional().isBoolean()), `review.controller.js` (submitReview) |
000061: 
000062: **Note:** If an SME who had overridden later submits again with the override checkbox unchecked, the interview is not automatically reverted to the AI score (the last final score remains). This avoids overwriting another reviewer’s override. If your policy is single-reviewer or last-submission-wins, you could add logic to set `finalOverallScore = overallScore` and `finalScoreSource = 'AI'` when `overrideOverall === false`.
000063: 
000064: ---
000065: 
000066: ## 4. Fairness metrics and calibration in admin (FR10)
000067: 
000068: **Original gap:** Report (FR10) asks for admin analytics that include fairness metrics and calibration. System admin dashboard exists; dedicated fairness/calibration views or metrics were not clearly present.
000069: 
000070: **Status: ✅ Complete**
000071: 
000072: ### Verification
000073: 
000074: | Requirement | Implementation | Location |
000075: |------------|----------------|----------|
000076: | Dedicated admin view | System Admin Dashboard has a **“Fairness & Calibration”** tab (icon: Scale) that renders `FairnessCalibrationPanel`. | `system-admin-dashboard/index.jsx` (tabs array, activeTab === 'fairness') |
000077: | Fairness metrics | Panel shows: completed interviews, with AI score, SME override count, sample size; **AI overall score distribution** (0–20, 21–40, 41–60, 61–80, 81–100); **Final score distribution** (after SME override when applicable) with bar charts. | `FairnessCalibrationPanel.jsx` (fairness section, scoreDistribution, finalScoreDistribution) |
000078: | Calibration metrics | Panel shows: reviews with both scores, mean \|AI − SME\| (pts), agreement within 10 pts (%), override count. | `FairnessCalibrationPanel.jsx` (calibration section), `admin.controller.js` (getFairnessCalibration) |
000079: | Backend aggregation | GET `/api/admin/fairness-calibration?limit=500` uses `interviewStore.listRecent(limit)` and `reviewStore.listRecent(limit)`, computes buckets and calibration stats, returns `fairness`, `calibration`, `sampleSize`. | `admin.routes.js`, `admin.controller.js` (getFairnessCalibration), `firebaseData.service.js` (listRecent for interviews and reviews) |
000080: | FR10 alignment | Comment in code and panel title reference FR10. | `admin.controller.js`, `FairnessCalibrationPanel.jsx` |

000083: 
000084: ## 5. Explainable output tied to rubrics for recruiters/SMEs
000085: 
000086: **Original gap:** Scoring is structured and criterion-based (STAR + criteria). Report also wants explanations explicitly tied to rubric criteria for recruiters/SMEs; how much of that is surfaced in the recruiter UI (not just raw JSON) needed checking.
000087: 
000088: **Status: ✅ Complete**
000089: 
000090: ### Verification
000091: 
000092: | Requirement | Implementation | Location |
000093: |------------|----------------|----------|
000094: | Rubric-tied criteria in UI | **AI Evaluation** tab uses `EVALUATION_RUBRIC_CRITERIA` (Technical Skills, Communication Skills, Problem Solving, Cultural Fit). For each criterion present in `interview.evaluation` with `score` or `feedback`, a card is shown with label, score (X/100), and feedback text. | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (EVALUATION_RUBRIC_CRITERIA, lines 552–582) |
000095: | Structured sections (not only raw JSON) | Strengths (green list), Areas for Improvement / weaknesses (amber list), Recommendations (blue list), Detailed feedback (text block). Each section is only rendered when the corresponding data exists. | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (lines 584–632) |
000096: | Raw JSON available but secondary | Collapsible **“Raw evaluation (JSON)”** `<details>` section at the bottom for transparency and debugging. | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (lines 634–641) |
000097: | Legacy / string evaluation | If `interview.evaluation` is a string or non-object, the previous behavior is preserved (single pre block with string or stringified JSON). | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (lines 658–665) |
000098: | Recruiter/SME-facing | All of the above live in `InterviewReviewEnhanced`, which is the company dashboard interview review modal used by recruiters and SMEs. | `InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx` (used from company dashboard) |
000099: 
000100: The LLM evaluation shape in `server/src/services/llm.service.js` (generateInterviewSummary) returns `technicalSkills`, `communicationSkills` with `score` and `feedback`, plus `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `recommendations`, `detailedFeedback`. The frontend rubric criteria and sections align with this structure; if the backend adds e.g. `problemSolving` or `culturalFit`, they are already in the rubric and will render automatically.
000101:

One optional improvement: if only one SME reviews per interview and they should be able to “revert” an override, consider updating the interview to `finalOverallScore = overallScore` and `finalScoreSource = 'AI'` when a review is submitted with `overrideOverall: false` (with care for multi-reviewer scenarios).

000001: # Interview Evaluation Export Schema (FR12 / Interoperability)
000002: 
000003: This document describes the **structured output** used when exporting interview evaluations and reviews for recruiters (e.g. from the Interview Review modal → “Export report”). The format is designed to support **interoperability** with external ATS/HR systems and analysis tools (Contextual Report 2.7.3 point 9, FR12).
000004: 
000005: ## Schema version
000006: 
000007: - **Current:** `1.0`
000008: - **Export trigger:** Recruiter/SME clicks “Export report” in `InterviewReviewEnhanced` (company dashboard).
000009: 
000010: ## Top-level fields
000011: 
000012: | Field | Type | Description |
000013: |-------|------|-------------|
000014: | `schemaVersion` | string | Schema version (e.g. `"1.0"`) |
000015: | `exportDate` | string (ISO 8601) | When the export was generated |
000016: | `interviewId` | string | Interview document ID |
000017: | `candidate` | object | Candidate summary (id, fullName, email) |
000018: | `jobRole` | string | Role for the interview |
000019: | `startedAt` | string \| null | Interview start (ISO 8601) |
000020: | `endedAt` | string \| null | Interview end (ISO 8601) |
000021: | `status` | string | e.g. COMPLETED |
000022: | `overallScore` | number \| null | AI overall score (0–100) |
000023: | `finalOverallScore` | number \| null | Final score (AI or SME override) |
000024: | `finalScoreSource` | string | `"AI"` or `"SME"` |
000025: | `readinessLevel` | string \| null | e.g. Intermediate |
000026: | `evaluation` | object \| null | Overall AI evaluation (rubric criteria, strengths, weaknesses, recommendations, detailedFeedback) |
000027: | `perQuestionEvaluation` | array | Per-answer evaluations (questionId, question, answer, score, starAnalysis, strengths, weaknesses) |
000028: | `reviewSummary` | object | SME review summary (rating, category scores, recommendation, overrideOverall, notesExcerpt) |
000029: 
000030: ## Evaluation object (overall)
000031: 
000032: When present, `evaluation` contains:
000033: 
000034: - `technicalSkills`, `communicationSkills`, `problemSolving`, `culturalFit`: each `{ score?, feedback? }`
000035: - `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `recommendations`: arrays of strings
000036: - `detailedFeedback`: string
000037: 
000038: ## Per-question evaluation
000039: 
000040: Each item in `perQuestionEvaluation`:
000041: 
000042: - `questionId`, `question`, `answer`
000043: - `score`: 0–10
000044: - `starAnalysis`: `{ situation?, task?, action?, result? }` each `{ present?, quality?, feedback? }`
000045: - `strengths`, `weaknesses`: arrays
000046: 
000047: ## Review summary
000048: 
000049: - `rating`: 0–10 (SME overall)
000050: - `technicalScore`, `communicationScore`, `problemSolvingScore`, `culturalFitScore`: 0–10
000051: - `recommendation`: e.g. STRONG_YES, YES, MAYBE, NO, UNDECIDED
000052: - `overrideOverall`: boolean
000053: - `notesExcerpt`: first 200 characters of notes (or null)
000054: 
000055: ## File format
000056: 
000057: - **Export format:** JSON (UTF-8)
000058: - **Filename pattern:** `interview-evaluation-{interviewId}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.json`
000059: - **Usage:** Download from browser; can be consumed by external tools or re-imported for analysis.
000060: 
000061: ## Alignment with report
000062: 
000063: - **FR12:** Exports and reporting — organized output for analysis.
000064: - **2.7.3 point 9:** Structured outputs that assist with interoperability.
000065: 
000066: ---
000067: 
000068: *Defined: January 2026.*
000069: 
```
