000001: # Interview Style Removal - Summary
000002: 
000003: ## What Was Removed
000004: 
000005: The **Interview Style** setting has been completely removed from the practice interview setup process.
000006: 
000007: ## Why It Was Removed
000008: 
000009: 1. **Redundancy**: Interview Style was doing the same thing as Personality - controlling AI communication style
000010: 2. **Conflicts**: Having both settings could create contradictory instructions to the AI
000011: 3. **Complexity**: Two settings for the same purpose confused users
000012: 4. **Superior Alternative**: Personality provides 12 detailed options vs. 4 basic styles
000013: 
000014: ## What Replaced It
000015: 
000016: **Personality** is now the single setting that controls AI communication style. All interview style variations are covered by personality options:
000017: 
000018: | Old Interview Style | Personality Equivalent |
000019: |-------------------|----------------------|
000020: | Formal & Professional | `professional-encouraging` |
000021: | Conversational & Relaxed | `conversational-authentic` |
000022: | Challenging & Rigorous | `experienced-challenging` |
000023: | Supportive & Encouraging | `growth-oriented-developmental` or `warm-insightful` |
000024: 
000025: ## Changes Made
000026: 
000027: ### 1. UI Changes
000028: - ✅ Removed Interview Style selector from Advanced Settings
000029: - ✅ Removed interviewStyles array from AdvancedSettings component
000030: 
000031: ### 2. Code Changes
000032: - ✅ Removed `interviewStyle` from formData.advancedSettings
000033: - ✅ Removed `interviewStyle` from default state values
000034: - ✅ Removed all `interviewStyle` references from AI prompts
000035: - ✅ Removed `getInterviewStyleDescription()` function from personalityMapper.js
000036: 
000037: ### 3. Files Modified
000038: - `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/components/AdvancedSettings.jsx` - Removed Interview Style selector
000039: - `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx` - Removed from formData defaults
000040: - `src/services/aiInterviewer.js` - Removed from all prompt generation methods
000041: - `src/utils/personalityMapper.js` - Removed interview style mapping function
000042: 
000043: ## User Impact
000044: 
000045: **For New Users:**
000046: - Simpler setup process (one less setting to configure)
000047: - Clearer choice (Personality covers everything)
000048: 
000049: **For Existing Users:**
000050: - If they had saved configs with `interviewStyle`, it will be ignored (no breaking behavior)
000051: - They should use Personality selection instead
000052: 
000053: ## Migration Notes
000054: 
000055: - No migration needed - `interviewStyle` will simply be ignored if present in old configs
000056: - Personality selection is mandatory in Step 3, so all interviews will have a personality
000057: 
000058: ## Benefits
000059: 
000060: 1. ✅ Eliminated redundancy
000061: 2. ✅ Removed potential conflicts
000062: 3. ✅ Simplified user experience
000063: 4. ✅ More comprehensive options (12 personalities vs. 4 styles)
000064: 
000065: 
```

000001: # Jobs Feature Implementation Summary
000002: 
000003: ## Issue
000004: The Company Dashboard was missing the Jobs section in the sidebar navigation. Companies had no way to create and manage job postings.
000005: 
000006: ## Root Cause
000007: The `companyNavItems` in `src/components/ui/UserContextNavigation.jsx` only had 3 items:
000008: - Dashboard
000009: - Interview Setup
000010: - Live Session
000011: 
000012: The Jobs navigation item was missing, and there was no dedicated Jobs management page for companies.
000013: 
000014: ## Solution Implemented
000015: 
000016: ### 1. Created Company Jobs Page
000017: **File**: `src/pages/company-jobs/index.jsx`
000018: 
000019: A comprehensive job management interface with:
000020: - **Job Listing**: Display all jobs with status badges (Draft, Published, Archived)
000021: - **Search & Filter**: Search by job title and filter by status
000022: - **Create Job**: Modal form to create new job postings with fields:
000023:   - Title, Department, Location
000024:   - Employment Type (Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Internship)
000025:   - Experience Level (Entry, Mid, Senior, Lead)
000026:   - Description, Requirements, Benefits
000027:   - Salary Range
000028:   - Status (Draft, Published, Archived)
000029: - **Edit Job**: Update existing job postings
000030: - **Publish Job**: Change status from Draft to Published
000031: - **Archive Job**: Archive published jobs
000032: - **Delete Job**: Remove job postings (with confirmation)
000033: - **Application Count**: Shows number of applications per job
000034: - **Responsive Design**: Works on mobile, tablet, and desktop
000035: 
000036: ### 2. Added Jobs to Company Navigation
000037: **File**: `src/components/ui/UserContextNavigation.jsx`
000038: 
000039: Added Jobs navigation item to `companyNavItems`:
000040: ```javascript
000041: { 
000042:   label: 'Jobs', 
000043:   path: '/company-jobs', 
000044:   icon: 'Briefcase',
000045:   description: 'Manage job postings'
000046: }
000047: ```
000048: 
000049: ### 3. Created Protected Route
000050: **File**: `src/Routes.jsx`
000051: 
000052: Added new route for company jobs:
000053: ```javascript
000054: <Route
000055:   path="/company-jobs"
000056:   element={(
000057:     <ProtectedRoute roles={['COMPANY']}>
000058:       <CompanyJobsPage />
000059:     </ProtectedRoute>
000060:   )}
000061: />
000062: ```
000063: 
000064: ## Features
000065: 
000066: ### Job Creation
000067: - Full form with all necessary fields
000068: - Validation for required fields
000069: - Draft/Published/Archived status
000070: - Template configuration support
000071: 
000072: ### Job Management
000073: - List all organization jobs
000074: - Filter by status
000075: - Search by title
000076: - Edit existing jobs
000077: - Publish/Archive/Delete actions
000078: - Application count tracking
000079: 
000080: ### UI/UX
000081: - Modern card-based layout
000082: - Gradient buttons matching site theme
000083: - Status badges with color coding
000084: - Responsive grid layout
000085: - Loading states
000086: - Error handling
000087: - Empty state with call-to-action
000088: 
000089: ### Integration
000090: - Uses `apiClient.jobs` for all API calls
000091: - Supports organization context
000092: - Role-based access (COMPANY only)
000093: - Syncs with existing job endpoints
000094: 
000095: ## API Endpoints Used
000096: 
000097: - `GET /api/jobs/organization` - List organization jobs
000098: - `POST /api/jobs` - Create new job
000099: - `PUT /api/jobs/:id` - Update job
000100: - `DELETE /api/jobs/:id` - Delete job
000101: 
000102: ## Testing
000103: 
000104: ### To Test Job Creation:
000105: 1. Log in as a company user (recruiter/admin)
000106: 2. Click "Jobs" in the sidebar
000107: 3. Click "Create Job" button
000108: 4. Fill in the form:
000109:    - Title: "Senior Frontend Developer"
000110:    - Department: "Engineering"
000111:    - Location: "San Francisco, CA"
000112:    - Employment Type: "Full-time"
000113:    - Experience Level: "Senior"
000114:    - Description: "We're looking for an experienced React developer..."
000115:    - Requirements: "5+ years React, TypeScript, Node.js"
000116:    - Salary Range: "$120,000 - $160,000"
000117:    - Status: "Published"
000118: 5. Click "Create Job"
000119: 6. ✅ Job should appear in the list

000001: # Live Chat Setup (Realtime Database)
000002: 
000003: The live chat uses Firebase Realtime Database with anonymous sign-in for public users and full access for system admins.
000004: 
000005: ## Required Firebase Console Steps
000006: 
000007: 1) Enable anonymous auth:
000008:    - Firebase Console -> Authentication -> Sign-in method -> Anonymous -> Enable.
000009: 
000010: 2) Apply RTDB rules:
000011:    - Firebase Console -> Realtime Database -> Rules
000012:    - Paste the contents of `firebase.database.rules.json` and publish.
000013: 
000014: 3) Ensure system admins are registered in RTDB:
000015:    - The backend now writes `/admins/{uid}` on admin seed/bootstrap.
000016:    - If the admin account existed before, re-run the seed/bootstrap to register it.
000017: 
000018: ## Notes
000019: - Each browser session creates a separate chat session id stored in `sessionStorage`.
000020: - Anonymous visitors are asked for a display name before starting the chat.
000021: - Companies show user name plus company name in the chat UI.
000022: 
```

000001: # MediaPipe Body Language Detection System
000002: ## Complete Research Documentation for Interview Analysis
000003: 
000004: ---
000005: 
000006: ## Executive Summary
000007: 
000008: This document provides comprehensive technical documentation for the research-grade body language detection system implemented using Google's MediaPipe. The system tracks **553 landmarks** in real-time for comprehensive interview performance analysis, providing quantitative metrics for academic research and practical application in professional interview settings.
000009: 
000010: **System Version:** 3.0.0 - Complete Research Edition  
000011: **Last Updated:** January 28, 2026  
000012: **Author:** InterviewAI Pro Research Team
000013: 
000014: ---
000015: 
000016: ## Table of Contents
000017: 
000018: 1. [Introduction & Research Background](#1-introduction--research-background)
000019: 2. [System Architecture](#2-system-architecture)
000020: 3. [Detection Models](#3-detection-models)
000021: 4. [Landmark Specifications](#4-landmark-specifications)
000022: 5. [Metrics Calculations](#5-metrics-calculations)
000023: 6. [Scoring System](#6-scoring-system)
000024: 7. [Data Collection & Export](#7-data-collection--export)
000025: 8. [Validation & Accuracy](#8-validation--accuracy)
000026: 9. [Research Applications](#9-research-applications)

000031: 
000032: ## 1. Introduction & Research Background
000033: 
000034: ### 1.1 Research Context
000035: 
000036: Nonverbal communication plays a crucial role in professional interviews, accounting for up to 55% of communication impact according to Mehrabian's research (1971). This system provides objective, quantitative measurement of nonverbal cues that influence interview outcomes.
000037: 
000038: ### 1.2 Research Objectives
000039: 
000040: 1. **Quantify** body language metrics during video interviews
000041: 2. **Track** 553 anatomical landmarks in real-time
000042: 3. **Score** interview performance across 5 key dimensions
000043: 4. **Export** data for statistical analysis and research
000044: 
000045: ### 1.3 Key Research Questions Addressed
000046: 
000047: - How do posture and body alignment affect perceived professionalism?
000048: - What eye contact patterns correlate with positive interviewer impressions?
000049: - How does hand visibility and steadiness relate to perceived confidence?
000050: - Can facial expressions be quantified to assess engagement?
000051: 
000052: ---
000053: 
000054: ## 2. System Architecture
000055: 
000056: ### 2.1 Technology Stack
000057: 
000058: | Component | Technology | Purpose |
000059: |-----------|------------|---------|
000060: | Frontend | React 18 + Vite | User interface |
000061: | Detection | MediaPipe Tasks-Vision | AI-powered landmark detection |
000062: | Processing | WebGL + GPU | Real-time computation |
000063: | Storage | IndexedDB + localStorage | Client-side data persistence |
000064: | Export | JSON/CSV | Research data export |
000065: 
000066: ### 2.2 Architecture Diagram
000067: 
000068: ```
000069: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
000070: │                      VIDEO INPUT (Webcam)                        │
000071: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
000072:                                │
000073:                                ▼
000074: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
000075: │                    MediaPipe Detection Layer                     │
000076: │  ┌─────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────┐  │
000077: │  │  PoseLandmarker │  FaceLandmarker  │    HandLandmarker    │  │
000078: │  │  (33 landmarks) │ (478 landmarks)  │  (21 × 2 landmarks)  │  │
000079: │  └─────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────────┘  │
000080: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
000081:                                │
000082:                                ▼
000083: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
000084: │                    Metrics Calculation Engine                    │
000085: │  • Geometric calculations (angles, distances, ratios)           │
000086: │  • Temporal analysis (stability, movement over time)            │
000087: │  • Composite scoring (weighted multi-factor analysis)           │
000088: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
000089:                                │
000090:                                ▼
000091: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
000092: │                      Output Layer                                │
000093: │  ┌─────────────┬─────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐ │
000094: │  │ Real-time   │ Session Data    │ Research Reports           │ │
000095: │  │ Visualization│ Collection     │ (JSON/CSV/TXT)             │ │
000096: │  └─────────────┴─────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘ │
000097: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
000098: ```

000101: 
000102: ## 3. Detection Models
000103: 
000104: ### 3.1 PoseLandmarker (Body Skeleton)
000105: 
000106: **Landmarks:** 33  
000107: **Model:** `pose_landmarker_lite`  
000108: **Delegate:** GPU (WebGL)
000109: 
000110: Tracks the full body skeleton including:
000111: - Face reference points (nose, eyes, ears, mouth corners)
000112: - Upper body (shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands)
000113: - Lower body (hips, knees, ankles, feet)
000114: 
000115: ### 3.2 FaceLandmarker (Face Mesh)
000116: 
000117: **Landmarks:** 478 (468 face + 10 iris)  
000118: **Model:** `face_landmarker`  
000119: **Delegate:** GPU (WebGL)
000120: 
000121: Provides detailed facial analysis including:
000122: - Eye contours and iris tracking
000123: - Eyebrow positions
000124: - Nose and lip boundaries
000125: - Face oval and jaw line
000126: 
000127: ### 3.3 HandLandmarker (Hand Skeleton)
000128: 
000129: **Landmarks:** 21 per hand (42 total)  
000130: **Model:** `hand_landmarker`  
000131: **Delegate:** GPU (WebGL)
000132: 
000133: Tracks detailed hand anatomy:
000134: - Wrist position
000135: - All finger joints (MCP, PIP, DIP)
000136: - Fingertips for gesture recognition
000137: 
000138: ---
000139: 
000140: ## 4. Landmark Specifications
000141: 
000142: ### 4.1 Pose Landmarks (33 Total)

000181: 
000182: ## 5. Metrics Calculations
000183: 
000184: ### 5.1 Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR)
000185: 
000186: Used for blink detection and eye openness measurement.
000187: 
000188: **Formula:**
000189: ```
000190: EAR = vertical_distance / horizontal_distance
000191:     = distance(eye_top, eye_bottom) / distance(eye_left, eye_right)
000192: ```
000193: 
000194: **Reference Values:**
000195: | State | EAR Range |
000196: |-------|-----------|
000197: | Closed | < 0.16 |
000198: | Narrowed | 0.16 - 0.18 |
000199: | Normal | 0.22 - 0.26 |
000200: | Wide Open | > 0.35 |
000201: 
000202: ### 5.2 Mouth Aspect Ratio (MAR)
000203: 
000204: Used for speech detection.
000205: 
000206: **Formula:**
000207: ```
000208: MAR = vertical_distance / horizontal_distance
000209:     = distance(upper_lip, lower_lip) / distance(mouth_left, mouth_right)
000210: ```
000211: 
000212: **Reference Values:**
000213: | State | MAR Range |
000214: |-------|-----------|
000215: | Closed | < 0.05 |
000216: | Slightly Open | 0.05 - 0.12 |
000217: | Speaking | 0.12 - 0.18 |
000218: | Wide Open | > 0.35 |
000219: 
000220: ### 5.3 Face Orientation (Yaw, Pitch, Roll)
000221: 
000222: **Yaw (Left-Right Turn):**
000223: ```javascript
000224: yaw = atan2(eyeCenter.x - noseTip.x, |noseTip.z - eyeCenter.z|) × (180/π)
000225: ```
000226: 
000227: **Pitch (Up-Down Tilt):**
000228: ```javascript
000229: pitch = atan2(noseHeight - expectedNoseHeight, faceHeight) × (180/π)
000230: ```
000231: 
000232: **Roll (Head Tilt):**
000233: ```javascript
000234: roll = atan2(rightEye.y - leftEye.y, rightEye.x - leftEye.x) × (180/π)
000235: ```
000236: 
000237: ### 5.4 Shoulder Metrics
000238: 
000239: **Slope (Level Detection):**
000240: ```javascript
000241: slope = |leftShoulder.y - rightShoulder.y|
000242: ```
000243: 
000244: | Slope | Status | Score |
000245: |-------|--------|-------|
000246: | < 0.015 | Excellent | 100 |
000247: | < 0.030 | Good | 85 |
000248: | < 0.050 | Fair | 70 |
000249: | < 0.080 | Poor | 50 |
000250: | ≥ 0.100 | Critical | 30 |
000251: 
000252: ### 5.5 Finger Curl (Hand Analysis)
000253: 
000254: **Formula:**
000255: ```javascript
000256: angle1 = angle(MCP, PIP, DIP)
000257: angle2 = angle(PIP, DIP, TIP)
000258: curl = 1 - (average(angle1, angle2) / 180)
000259: // Result: 0 = extended, 1 = fully curled
000260: ```
000261: 
000262: ### 5.6 Body Stability
000263: 
000264: **Movement Magnitude:**
000265: ```javascript
000266: movement = average(
000267:   distance(currentNose, previousNose),
000268:   distance(currentLeftShoulder, previousLeftShoulder),
000269:   distance(currentRightShoulder, previousRightShoulder)
000270: )
000271: ```
000272: 
000273: **Reference Values:**
000274: | Movement | Status | Score |
000275: |----------|--------|-------|
000276: | < 0.005 | Very Still | 100 |
000277: | < 0.012 | Stable | 90 |
000278: | < 0.025 | Normal | 75 |
000279: | < 0.045 | Active | 60 |
000280: | < 0.070 | Restless | 40 |
000281: | > 0.100 | Excessive | 20 |
000282: 
000283: ---
000284: 
000285: ## 6. Scoring System
000286: 
000287: ### 6.1 Component Weights
000288: 
000289: | Component | Weight | Justification |
000290: |-----------|--------|---------------|
000291: | Eye Contact | 25% | Primary connection indicator |
000292: | Posture | 20% | Professional appearance |
000293: | Stability | 20% | Composure indicator |
000294: | Expression | 20% | Engagement/approachability |
000295: | Hands | 15% | Trust and confidence |
000296: 
000297: ### 6.2 Overall Score Formula
000298: 
000299: ```
000300: Overall = (Posture × 0.20) + (Eye Contact × 0.25) + (Expression × 0.20) 
000301:         + (Hands × 0.15) + (Stability × 0.20)
000302: ```
000303: 
000304: ### 6.3 Component Score Breakdown
000305: 
000306: #### Posture Score (0-100)
000307: ```
000308: Posture = (Shoulder Score × 0.40) + (Spine Score × 0.40) + (Head Score × 0.20)
000309: ```
000310: 
000311: #### Eye Contact Score (0-100)
000312: ```
000313: Eye Contact = (Orientation Score × 0.50) + (Gaze Score × 0.30) + (Eye Openness × 0.20)
000314: ```
000315: 
000316: #### Expression Score (0-100)
000317: ```
000318: Expression = (Naturalness × 0.40) + (Smile Score × 0.30) + (Mouth State × 0.30)
000319: ```
000320: 
000321: #### Hands Score (0-100)
000322: ```
000323: Hands = (Visibility × 0.40) + (Steadiness × 0.35) + (Openness × 0.25)
000324: ```
000325: 
000326: #### Stability Score (0-100)
000327: Based on body movement magnitude with thresholds defined in section 5.6.
000328: 
000329: ### 6.4 Score Levels
000330: 
000331: | Score Range | Level | Interpretation |
000332: |-------------|-------|----------------|
000333: | 90-100 | Excellent | Outstanding interview presence |
000334: | 75-89 | Good | Positive impression likely |
000335: | 60-74 | Fair | Acceptable with room for improvement |
000336: | 40-59 | Needs Improvement | Notable issues to address |
000337: | 0-39 | Poor | Significant concerns |
000338: 
000339: ---

000404: ## 8. Validation & Accuracy
000405: 
000406: ### 8.1 MediaPipe Model Accuracy
000407: 
000408: According to Google's documentation:
000409: - **PoseLandmarker:** ~95% accuracy on standard benchmarks
000410: - **FaceLandmarker:** ~98% accuracy for face detection
000411: - **HandLandmarker:** ~94% accuracy for hand detection
000412: 
000413: ### 8.2 System Validation
000414: 
000415: | Metric | Method | Expected Accuracy |
000416: |--------|--------|-------------------|
000417: | Eye Contact | Face orientation + gaze | ±5° yaw/pitch |
000418: | Blink Detection | EAR threshold | ~95% |
000419: | Speech Detection | MAR threshold | ~90% |
000420: | Shoulder Level | Slope calculation | ±1° |
000421: | Hand Gesture | Finger curl analysis | ~85% |
000422: 
000423: ### 8.3 Limitations
000424: 
000425: 1. **Lighting Conditions:** Performance degrades in low light
000426: 2. **Occlusion:** Partial visibility reduces accuracy
000427: 3. **Distance:** Optimal range 0.5-2m from camera
000428: 4. **Frame Rate:** Dependent on hardware (target 30+ FPS)
000429:

000537: ## Appendix A: Gesture Recognition Criteria
000538:

000541: | Open Palm | All 5 fingers extended, openness > 0.7 |
000542: | Closed Fist | No fingers extended, openness < 0.2 |
000543: | Pointing | Only index extended |

000550: ## Appendix B: Quick Reference Card
000551: 
000552: ### Score Interpretation
000553: 
000554: | Overall Score | Recommendation |
000555: |---------------|----------------|
000556: | 90+ | Excellent - Maintain current behavior |
000557: | 75-89 | Good - Minor refinements suggested |
000558: | 60-74 | Fair - Focus on weakest component |
000559: | 40-59 | Improve - Practice recommended |
000560: | < 40 | Significant training needed |
000561: 
000562: ### Key Thresholds
000563: 
000564: | Metric | Good | Concerning |
000565: |--------|------|------------|
000566: | Eye Contact | Yaw < 10° | Yaw > 25° |
000567: | Shoulder Level | Slope < 0.03 | Slope > 0.08 |
000568: | Stability | Movement < 0.012 | Movement > 0.045 |
000569: | Eye Openness | EAR > 0.22 | EAR < 0.18 |
000570: 
000571: ---
000572: 
000573: **Document Version:** 3.0.0  
000574: **Classification:** Research Documentation  
000575: **Status:** Production Ready
000576: 
000577: *This documentation supports the MediaPipe-based interview analysis system developed for academic research in nonverbal communication assessment.*
000578: 
```

000001: # Personality vs Interview Style - Redundancy Analysis
000002: 
000003: ## The Question
000004: Are "AI Interviewer Personality" and "Interview Style" doing the same thing? Are they redundant?
000005: 
000006: ## Current Implementation
000007: 
000008: ### Interview Style (Advanced Settings)
000009: **Location:** `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/components/AdvancedSettings.jsx`
000010: 
000011: **Options:**
000012: 1. `formal` - "Formal & Professional"
000013: 2. `conversational` - "Conversational & Relaxed"
000014: 3. `challenging` - "Challenging & Rigorous"
000015: 4. `supportive` - "Supportive & Encouraging"
000016: 
000017: **Description in UI:** "Choose the tone and approach for your AI interviewer"
000018: 
000019: **Actual Prompt Text:**
000020: - `formal`: "Use a formal and professional tone. Address the candidate with respect and maintain a structured, business-like approach throughout."
000021: - `conversational`: "Use a conversational and relaxed tone. Make the interview feel natural and comfortable, like a friendly discussion between professionals."
000022: - `challenging`: "Use a challenging and rigorous tone. Push the candidate to demonstrate their expertise and think critically about complex problems."
000023: - `supportive`: "Use a supportive and encouraging tone. Help the candidate feel comfortable and confident while still asking meaningful questions."
000024: 
000025: ### AI Interviewer Personality (Step 3)
000026: **Location:** `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/components/AIInterviewerPreview.jsx`
000027: 
000028: **Options (12 total):**
000029: 1. `professional-encouraging` - "Professional, thorough, and encouraging" - "Balanced and supportive approach"
000030: 2. `warm-insightful` - "Warm, insightful, and detail-oriented" - "Friendly and empathetic style"
000031: 3. `strategic-analytical` - "Strategic, analytical, and forward-thinking" - "Thoughtful and methodical approach"
000032: 4. `experienced-challenging` - "Experienced, challenging, and insightful" - "Rigorous and thought-provoking style"
000033: 5. `data-driven-methodical` - "Data-driven, methodical, and curious" - "Evidence-based and systematic approach"
000034: 6. `fast-paced-innovative` - "Fast-paced, innovative, and results-oriented" - "Dynamic and action-focused style"
000035: 7. `user-focused-empathetic` - "User-focused, empathetic, and creative" - "Human-centered and understanding approach"
000036: 8. `collaborative-team-oriented` - "Collaborative, team-oriented, and inclusive" - "Emphasizes teamwork and diverse perspectives"
000037: 9. `direct-transparent` - "Direct, transparent, and candid" - "Straightforward and honest communication style"
000038: 10. `growth-oriented-developmental` - "Growth-oriented, developmental, and supportive" - "Focuses on learning and continuous improvement"
000039: 11. `conversational-authentic` - "Conversational, authentic, and relatable" - "Natural and genuine interaction style"
000040: 12. `outcome-focused-metrics` - "Outcome-focused, metrics-driven, and results-oriented" - "Emphasizes measurable impact and performance"
000041: 
000042: **Actual Prompt Text Examples:**
000043: - `professional-encouraging`: "Professional, thorough, and encouraging. You maintain a balanced and supportive approach, providing constructive feedback while keeping the candidate at ease."
000044: - `conversational-authentic`: "Conversational, authentic, and relatable. You use a natural and genuine interaction style, making the interview feel like a real conversation between professionals."
000045: - `experienced-challenging`: "Experienced, challenging, and insightful. You use a rigorous and thought-provoking style, pushing candidates to demonstrate their true expertise and problem-solving abilities."
000046: - `growth-oriented-developmental`: "Growth-oriented, developmental, and supportive. You focus on learning and continuous improvement, helping candidates reflect on their experiences and growth potential."
000047: 
000048: ## Comparison Analysis
000049: 
000050: ### Overlap Examples
000051: 
000052: | Interview Style | Similar Personality | Match Level |
000053: |----------------|-------------------|-------------|
000054: | `formal` | `professional-encouraging` | 90% - Both emphasize professional, structured approach |
000055: | `conversational` | `conversational-authentic` | 95% - Nearly identical - both want natural, relaxed tone |
000056: | `challenging` | `experienced-challenging` | 95% - Both emphasize rigorous, pushing candidate |
000057: | `supportive` | `growth-oriented-developmental` or `warm-insightful` | 85% - Supportive/encouraging focus |
000058: 
000059: ### How They're Currently Combined
000060: 
000061: In `src/services/aiInterviewer.js`, both are added to the prompt:
000062: 
000063: ```javascript
000064: let personalityContext = '';
000065: if (personalityDesc) {
000066:   personalityContext = `\n\nYour personality and communication style: ${personalityDesc}`;
000067: }
000068: if (styleDesc) {
000069:   personalityContext += `\n\nInterview tone: ${styleDesc}`;
000070: }
000071: ```
000072: 
000073: **Example combined prompt:**
000074: ```
000075: Your personality and communication style: User-focused, empathetic, and creative. You take a human-centered and understanding approach...
000076: 
000077: Interview tone: Use a conversational and relaxed tone. Make the interview feel natural and comfortable...
000078: ```
000079: 
000080: ## The Problem
000081: 
000082: ### 1. **Redundancy**
000083: - Personality already includes tone/style information
000084: - Interview Style duplicates what personality already provides
000085: - Both control "how the AI communicates"
000086: 
000087: ### 2. **Conflicting Instructions**
000088: - If user selects `experienced-challenging` personality but `conversational` style, instructions conflict
000089: - Personality says "rigorous and thought-provoking" but style says "natural and comfortable"
000090: - The AI receives contradictory instructions
000091: 
000092: ### 3. **User Confusion**
000093: - User sees two settings that seem to do the same thing
000094: - Not clear which takes precedence
000095: - Difficult to understand the difference
000096: 
000097: ### 4. **Unnecessary Complexity**
000098: - Two separate settings when one would suffice
000099: - More configuration = more confusion
000100: - Extra fields to maintain and test
000101: 
000102: ## Recommendation
000103: 
000104: ### Option 1: Remove Interview Style (Recommended)
000105: **Pros:**
000106: - Personality is more comprehensive and detailed
000107: - Eliminates redundancy
000108: - Simpler for users
000109: - Personality already covers all style variations
000110: 
000111: **Cons:**
000112: - Removes a setting some users might prefer
000113: - Need to ensure personality options cover all use cases
000114: 
000115: **Implementation:**
000116: 1. Remove Interview Style from AdvancedSettings
000117: 2. Keep only Personality selection
000118: 3. Update any references to interviewStyle
000119: 
000120: ### Option 2: Make Interview Style a Quick Preset
000121: **Pros:**
000122: - Keeps both options
000123: - Style becomes a shortcut to select matching personality
000124: - Less confusing if presented as "preset personalities"
000125: 
000126: **Cons:**
000127: - Still redundant
000128: - More complex to maintain
000129: 
000130: **Implementation:**
000131: 1. When Interview Style is selected, auto-select matching Personality
000132: 2. Hide or disable Personality when Style is used
000133: 3. Or merge them into one selector with presets
000134: 
000135: ### Option 3: Use Style as a Tone Modifier
000136: **Pros:**
000137: - Different conceptual levels (personality = who, style = how)
000138: - Could work if personality = traits, style = formality level
000139: 
000140: **Cons:**
000141: - Current implementations overlap too much
000142: - Would require redesigning personality descriptions to exclude tone
000143: 
000144: ## Conclusion
000145: 
000146: **YES, they are redundant.** Both control the same thing: how the AI interviewer communicates. The Personality option is more detailed and comprehensive, while Interview Style is a simplified version.
000147: 
000148: **Best Solution:** Remove Interview Style and use Personality only. The personality options already cover all the styles:
000149: - Professional/Formal → `professional-encouraging`
000150: - Conversational → `conversational-authentic`
000151: - Challenging → `experienced-challenging`
000152: - Supportive → `growth-oriented-developmental` or `warm-insightful`
000153: 
000154: The personality system provides 12 nuanced options vs. 4 basic styles, making it more flexible and powerful.
000155: 
000156: 
```

000001: # Practice Interview Setup - Data Flow Analysis
000002: 
000003: ## Summary
000004: This document analyzes what data is collected during the practice interview setup process and how it flows through the system.
000005: 
000006: **Related Documents:**
000007: - See [practice-interview-fixes-summary.md](./practice-interview-fixes-summary.md) for summary of fixes applied
000008: - See [interview-style-removal-summary.md](./interview-style-removal-summary.md) for details on Interview Style removal
000009: 
000010: ## Data Collected in Setup Forms
000011: 
000012: ### Step 1: Job Details
000013: - ✅ `jobRole` - Selected job role
000014: - ✅ `experienceLevel` - Selected experience level  
000015: - ✅ `industry` - Selected industry
000016: 
000017: ### Step 2: Interview Setup
000018: - ✅ `interviewTypes` - Array of selected interview types
000019: - ✅ `sessionDuration` - Selected duration (default: 30)
000020: - ✅ `advancedSettings`:
000021:   - ✅ `skillFocus` - Array of skill areas to focus on
000022:   - ✅ `language` - Language preference (default: 'en')
000023:   - ✅ `realTimeFeedback` - Boolean flag
000024:   - ✅ `followUpQuestions` - Boolean flag
000025:   - ✅ `recordSession` - Boolean flag
000026:   - ✅ `practiceMode` - Boolean flag
000027:   - ✅ `difficulty` - Difficulty level (easy, medium, hard)
000028: 
000029: **Note:** Interview Style was removed as it was redundant with Personality (see Step 3).
000030: 
000031: ### Step 3: AI Interviewer
000032: - ✅ `personality` - Selected AI interviewer personality ID
000033: - ✅ `voice` - Selected voice/actor ID
000034: - ✅ `interviewerName` - Generated or custom interviewer name
000035: 
000036: ### Step 4: Preparation
000037: - No data collected (just a readiness checklist)
000038: 
000039: ---
000040: 
000041: ## What Gets Sent to API (when Start Interview is pressed)
000042: 
000043: **Location:** `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx:135-143`
000044: 
000045: Currently sent to API:
000046: ```javascript
000047: {
000048:   mode: 'PRACTICE',
000049:   jobRole: formData.jobRole,                    // ✅ SENT
000050:   experienceLevel: formData.experienceLevel,    // ✅ SENT
000051:   industry: formData.industry,                  // ✅ SENT
000052:   interviewTypes: formData.interviewTypes,      // ✅ SENT
000053:   skillFocus: formData.advancedSettings?.skillFocus,  // ✅ SENT
000054:   duration: formData.sessionDuration,           // ✅ SENT
000055:   config: {                                     // ✅ SENT (added in fixes)
000056:     personality: formData.personality,
000057:     voice: formData.voice,
000058:     interviewerName: formData.interviewerName,
000059:     advancedSettings: formData.advancedSettings
000060:   }
000061: }
000062: ```
000063: 
000064: **Note:** Additional configuration is now included in the `config` field, making all settings available to the backend.
000065: 
000066: ---
000067: 
000068: ## What Gets Saved to localStorage
000069: 
000070: **Location:** `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx:151-154`
000071: 
000072: ✅ **Full `formData` object is saved:**
000073: ```javascript
000074: localStorage.setItem('interviewConfig', JSON.stringify({
000075:   ...formData,  // Includes ALL fields
000076:   interviewId: result.interview.id,
000077: }));
000078: ```
000079: 
000080: This means all collected data is available in the interview session via localStorage.
000081: 
000082: ---
000083: 
000084: ## What Gets Used in Live Interview Session
000085: 
000086: **Location:** `src/pages/live-interview-session/index.jsx:125-161`
000087: 
000088: The session loads config using a multi-source fallback mechanism:
000089: 
000090: ```javascript
000091: // Priority order:
000092: // 1. localStorage (if available)
000093: // 2. Backend database (if localStorage missing and interviewId available)
000094: // 3. Default values (if both unavailable)
000095: 
000096: const configStr = localStorage.getItem('interviewConfig');
000097: let config = configStr ? JSON.parse(configStr) : null;
000098: 
000099: // Fallback to backend if localStorage missing
000100: if (!config && interviewId) {
000101:   const response = await apiClient.interviews.getById(interviewId);
000102:   config = buildConfigFromInterview(response.interview);
000103: }
000104: 
000105: // Final fallback to defaults
000106: if (!config) {
000107:   config = { /* defaults */ };
000108: }
000109: 
000110: await initializeInterview(config);
000111: ```
000112: 
000113: **Improvement:** Config is now loaded from multiple sources, ensuring availability even after browser refresh or localStorage clearance.
000114: 
000115: ### Used by useAIInterviewer Hook
000116: 
000117: **Location:** `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js:159-250`
000118: 
000119: ✅ **USED:**
000120: - `interviewConfig.voice` - Used to configure TTS voice (lines 195-214)
000121: - `interviewConfig.personality` - Used in AI prompts (via personalityMapper)
000122: - `interviewConfig.interviewerName` - Used in AI prompts and displayed in UI
000123: - `interviewConfig.advancedSettings.difficulty` - Used in question generation prompts
000124: - `interviewConfig.advancedSettings.followUpQuestions` - Enforced in answer processing
000125: - `interviewConfig.advancedSettings.language` - ✅ Used in transcription (Whisper) and browser STT
000126: - All config passed to `createAIInterviewer()` (lines 217-220)
000127: 
000128: ✅ **USED:**
000129: - `advancedSettings.realTimeFeedback` - ✅ Feature now conditionally displayed based on flag
000130: - `advancedSettings.practiceMode` - ✅ Pause/resume and retry functionality implemented (re-speaks question)
000131: - `advancedSettings.recordSession` - ✅ Recording state managed based on flag
000132: 
000133: **Config Merging:**
000134: - Backend config merged with localStorage config when both exist (backend takes precedence)
000135: - Ensures most up-to-date configuration is used
000136: 
000137: ### Used by Backend LLM Service
000138: 
000139: **Location:** `server/src/services/llm.service.js:93-132`
000140: 
000141: ✅ **USED in question generation:**
000142: - `jobRole`
000143: - `experienceLevel`
000144: - `industry`
000145: - `interviewTypes`
000146: - `skillFocus`
000147: - `totalQuestions` (derived from duration)
000148: - `personality` - ✅ Now used to influence question style and tone
000149: - `difficulty` - ✅ Now used to control question complexity (easy/medium/hard)
000150: - `interviewerName` - ✅ Used in question generation prompts
000151: 
000152: ### Used by Frontend AI Interviewer
000153: 
000154: **Location:** `src/services/aiInterviewer.js:21-30`
000155: 
000156: ✅ **USED:**
000157: - `jobRole`
000158: - `company` (default: 'Tech Company')
000159: - `experienceLevel`
000160: - `industry`
000161: - `interviewTypes`
000162: - `interviewDuration`
000163: - `totalQuestions`
000164: - `personality` - ✅ Used in all system prompts (via personalityMapper)
000165: - `interviewerName` - ✅ Used in system prompts and displayed in UI
000166: - `advancedSettings.difficulty` - ✅ Used in question generation instructions
000167: - `advancedSettings.followUpQuestions` - ✅ Enforced in answer processing logic
000168: 
000169: ---
000170: 
000171: ## Issues & Recommendations
000172: 
000173: ### Issue 1: Missing Data in API Payload (RESOLVED)
000174: **Problem:** Many collected fields are not sent to the backend API, so they cannot be stored in the database or used by backend services.
000175: 
000176: **Resolution:**
000177: - Updated `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js` to extract `config` from request body
000178: - Updated `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js` to store `config` field in interview record
000179: - All configuration (personality, voice, interviewerName, advancedSettings) is now persisted in database
000180: 
000181: **Status:** ✅ **FIXED** - Config object is now stored in backend interview record.
000182: 
000183: ### Issue 2: Personality Not Used in Prompts (RESOLVED)
000184: **Problem:** User selects a personality but it's not incorporated into the AI interviewer's behavior.
000185: 
000186: **Resolution:**
000187: - Created personalityMapper.js to map personality IDs to descriptions
000188: - Updated all AI interviewer prompts to include personality descriptions
000189: - Personality now influences communication style throughout the interview
000190: 
000191: **Status:** ✅ **FIXED** - Personality is now used in all AI prompts.
000192: 
000193: ### Issue 3: Interview Style Removed (RESOLVED)
000194: **Problem:** Interview Style was redundant with Personality - both controlled the same thing.
000195: 
000196: **Resolution:**
000197: - Interview Style has been removed from Advanced Settings
000198: - Personality now controls all communication style and tone
000199: - Eliminated redundancy and potential conflicts
000200: 
000201: **Status:** ✅ **FIXED** - Interview Style removed, using Personality only.
000202: 
000203: ### Issue 4: Difficulty Setting Not Used (RESOLVED)
000204: **Problem:** User selects difficulty level but questions are generated with LLM-determined difficulty.
000205: 
000206: **Resolution:**
000207: - Difficulty is now used in frontend AI interviewer prompts
000208: - Difficulty affects question complexity during the interview
000209: - Updated backend LLM service (`server/src/services/llm.service.js`) to use difficulty when generating questions
000210: - Backend question generation now respects selected difficulty level (easy/medium/hard)
000211: - Personality descriptions added to backend LLM service to influence question style
000212: 
000213: **Status:** ✅ **FIXED** - Difficulty is used in both frontend and backend question generation.
000214: 
000215: ### Issue 5: Advanced Settings Flags Not Enforced (RESOLVED)
000216: **Problem:** Flags like `followUpQuestions`, `realTimeFeedback`, `practiceMode` exist but aren't used to control behavior.
000217: 
000218: **Resolution:**
000219: - `followUpQuestions` - ✅ Now enforced in answer processing logic
000220: - `realTimeFeedback` - ✅ Feature conditionally displayed based on flag (RealTimeFeedbackPanel only shows when enabled)
000221: - `practiceMode` - ✅ Pause/resume functionality implemented, retry button added to SessionControlPanel
000222: - `recordSession` - ✅ Recording state initialized from flag and properly managed throughout session
000223: 
000224: **Status:** ✅ **FIXED** - All advanced settings flags are now properly enforced.
000225: 
000226: ### Issue 6: Interviewer Name Not Used (RESOLVED)
000227: **Problem:** Generated/custom interviewer name is saved but not displayed or used in prompts.
000228: 
000229: **Resolution:**
000230: - Interviewer name is now used in all AI prompts
000231: - Name is displayed in the interview session UI (AI Interviewer Panel)
000232: 
000233: **Status:** ✅ **FIXED** - Interviewer name is used in prompts and displayed in UI.
000234: 
000235: ---
000236: 
000237: ## Fixes Applied
000238: 
000239: ### ✅ Completed Fixes
000240: 
000241: 1. **API payload updated** - Added `config` field with all additional configuration
000242: 2. **Backend storage** - Config object now stored in interview record (`server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`)
000243: 3. **Personality integrated** - Now used in all frontend and backend AI prompts
000244: 4. **Interview Style removed** - Eliminated redundancy with Personality
000245: 5. **Interviewer name** - Used in prompts and displayed in UI
000246: 6. **Difficulty** - Now used in both frontend and backend question generation
000247: 7. **Follow-up questions** - Flag now enforced in answer processing
000248: 8. **Backend question generation** - Uses personality and difficulty when initially generating questions
000249: 9. **Real-time feedback** - Feature conditionally displayed based on flag
000250: 10. **Practice mode** - Pause/resume and retry functionality implemented
000251: 11. **Session recording** - Recording state managed based on flag
000252: 12. **URL parameter handling** - Support for both `interviewId` and `id` URL parameters
000253: 13. **Backend config loading** - Config loads from database when localStorage is missing
000254: 14. **Language setting** - Language preference now used in transcription and TTS
000255: 15. **Config merging** - Backend config properly merged with localStorage config
000256: 16. **skillFocus in backend** - skillFocus now passed to backend LLM service
000257: 
000258: ### ✅ All Issues Resolved
000259: 
000260: All identified issues have been resolved. The system now fully utilizes all collected configuration data and handles edge cases properly.
000261: 
000262: ## Current State Summary
000263: 
000264: **✅ All collected data is now:**
000265: - Sent to API (in `config` field)
000266: - Stored in backend database (interview record)
000267: - Saved to localStorage (for session access)
000268: - **Loaded from backend when localStorage missing** - Fallback mechanism ensures config availability
000269: - Used in frontend AI prompts (personality, name, difficulty, follow-up flag)
000270: - Used in backend question generation (personality, difficulty, interviewerName, skillFocus)
000271: - Displayed in UI (interviewer name)
000272: - All advanced settings flags properly enforced:
000273:   - Real-time feedback panel conditionally displayed
000274:   - Practice mode pause/resume/retry functional (includes re-speaking question)
000275:   - Session recording state managed
000276:   - Language preference used in speech recognition and transcription
000277: 
000278: **✅ Edge cases handled:**
000279: - URL parameter flexibility (supports both `interviewId` and `id`)
000280: - Config loading from multiple sources (localStorage → backend → defaults)
000281: - Config merging when multiple sources exist (backend takes precedence)
000282: - Error handling for missing config scenarios
000283: 
000284:

000001: # Practice Interview Setup - Fixes Summary
000002: 
000003: ## Overview
000004: This document summarizes the fixes applied to ensure all data collected during the practice interview setup process is properly captured and used when starting the interview.
000005: 
000006: **Related Documents:**
000007: - See [practice-interview-data-flow-analysis.md](./practice-interview-data-flow-analysis.md) for detailed data flow analysis
000008: - See [interview-style-removal-summary.md](./interview-style-removal-summary.md) for details on Interview Style removal
000009: 
000010: ## Issues Identified
000011: 
000012: ### 1. Missing Data in API Payload
000013: **Problem:** Many configuration fields (personality, voice, interviewerName, advancedSettings) were collected but not sent to the backend API.
000014: 
000015: **Fix Applied:**
000016: - Updated `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx` to include a `config` field in the API payload containing all additional configuration data.
000017: - The full `formData` is already saved to localStorage, so all data is available in the interview session.
000018: 
000019: ### 2. Personality Not Used in AI Prompts
000020: **Problem:** User-selected personality was saved but not used to influence AI interviewer behavior.
000021: 
000022: **Fix Applied:**
000023: - Created `src/utils/personalityMapper.js` to map personality IDs to descriptive text.
000024: - Updated `src/services/aiInterviewer.js` to include personality descriptions in all system prompts.
000025: - Personality now influences the AI's communication style throughout the interview.
000026: 
000027: ### 3. Interview Style Removed (Redundancy Fix)
000028: **Problem:** Interview Style was redundant with Personality - both controlled the same thing (AI communication style), causing confusion and potential conflicts.
000029: 
000030: **Fix Applied:**
000031: - Removed Interview Style from Advanced Settings component.
000032: - Removed interviewStyle from form data and defaults.
000033: - Removed interviewStyle from AI prompts.
000034: - Now using Personality only, which is more comprehensive (12 options vs 4).
000035: 
000036: **Note:** Interview Style options (formal, conversational, challenging, supportive) are all covered by Personality options:
000037: - Formal → `professional-encouraging`
000038: - Conversational → `conversational-authentic`
000039: - Challenging → `experienced-challenging`
000040: - Supportive → `growth-oriented-developmental` or `warm-insightful`
000041: 
000042: ### 4. Difficulty Setting Not Enforced
000043: **Problem:** User-selected difficulty level was not used when generating questions.
000044: 
000045: **Fix Applied:**
000046: - Updated AI interviewer prompts to include difficulty level in question generation instructions.
000047: - Difficulty is now respected when the AI asks questions.
000048: 
000049: ### 5. Interviewer Name Not Displayed
000050: **Problem:** Generated/custom interviewer name was saved but not displayed in the UI.
000051: 
000052: **Fix Applied:**
000053: - Updated `src/pages/live-interview-session/components/AIInterviewerPanel.jsx` to accept and display interviewer name.
000054: - Updated `src/pages/live-interview-session/index.jsx` to pass interviewer name from config to the panel.
000055: - Interviewer name is now shown in the interview session UI.
000056: 
000057: ### 6. Follow-Up Questions Flag Not Enforced
000058: **Problem:** `followUpQuestions` setting existed but wasn't used to control behavior.
000059:

000001: # PROJECT_SUMMARY
000002: 
000003: ## What This Repo Is
000004: 
000005: InterviewAI Pro is a React/Vite single-page app plus an Express backend that uses Firebase (Auth + Firestore + Realtime DB) and optional local AI services (Ollama for LLM, Faster-Whisper for speech-to-text, MediaPipe for pose analysis). See `README.md`, `src/`, `server/`.
000006: 
000007: ## High-Level Architecture (Runtime)
000008: 
000009: - **Frontend (SPA)**: Vite + React app mounted from `index.html` → `src/index.jsx` → `src/App.jsx` → `src/Routes.jsx`.
000010: - **Backend API + sockets**: Express + Socket.IO server in `server/src/server.js`, with routes mounted in `server/src/routes/index.js`.
000011: - **Data stores**:
000012:   - Firestore collections and helpers in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`
000013:   - Firebase Realtime DB usage for “live session events” in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js` (`recordRealtimeEvent`) and Socket.IO handlers in `server/src/socket/interview.socket.js`.
000014: - **Optional local AI services**:
000015:   - Ollama (frontend calls via `src/services/llmClient.js`, backend calls via `server/src/services/llm.service.js`)
000016:   - Local Whisper server (Python) in `server/whisper_server.py`, called by `src/services/localWhisperService.js`
000017:   - MediaPipe pose detection (browser) via `src/hooks/usePoseDetection.js` and stored locally via `src/services/poseAnalyticsStorage.js`
000018: 
000019: ## Repository Layout
000020: 
000021: - Frontend app code: `src/`
000022:   - Routing: `src/Routes.jsx`
000023:   - Auth state/context: `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx`
000024:   - Firebase client wrapper: `src/config/firebase.js`
000025:   - Backend API client: `src/services/apiClient.js`
000026:   - AI interviewer (local Ollama): `src/services/aiInterviewer.js` and `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js`
000027:   - Live session page: `src/pages/live-interview-session/index.jsx` and `src/pages/live-interview-session/components/*`
000028:   - Practice setup wizard: `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx` and `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/components/*`
000029:   - Company dashboard + recruiting tools: `src/pages/company-dashboard/index.jsx` and `src/pages/company-dashboard/components/*`
000030:   - Candidate dashboard + assistant: `src/pages/candidate-dashboard/index.jsx` and `src/pages/candidate-dashboard/components/*`
000031: - Backend app code: `server/src/`
000032:   - Entry point: `server/src/server.js`
000033:   - Firebase Admin + env loading: `server/src/config/firebase.js`, `server/src/config/env.js`
000034:   - Auth middleware: `server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js`
000035:   - Route mounting: `server/src/routes/index.js`
000036:   - Controllers: `server/src/controllers/*.controller.js`
000037:   - Stores/services (Firestore + Realtime DB + Ollama + moderation): `server/src/services/*.service.js`
000038:   - Socket.IO handlers: `server/src/socket/interview.socket.js`
000039: - Static assets (PWA-ish): `public/` (see `public/manifest.json`, `public/assets/`)
000040: - CI deploy to GitHub Pages: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
000041: - Engineering notes: `docs/*.md` (these are not authoritative over implementation; compare with current code in `src/` and `server/src/`)
000042: 
000043: ## How To Run Locally
000044: 
000045: ### Frontend
000046: 
000047: - Install deps: `npm install` (root `package.json`)
000048: - Start dev server: `npm start` (root `package.json`, Vite config in `vite.config.mjs` uses port `4028`)
000049: 
000050: ### Backend
000051: 
000052: - Install deps: `cd server && npm install` (server `server/package.json`)
000053: - Create env file: copy `server/.env.example` → `server/.env` (loaded by `server/src/config/env.js`)
000054: - Start API/sockets: `cd server && npm run dev` (server `server/package.json`)
000055: 
000056: ### Optional: Ollama (LLM)
000057: 
000058: - Frontend calls Ollama directly via `src/services/llmClient.js` (uses `VITE_OLLAMA_URL`, `VITE_OLLAMA_MODEL` from root `.env`).
000059: - Backend calls Ollama directly via `server/src/services/llm.service.js` (uses `OLLAMA_URL`, `OLLAMA_MODEL` from `server/.env.example` / `server/.env`).
000060: 
000061: ### Optional: Local Whisper (speech-to-text)
000062: 
000063: - Whisper server: `server/whisper_server.py` (deps in `server/requirements.txt`)
000064: - Frontend uses it only when `VITE_LOCAL_WHISPER_URL` is set (see `src/services/localWhisperService.js`).
000065: 
000066: ## Environment Variables (Verified Keys)
000067: 
000068: ### Frontend (`.env`)
000069: 
000070: Keys present in the repo’s root `.env` (values intentionally not shown): `VITE_API_URL`, `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`, `VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET`, `VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID`, `VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID`, `VITE_FIREBASE_DATABASE_URL`, `VITE_OLLAMA_URL`, `VITE_OLLAMA_MODEL` (root `.env`, Firebase client usage in `src/config/firebase.js`, API base usage in `src/services/apiClient.js`).
000071: 
000072: Optional key used by code: `VITE_LOCAL_WHISPER_URL` (checked in `src/services/localWhisperService.js`).
000073: 
000074: ### Backend (`server/.env`)
000075: 
000076: Keys present in `server/.env` (values intentionally not shown): `PORT`, `NODE_ENV`, `FRONTEND_URL`, `FIREBASE_DATABASE_URL`, `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH`, `SIGHTENGINE_USER`, `SIGHTENGINE_SECRET`, `OLLAMA_URL`, `OLLAMA_MODEL`, `WHISPER_SERVER_URL`, `WHISPER_MODEL`, `STUN_SERVER`, `LOG_LEVEL` (`server/.env.example`, loaded by `server/src/config/env.js`).
000077: 
000078: ## Auth Model (Frontend ↔ Backend)
000079: 
000080: - Frontend uses Firebase Auth (email/password + Google) via `src/config/firebase.js` and maintains app-level state in `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx`.
000081: - Backend verifies Firebase ID tokens in `server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js` using `server/src/config/firebase.js` (`verifyFirebaseToken`).
000082: - After token verification, the backend loads the user profile from Firestore (`userStore.getByUid`) and attaches org context if `primaryOrganizationId` exists (`server/src/middleware/auth.middleware.js`, stores in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`).
000083: - Route gating in the SPA is based on `user.accountType` via `src/components/ProtectedRoute.jsx` and the route table in `src/Routes.jsx`.
000084: 
000085: ## Registration + Upload Moderation
000086: 
000087: Registration is a two-step sync:
000088: 
000089: 1. User signs up/signs in with Firebase on the frontend (`src/config/firebase.js`, used by `src/pages/register/index.jsx` and `src/pages/login/index.jsx`).
000090: 2. Frontend calls backend `POST /api/auth/register` via `src/services/apiClient.js` (route in `server/src/routes/auth.routes.js`, implementation in `server/src/controllers/auth.controller.js`).
000091: 
000092: Backend registration behavior (verified in `server/src/controllers/auth.controller.js`):
000093: 
000094: - **Candidate** requires `profilePhoto` + `resumeFile` uploads and validates:
000095:   - Profile photo moderation via Sightengine when configured (`server/src/services/imageModeration.service.js`)
000096:   - Resume parsing + heuristics + optional LLM verification (`server/src/services/documentModeration.service.js`, `server/src/services/llm.service.js`)
000097:   - Resume hash dedupe against existing users (`userStore.findByResumeHash` in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`)
000098: - **Company** requires `companyLogo` + `companyProof` uploads and validates similarly (logo moderation + document verification + hash dedupe via `userStore.findByVerificationHash`).
000099: - Uploads are stored under `server/uploads/*` and served statically at `/uploads` (`server/src/server.js`, upload paths in `server/src/middleware/upload.middleware.js`).
000100: - Company registration creates an organization + admin membership (`organizationStore.create`, `organizationMemberStore.addMember` in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`, orchestrated in `server/src/controllers/auth.controller.js`).
000101: 
000102: There are also standalone moderation endpoints (no auth) under `/api/uploads/moderate/*` (`server/src/routes/upload.routes.js`, called by `src/services/apiClient.js`).
000103: 
000104: ## Data Model (Firestore + Realtime DB)
000105: 
000106: Firestore collections used by the backend (defined in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`):
000107: 
000108: - `users`
000109: - `interviews` (+ subcollections: `questions`, `poseData`)
000110: - `webrtcSessions`
000111: - `organizations`
000112: - `organizationMembers`
000113: - `jobs`
000114: - `invitations`
000115: - `interviewReviews`
000116: - `activityLogs`
000117: 
000118: Realtime Database usage (defined in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js`):
000119: 
000120: - Events written under `sessions/{interviewId}/events` and `sessions/{interviewId}/lastEvent` by `recordRealtimeEvent` (called from Socket.IO handlers in `server/src/socket/interview.socket.js`).
000121: 
000122: ## Backend API Surface (Route Map)
000123: 
000124: Routes are mounted in `server/src/routes/index.js` and mirrored by client helpers in `src/services/apiClient.js`.
000125: 
000126: Key groups:
000127: 
000128: - Auth: `server/src/routes/auth.routes.js` (`/api/auth/*`)
000129: - Interviews: `server/src/routes/interview.routes.js` (`/api/interviews/*`) with orchestration in `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js`
000130: - Analytics: `server/src/routes/analytics.routes.js` (`/api/analytics/*`) with stats in `server/src/services/firebaseData.service.js` (`analyticsStore`)
000131: - Video/WebRTC: `server/src/routes/video.routes.js` (`/api/video/*`) with ICE config in `server/src/controllers/video.controller.js`
000132: - Organizations: `server/src/routes/organization.routes.js` (`/api/organizations/*`)
000133: - Jobs: `server/src/routes/job.routes.js` and public job browsing via `server/src/routes/public.routes.js`
000134: - Invitations: `server/src/routes/invitation.routes.js` and public preview via `server/src/routes/public.routes.js`
000135: - Pipeline: `server/src/routes/pipeline.routes.js`
000136: - Reviews: `server/src/routes/review.routes.js`
000137: - Activity: `server/src/routes/activity.routes.js`
000138: - Upload moderation: `server/src/routes/upload.routes.js`
000139: 
000140: ## Core User Flows
000141: 
000142: ### Practice Interview (Candidate)
000143: 
000144: - Setup wizard collects role/type/duration/personality/voice/advanced settings in `src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx`.
000145: - Creates a `PRACTICE` interview on the backend via `src/services/apiClient.js` → `POST /api/interviews/create` (`server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js`).
000146: - Saves config to localStorage as `interviewConfig` and navigates to the live session (`src/pages/practice-interview-setup/index.jsx`).
000147: 
000148: ### Live Interview Session (Candidate)
000149: 
000150: - Loads config from localStorage, else falls back to backend interview record (`src/pages/live-interview-session/index.jsx`).
000151: - Runs the local AI interviewer (Ollama) via `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js` and `src/services/aiInterviewer.js`.
000152: - Optionally records microphone audio and transcribes with local Whisper when enabled (`src/services/audioRecorderService.js`, `src/services/localWhisperService.js`).

000154: - Backend sync for question/answer persistence is done opportunistically via `src/services/interviewBackendSync.js` from inside `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js`.

000156: Notable implementation detail: the UI “end session” flow concludes the local AI interview and navigates away without calling the backend `POST /api/interviews/:id/end` endpoint (`src/pages/live-interview-session/index.jsx`, backend endpoint in `server/src/routes/interview.routes.js` / `server/src/controllers/interview.controller.js`).

000159: 
000160: - Company dashboard data loads interviews + metrics via `src/pages/company-dashboard/index.jsx` (backend endpoints in `server/src/routes/interview.routes.js`, `server/src/routes/analytics.routes.js`).

000166: 
000167: ## AI/ML Components (Where They Live)
000168: 
000169: - **Local LLM client (frontend)**: `src/services/llmClient.js`, with higher-level helpers in `src/services/llmServices.js` and hook wrapper `src/hooks/useLLM.js`.
000170: - **AI interviewer (frontend)**: `src/services/aiInterviewer.js`, orchestrated by `src/hooks/useAIInterviewer.js`.

000187:

000189: - When user confirms resolve flow, active applications become terminal before job removal from active lists.
000190: 
000191: ### C. Candidate transparency for closed roles
000192: 
000193: 1. Resolve-and-delete a job with active applications.
000194: 2. Open candidate applications view.
000195: 
000196: Expected:
000197: 
000198: - Application displays closed/deleted role context (not blank/unknown).
000199: - Status is visible with closure context (Position Closed / rejected via closure disposition).
000200: - Candidate receives closure status communication if notifications were enabled.
000201: 
000202: ### D. Disposition reason capture
000203: 
000204: 1. Recruiter manually sets an application to `REJECTED`.
000205: 2. Provide a disposition option in the prompt.
000206: 3. Re-open application details.
000207: 
000208: Expected:
000209: 
000210: - Disposition reason/code appears in recruiter view.
000211: - Candidate view surfaces the disposition label/reason.
000212: - Status trail metadata is persisted by backend.
000213: 
000214: ## 7. ATS core governance + scale verification (new)
000215: 
000216: ### A. Status transition guardrails
000217: 
000218: 1. Move an application through normal stages (e.g., `SUBMITTED -> SCREENING -> INTERVIEWING -> REJECTED`).
000219: 2. Attempt invalid transition from terminal state (e.g., `REJECTED -> SCREENING`).
000220: 
000221: Expected:
000222: 
000223: - Valid transitions succeed.
000224: - Invalid terminal transition is rejected with conflict response and allowed-next-status metadata.
000225: 
000226: ### B. Bulk application updates
000227: 
000228: 1. Select a set of applications in different jobs within same organization.
000229: 2. Call bulk status endpoint (or wire UI action) with one target status.
000230: 
000231: Expected:
000232: 
000233: - Endpoint returns updated/skipped summary with per-item result.
000234: - Realtime feeds update for candidate and organization viewers.
000235: 
000236: ### C. Invitation-to-application continuity
000237: 
000238: 1. Create a job invitation.
000239: 2. Accept invitation as candidate.
000240: 3. Open company applications view and candidate applications view.
000241: 
000242: Expected:
000243: 
000244: - Accepted invitation creates or advances an ATS application into interviewing flow.
000245: - Application appears in both company and candidate application surfaces.
000246: - Duplicate active invitation for same job+email is blocked.
000247: 
000248: ### D. Organization interview scope
000249: 
000250: 1. Create interview with one recruiter in organization.
000251: 2. Open company interview list and interview detail with a different recruiter/reviewer in same organization.
000252: 
000253: Expected:
000254: 
000255: - Interview appears in organization-scoped company list.
000256: - Authorized organization member can access detail successfully.
000257: 
```

000001: # Fix Proposal: Remove Interview Style Redundancy
000002: 
000003: ## Problem
000004: Interview Style and Personality are redundant and can conflict. Both control the same thing (AI communication style).
000005: 
000006: ## Current Issues
000007: 
000008: ### 1. Redundant Control
000009: Both settings control AI communication style/tone:
000010: - **Interview Style**: Simple tone selector (4 options)
000011: - **Personality**: Detailed personality traits (12 options)
000012: 
000013: ### 2. Potential Conflicts
000014: Example conflict:
000015: - Personality: `experienced-challenging` → "rigorous and thought-provoking style"
000016: - Style: `conversational` → "natural and comfortable"
000017: - **Result**: Contradictory instructions to AI
000018: 
000019: ### 3. User Confusion
000020: - Two settings doing the same thing
000021: - Unclear which takes precedence
000022: - Extra cognitive load
000023: 
000024: ## Recommended Solution
000025: 
000026: ### Remove Interview Style from Advanced Settings
000027: 
000028: **Reasoning:**
000029: - Personality is more comprehensive (12 options vs 4)
000030: - Personality already includes tone/style information
000031: - All style variations are covered by personality options
000032: 
000033: ### Personality Coverage of Styles
000034: 
000035: | Interview Style | Personality Equivalent |
000036: |----------------|----------------------|
000037: | Formal & Professional | `professional-encouraging` |
000038: | Conversational & Relaxed | `conversational-authentic` |
000039: | Challenging & Rigorous | `experienced-challenging` |
000040: | Supportive & Encouraging | `growth-oriented-developmental` or `warm-insightful` |
000041: 
000042: ### Implementation Steps
000043: 
000044: 1. **Remove from UI:**
000045:    - Remove Interview Style Select from AdvancedSettings component
000046:    - Remove from formData.advancedSettings
000047:    - Remove from default state
000048: 
000049: 2. **Remove from prompts:**
000050:    - Remove interviewStyle from AI prompts in aiInterviewer.js
000051:    - Remove getInterviewStyleDescription usage
000052:    - Keep only personality descriptions
000053: 
000054: 3. **Update documentation:**
000055:    - Remove references to interviewStyle
000056:    - Clarify that Personality controls communication style
000057: 
000058: 4. **Migration (if needed):**
000059:    - If existing data has interviewStyle, could auto-map to personality
000060:    - Or simply ignore it going forward
000061: 
000062: ## Alternative: Keep as Quick Preset
000063: 
000064: If we want to keep both, make Interview Style a quick preset that auto-selects matching Personality:
000065: 
000066: - User selects "Conversational" style → Auto-selects "conversational-authentic" personality
000067: - Disable manual personality selection when style is used
000068: - Or show personality as "auto-selected" based on style
000069: 
000070: **But this is still redundant - better to just remove it.**
000071: 
000072: ## Impact Assessment
000073: 
000074: ### Breaking Changes
000075: - Users who rely on Interview Style will need to use Personality instead
000076: - Existing saved configs with interviewStyle will be ignored
000077: 
000078: ### Benefits
000079: - Simpler UI (one less setting)
000080: - Clearer user experience
000081: - No conflicting instructions
000082: - Less code to maintain
000083: 
000084: ## Recommendation
000085: 
000086: **Remove Interview Style entirely.** It's redundant and the Personality system is superior.
000087: 
000088: 
```
