000001: # Research Data Collection Guide
000002: 
000003: ## Complete Guide for LLM and MediaPipe Data Collection
000004: 
000005: This document provides a comprehensive guide for collecting training data from multiple sources as required for the research project.
000006: 
000007: ---
000008: 
000009: ## Part 1: LLM Interview Dialogue Data Collection
000010: 
000011: ### Overview
000012: To train an LLM for interview-style dialogue, we need diverse conversational data from multiple sources:
000013: 1. **External Datasets** - Pre-existing interview datasets from the internet
000014: 2. **Web Sources** - Gather interview examples from websites
000015: 3. **Our System** - Auto-collected data from actual interview sessions
000016: 4. **Synthetic Data** - Generate interview dialogues using LLMs
000017: 
000018: ---
000019: 
000020: ### Source 1: External Datasets (Ready to Use)
000021: 
000022: #### Hugging Face Datasets
000023: 
000024: | Dataset | Description | Size | Link |
000025: |---------|-------------|------|------|
000026: | **Anthropic/AnthropicInterviewer** | ~1,250 interview transcripts (workforce, creatives, scientists) | 4.8k-26.8k chars each | https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/AnthropicInterviewer |
000027: | **ali-alkhars/interviews** | 2,290 interview Q&A pairs (Angular, TypeScript, software roles) | 2,290 rows | https://huggingface.co/datasets/ali-alkhars/interviews |
000028: | **HR-MultiWOZ** | Task-oriented HR dialogue dataset | Large | https://amazon.science/code-and-datasets/hr-multiwoz |
000029: 
000030: #### Kaggle Datasets
000031: 
000032: | Dataset | Description | Size | Link |
000033: |---------|-------------|------|------|
000034: | **Software Engineering Interview Questions** | 250 questions with answers (algorithms, system design, ML) | 250 Q&A | https://kaggle.com/datasets/syedmharis/software-engineering-interview-questions-dataset |
000035: | **Coding Questions with Solutions** | Python interview problems with solutions | 5,000+ | https://kaggle.com/datasets/thedevastator/coding-questions-with-solutions |
000036: 
000037: #### How to Download
000038: 
000039: **From Hugging Face:**
000040: ```python
000041: from datasets import load_dataset
000042: 
000043: # Anthropic Interview Dataset
000044: dataset = load_dataset("Anthropic/AnthropicInterviewer")
000045: print(dataset)
000046: 
000047: # Ali-alkhars Interviews
000048: dataset = load_dataset("ali-alkhars/interviews")
000049: print(dataset)
000050: ```
000051: 
000052: **From Kaggle:**
000053: 1. Create account at kaggle.com
000054: 2. Go to dataset page
000055: 3. Click "Download" button
000056: 4. Extract CSV/JSON files
000057: 
000058: ---
000059: 
000060: ### Source 2: Web Sources for Interview Data
000061: 
000062: #### Websites with Interview Q&A
000063: 
000064: | Website | Type of Content | How to Use |
000065: |---------|-----------------|------------|
000066: | **Glassdoor.com** | Real interview questions by company | Search company → Interviews tab |
000067: | **Indeed.com** | Interview questions by job title | Search job → Interview Questions |
000068: | **InterviewBit.com** | Technical interview Q&A | Browse by topic |
000069: | **LeetCode.com** | Coding interview problems | Discussions section |
000070: | **GeeksforGeeks.org** | Technical Q&A with explanations | Interview corner |
000071: | **Blind (TeamBlind.com)** | Real interview experiences | Search by company |
000072: 
000073: #### Manual Collection Process
000074: 1. Visit the website
000075: 2. Search for relevant job roles (e.g., "Software Engineer interview")
000076: 3. Copy questions and answers
000077: 4. Save in structured format (see below)
000078: 
000079: ---
000080: 
000081: ### Data Format for All Sources
000082: 
000083: Save all collected data in this standardized JSON format:
000084: 
000085: ```json
000086: {
000087:   "source": "glassdoor",
000088:   "collection_date": "2026-01-28",
000089:   "job_role": "Software Engineer",
000090:   "industry": "Technology",
000091:   "experience_level": "mid",
000092:   "conversation": [
000093:     {
000094:       "role": "interviewer",
000095:       "content": "Tell me about a time you faced a challenging technical problem."
000096:     },
000097:     {
000098:       "role": "candidate",
000099:       "content": "In my previous role, we faced a database scaling issue..."
000100:     },
000101:     {
000102:       "role": "interviewer", 
000103:       "content": "How did you approach solving it?"
000104:     },
000105:     {
000106:       "role": "candidate",
000107:       "content": "First, I analyzed the query patterns using our monitoring tools..."
000108:     }
000109:   ],
000110:   "metadata": {
000111:     "company": "Google",
000112:     "interview_type": "behavioral",
000113:     "quality_rating": 4
000114:   }
000115: }
000116: ```
000117: 
000118: ---
000119: 
000120: ### Source 3: Synthetic Data Generation
000121: 
000122: Use LLMs to generate additional training data:
000123: 
000124: ```python
000125: # Using Ollama (local) or OpenAI API
000126: prompt = """
000127: Generate a realistic job interview conversation for a {job_role} position.
000128: Include:
000129: - 5-7 interview questions (mix of behavioral and technical)
000130: - Realistic candidate responses
000131: - Follow-up questions from the interviewer
000132: 
000133: Format as a dialogue between INTERVIEWER and CANDIDATE.
000134: """
000135: ```
000136: 
000137: ---
000138: 
000139: ## Part 2: MediaPipe Video Data Collection
000140: 
000141: ### Overview
000142: To create a proper reference data library, you need:
000143: 1. **Reference Videos** - Record examples of correct posture/gestures
000144: 2. **Counter-Examples** - Record examples of incorrect posture/gestures
000145: 3. **Analysis** - Run MediaPipe on videos to extract numerical values
000146: 4. **Documentation** - Document what makes posture "correct" vs "incorrect"
000147: 
000148: ---
000149: 
000150: ### Video Recording Protocol
000151: 
000152: #### Equipment Needed
000153: - Webcam or smartphone camera (720p minimum, 1080p preferred)
000154: - Good lighting (face clearly visible)
000155: - Plain background
000156: - Stable camera position (tripod or fixed mount)
000157: 
000158: #### Recording Environment
000159: - Camera at eye level
000160: - Distance: 50-80cm from camera
000161: - Lighting from front (no backlighting)
000162: - Neutral background (no distractions)
000163: 
000164: ---
000165: 
000166: ### Posture Categories to Record
000167: 
000168: #### Category 1: Upper Body Posture
000169: 
000170: | Good Posture | Bad Posture |
000171: |--------------|-------------|
000172: | Shoulders level | One shoulder higher |
000173: | Back straight | Slouching forward |
000174: | Centered in frame | Leaning to one side |
000175: | Natural position | Tense/stiff |
000176: 
000177: **Recording Instructions:**
000178: 1. Record 30-60 seconds of GOOD posture (sitting straight, shoulders level)
000179: 2. Record 30-60 seconds of BAD posture (slouching, uneven shoulders)
000180: 3. Label files clearly: `posture_good_01.mp4`, `posture_bad_slouch_01.mp4`
000181: 
000182: #### Category 2: Head Position
000183: 
000184: | Good Position | Bad Position |
000185: |---------------|--------------|
000186: | Looking at camera | Looking down |
000187: | Level head | Head tilted |
000188: | Centered | Turned away |
000189: 
000190: **Recording Instructions:**
000191: 1. Record GOOD: Looking directly at camera, head level
000192: 2. Record BAD: Head tilted, looking down, looking away
000193: 3. Labels: `head_good_01.mp4`, `head_bad_tilted_01.mp4`
000194: 
000195: #### Category 3: Eye Contact
000196: 
000197: | Good Eye Contact | Poor Eye Contact |
000198: |------------------|------------------|
000199: | Looking at camera | Looking away frequently |
000200: | Natural blinking | Eyes closed/drowsy |
000201: | Engaged expression | Distracted |
000202: 
000203: **Recording Instructions:**
000204: 1. Record GOOD: Maintaining camera eye contact while speaking
000205: 2. Record BAD: Looking around, avoiding camera, excessive blinking
000206: 3. Labels: `eyes_good_contact_01.mp4`, `eyes_bad_avoiding_01.mp4`
000207: 
000208: #### Category 4: Hand Movements
000209: 
000210: | Appropriate | Inappropriate |
000211: |-------------|---------------|
000212: | Hands visible, calm | Fidgeting constantly |
000213: | Natural gestures | Touching face repeatedly |
000214: | Hands folded/relaxed | Drumming/tapping |
000215: 
000216: **Recording Instructions:**
000217: 1. Record GOOD: Hands visible, occasional natural gestures
000218: 2. Record BAD: Fidgeting, touching face, nervous movements
000219: 3. Labels: `hands_good_calm_01.mp4`, `hands_bad_fidgeting_01.mp4`
000220: 
000221: #### Category 5: Facial Expressions
000222: 
000223: | Professional | Unprofessional |
000224: |--------------|----------------|
000225: | Neutral/pleasant | Frowning |
000226: | Natural smile | Forced/fake smile |
000227: | Engaged | Bored/disinterested |
000228: 
000229: ---
000230: 
000231: ### Video File Naming Convention
000232: 
000233: ```
000234: {category}_{quality}_{description}_{number}.mp4
000235: 
000236: Examples:
000237: - posture_good_straight_01.mp4
000238: - posture_bad_slouching_01.mp4
000239: - head_good_level_01.mp4
000240: - head_bad_tilted_left_01.mp4
000241: - eyes_good_contact_01.mp4
000242: - eyes_bad_looking_down_01.mp4
000243: - hands_good_calm_01.mp4
000244: - hands_bad_fidgeting_01.mp4
000245: ```
000246: 
000247: ---
000248: 
000249: ### Folder Structure for Video Library
000250: 
000251: ```
000252: research-data/
000253: ├── videos/
000254: │   ├── posture/
000255: │   │   ├── good/
000256: │   │   │   ├── posture_good_straight_01.mp4
000257: │   │   │   └── posture_good_straight_02.mp4
000258: │   │   └── bad/
000259: │   │       ├── posture_bad_slouching_01.mp4
000260: │   │       └── posture_bad_leaning_01.mp4
000261: │   ├── head_position/
000262: │   │   ├── good/
000263: │   │   └── bad/
000264: │   ├── eye_contact/
000265: │   │   ├── good/
000266: │   │   └── bad/
000267: │   ├── hand_movement/
000268: │   │   ├── good/
000269: │   │   └── bad/
000270: │   └── facial_expression/
000271: │       ├── good/
000272: │       └── bad/
000273: ├── analysis_results/
000274: │   └── (MediaPipe output JSON files)
000275: └── metadata/
000276:     └── video_labels.json
000277: ```
000278: 
000279: ---
000280: 
000281: ### Minimum Video Requirements
000282: 
000283: | Category | Good Examples | Bad Examples | Total |
000284: |----------|---------------|--------------|-------|
000285: | Posture | 5 videos | 5 videos | 10 |
000286: | Head Position | 3 videos | 3 videos | 6 |
000287: | Eye Contact | 3 videos | 3 videos | 6 |
000288: | Hand Movement | 3 videos | 3 videos | 6 |
000289: | Facial Expression | 3 videos | 3 videos | 6 |
000290: | **Total** | **17 videos** | **17 videos** | **34** |
000291: 
000292: Each video: 30-60 seconds
000293: Total recording time: ~17-34 minutes
000294: 
000295: ---
000296: 
000297: ## Part 3: Analysis Tools
000298: 
000299: We have created tools in the system to:
000300: 1. **Record reference videos** directly from the application
000301: 2. **Analyze videos** using MediaPipe and extract metrics
000302: 3. **Compare** good vs bad posture metrics
000303: 4. **Generate reference values** based on analyzed videos
000304: 
000305: See the tools at:
000306: - `src/pages/research-tools/VideoRecorder.jsx`
000307: - `src/pages/research-tools/VideoAnalyzer.jsx`
000308: - `src/services/videoAnalysisService.js`
000309: 
000310: ---
000311: 
000312: ## Summary Checklist
000313: 
000314: ### LLM Data Collection
000315: - [ ] Download Anthropic/AnthropicInterviewer dataset from Hugging Face
000316: - [ ] Download ali-alkhars/interviews dataset from Hugging Face
000317: - [ ] Download Kaggle interview datasets
000318: - [ ] Manually collect 50+ Q&A pairs from Glassdoor/Indeed
000319: - [ ] Generate synthetic interview data using LLMs
000320: - [ ] Format all data in standardized JSON
000321: - [ ] Use Data Aggregation Tool to combine sources
000322: 
000323: ### MediaPipe Video Collection
000324: - [ ] Set up recording environment (lighting, camera, background)
000325: - [ ] Record 17+ "good" example videos across all categories
000326: - [ ] Record 17+ "bad" example videos across all categories
000327: - [ ] Organize videos in folder structure
000328: - [ ] Run Video Analyzer tool on all videos
000329: - [ ] Generate reference values from analysis
000330: - [ ] Document findings
000331: 
000332: ---
000333: 
000334: ## Next Steps
000335: 
000336: 1. Start with the easiest sources (downloading existing datasets)
000337: 2. Collect Q&A pairs from websites (Glassdoor, Indeed, etc.)
000338: 3. Generate synthetic data using LLMs if needed
000339: 4. Record your own reference videos for MediaPipe
000340: 5. Use the analysis tools to process videos
000341: 6. Compile all data for training
000342: 
```

000001: # Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Implementation
000002: 
000003: ## Overview
000004: This document describes the comprehensive frontend role-based access control implementation for RECRUITER and REVIEWER roles in the company organization system.
000005: 
000006: ## Implementation Date
000007: January 4, 2026
000008: 
000009: ## Roles Defined
000010: 
000011: ### 1. ADMIN
000012: - **Full Access**: Complete control over all features
000013: - **Permissions**:
000014:   - Manage organization settings and members
000015:   - Create, edit, and delete jobs
000016:   - Manage applications and update statuses
000017:   - Send interview invitations
000018:   - Create and manage templates
000019:   - View analytics and export reports
000020:   - Start candidate reviews
000021: 
000022: ### 2. RECRUITER
000023: - **Hiring Management**: Full access to hiring workflow
000024: - **Permissions**:
000025:   - Create, edit, and delete jobs
000026:   - Manage applications and update statuses
000027:   - Send interview invitations
000028:   - Create and manage templates
000029:   - View analytics and export reports
000030:   - Start candidate reviews
000031: - **Restrictions**:
000032:   - Cannot manage organization settings or members

000034: ### 3. REVIEWER

000145: ## Permission Matrix
000146: 
000147: | Feature | ADMIN | RECRUITER | REVIEWER |
000148: |---------|-------|-----------|----------|
000149: | **Navigation** |
000150: | Dashboard | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000151: | Jobs | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000152: | Applications | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Read-only) |
000153: | Invitations | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000154: | Interviews | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Read-only) |
000155: | Candidates | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Read-only) |
000156: | Analytics | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000157: | **Dashboard Components** |
000158: | Overview Panel | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000159: | Candidate Pipeline | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000160: | Hiring Metrics | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000161: | Quick Actions | ✅ (All) | ✅ (Most) | ✅ (Limited) |
000162: | Reviewer Panel | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000163: | Organization Admin | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
000164: | **Job Management** |
000165: | Create Jobs | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000166: | Edit Jobs | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000167: | Delete Jobs | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000168: | View Jobs | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000169: | Publish/Archive | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000170: | **Application Management** |
000171: | View Applications | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000172: | Update Status | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000173: | Start Review | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000174: | **Interview Management** |
000175: | Send Invitations | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000176: | View Interviews | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000177: | Submit Reviews | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
000178: | **Templates** |
000179: | Create Templates | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000180: | Edit Templates | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000181: | View Templates | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
000182: | **Analytics** |
000183: | View Analytics | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |

000185: | **Organization** |
000186: | Manage Settings | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
000187: | Manage Members | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
000188: | Add/Remove Roles | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
000189: 
000190: ## Backend Enforcement
000191: 
000192: The backend already has complete role-based access control:
000193: 
000194: ### Middleware
000195: - `requireOrgRole(['ADMIN', 'RECRUITER'])` - Enforces role requirements
000196: - Applied to all protected routes
000197: 
000198: ### Routes with Role Enforcement
000199: - **Jobs**: `['ADMIN', 'RECRUITER']` for create/update/delete
000200: - **Applications**: `['ADMIN', 'RECRUITER']` for status updates
000201: - **Invitations**: `['ADMIN', 'RECRUITER']` for sending
000202: - **Templates**: `['ADMIN', 'RECRUITER']` for create/update/delete
000203: - **Reviews**: `['ADMIN', 'RECRUITER', 'REVIEWER']` for submit/view
000204: 
000205: ## User Experience
000206: 
000207: ### For ADMIN Users
000208: - Full access to all features
000209: - "Administrator" badge displayed in header
000210: - Purple-to-pink gradient badge color
000211: - Can manage organization and all hiring workflows
000212: 
000213: ### For RECRUITER Users
000214: - Full hiring workflow access
000215: - "Recruiter" badge displayed in header
000216: - Blue-to-purple gradient badge color
000217: - Cannot access organization settings
000218: - Focused on job and candidate management
000219: 
000220: ### For REVIEWER Users
000221: - Read-only access to applications, interviews, and candidates
000222: - "Reviewer" badge displayed in header
000223: - Emerald-to-teal gradient badge color
000224: - Can submit interview reviews
000225: - Simplified navigation (only Dashboard, Applications, Interviews, Candidates)
000226: - "View-only access" messages where appropriate
000227: - Status badges shown instead of status update buttons
000228: 
000229: ## Testing Recommendations
000230: 
000231: ### Test Scenario 1: ADMIN Role
000232: 1. Login as ADMIN user
000233: 2. Verify all navigation items are visible
000234: 3. Verify all dashboard components are visible
000235: 4. Verify can create/edit/delete jobs
000236: 5. Verify can update application statuses
000237: 6. Verify can send invitations
000238: 7. Verify can access analytics
000239: 8. Verify can manage organization settings
000240: 
000241: ### Test Scenario 2: RECRUITER Role
000242: 1. Login as RECRUITER user
000243: 2. Verify navigation excludes organization admin features
000244: 3. Verify can create/edit/delete jobs
000245: 4. Verify can update application statuses
000246: 5. Verify can send invitations
000247: 6. Verify can access analytics
000248: 7. Verify CANNOT access organization settings
000249: 8. Verify "Recruiter" badge is displayed
000250: 
000251: ### Test Scenario 3: REVIEWER Role
000252: 1. Login as REVIEWER user
000253: 2. Verify limited navigation (Dashboard, Applications, Interviews, Candidates only)
000254: 3. Verify CANNOT access Jobs page
000255: 4. Verify CANNOT access Invitations page
000256: 5. Verify CANNOT access Analytics page
000257: 6. Verify can VIEW applications but cannot update status
000258: 7. Verify can VIEW candidates but cannot start review
000259: 8. Verify can submit interview reviews
000260: 9. Verify "Reviewer" badge is displayed
000261: 10. Verify "View-only access" messages are shown
000262: 
000263: ### Test Scenario 4: Role-Based Redirects
000264: 1. As REVIEWER, try to navigate to `/company-invitations`
000265: 2. Verify automatic redirect to dashboard
000266: 3. As REVIEWER, try to navigate to `/company-analytics`
000267: 4. Verify page is not accessible (filtered from navigation)
000268: 
000269: ## Security Notes
000270: 
000271: 1. **Frontend + Backend**: Role enforcement exists on BOTH frontend (UI) and backend (API)
000272: 2. **Defense in Depth**: Even if a user bypasses frontend restrictions, backend will block unauthorized actions
000273: 3. **No Security Through Obscurity**: Hiding UI elements is for UX, not security
000274: 4. **API Always Validates**: Every API endpoint checks user role before processing
000275: 
000276: ## Future Enhancements
000277: 
000278: Potential improvements for future iterations:
000279: 
000280: 1. **Granular Permissions**: Move from role-based to permission-based for more flexibility
000281: 2. **Custom Roles**: Allow organizations to define custom roles with specific permissions
000282: 3. **Permission Inheritance**: Create role hierarchies with inherited permissions
000283: 4. **Audit Logging**: Track role changes and permission-based actions
000284: 5. **Role Switching**: Allow users with multiple roles to switch contexts
000285: 6. **Temporary Permissions**: Grant time-limited elevated permissions
000286: 
000287: ## Conclusion
000288: 
000289: This implementation provides a comprehensive, user-friendly role-based access control system that:
000290: - ✅ Clearly defines three distinct roles (ADMIN, RECRUITER, REVIEWER)
000291: - ✅ Enforces permissions at both frontend and backend levels
000292: - ✅ Provides visual feedback (role badges, disabled states, messages)
000293: - ✅ Maintains security while optimizing user experience
000294: - ✅ Is maintainable and extensible for future enhancements
000295: - ✅ Has zero linter errors
000296: - ✅ Follows React best practices (hooks, memoization, conditional rendering)
000297: 
000298: All code is production-ready and fully functional.
000299: 
000300:

000001: # Role Capability Audit & Delivery Plan
000002: 
000003: ## Context
000004: - Target experience covers **five human actors** (Individual Candidate, Job Applicant, Organisation Admin, Recruiter/HR, Hiring Manager) plus the **AI interviewer assistant**.
000005: - The current stack only distinguishes between `CANDIDATE` and `COMPANY` accounts, so most of the required workflows either do not exist or stop at UI placeholders.
000006: 
000007: ## Current Implementation Snapshot
000008: 
000009: ### Account types & auth
000010: - Registration hard-codes the `accountType` to `CANDIDATE` or `COMPANY`, and persists role-specific profile fields (skills vs. company metadata).
000011: 
000012: ```47:58:server/src/controllers/auth.controller.js
000013:       const accountTypeEnum = (accountType || '').toUpperCase() === 'COMPANY' ? 'COMPANY' : 'CANDIDATE';
000014: 
000015:       const user = await userStore.create(firebaseUid, {
000016:         email,
000017:         accountType: accountTypeEnum,
000018:         fullName,
000019:         experienceLevel: accountTypeEnum === 'CANDIDATE' ? experienceLevel || null : null,
000020:         skills: accountTypeEnum === 'CANDIDATE' ? (skills || []) : [],
000021:         companyName: accountTypeEnum === 'COMPANY' ? companyName || null : null,
000022:         companySize: accountTypeEnum === 'COMPANY' ? companySize || null : null,
000023:         industry: accountTypeEnum === 'COMPANY' ? industry || null : null,
000024:       });
000025: ```
000026: 
000027: - Frontend route protection mirrors the same two account types; no finer-grained permissions exist.
000028: 
000029: ```26:38:src/components/ProtectedRoute.jsx

000031:     const normalizedRole = user.accountType?.toUpperCase();

000143: ## Actor-by-Actor Status
000144: 
000145: | Actor / Need | Status | Notes |
000146: |--------------|--------|-------|
000147: | **Individual Candidate (Learner)** | **Mostly implemented** for practice flows (setup, live session, analytics). | Covered by `PracticeInterviewSetup`, `LiveInterviewSession`, `apiClient.interviews`. Missing job discovery, applications, and company-invite handoffs. |
000148: | **Job Applicant (Invited Candidate)** | **Missing** | No invitation links, tokens, or ability to join `HIRING` interviews without an existing account. |
000149: | **Organisation Admin (HR / Talent Lead)** | **Missing** | No organisation entity, billing, data policies, or member management. All company users are identical. |
000150: | **Recruiter / HR Officer** | **UI-only** | Dashboards show static data; there is no CRUD for job profiles, interview templates, invitations, or candidate pipeline transitions. |
000151: | **Hiring Manager / Interview Reviewer** | **Missing** | No reviewer permissions, scoring UI, commenting, or approval workflows beyond the placeholder table. |
000152: 
000153: ## Gap Categories
000154: 
000155: 1. **Role & permission model** – need organisation membership + granular roles (admin, recruiter, reviewer) instead of the current binary accountType.
000156: 2. **Job data & invitations** – need collections for jobs, stages, templates, invitations, applicant submissions, and statuses.
000157: 3. **Recruiter tooling** – job posting CRUD, template designer, invitation sender, pipeline Kanban tied to real data, dashboards with filters.
000158: 4. **Hiring manager workflow** – review portal with interview playback, AI rubric scoring, comments, decision logging, notifications.
000159: 5. **Candidate job experience** – job browsing/applications, invite entry points, status tracking separate from practice coaching.
000160: 
000161: ## Implementation Plan
000162: 
000163: ### Phase 1 – Domain & Auth Foundation
000164: 1. **Create organisation + membership collections** (e.g., `organizations`, `organizationMembers` with roles: `ADMIN`, `RECRUITER`, `REVIEWER`). ✅ Implemented via Firestore-backed stores and new controller/routes.
000165: 2. **Extend user profile** to include `primaryOrganizationId`, `memberRole`, and feature flags. ✅ User records now persist `primaryOrganizationId` plus `organizationRoles`.
000166: 3. **Introduce role-aware middleware** (`requireOrgRole('ADMIN')`, etc.) and update frontend `ProtectedRoute` to read org roles from context. ✅ Middleware stack attaches org context; `AuthContext` exposes `organizationContext`, `organizationRole`, and `isOrgAdmin`.
000167: 4. **Migrate company registration** so the first company user provisions an organisation + admin membership rather than a generic `COMPANY` record. ✅ Registration auto-creates an organization, admin membership, and returns org context.
000168: 
000169: ### Phase 2 – Job Data & Candidate Entry
000170: 1. **Jobs service/model** with fields for title, department, requisition id, stages, assigned recruiters, scoring templates. ✅ Backed by `jobStore` with CRUD APIs and organization-scoped routes.
000171: 2. **Interview templates** persisted alongside jobs; API endpoints to CRUD questions, timers, AI scoring rules. ✅ Template config captured in each job (interview types, duration, rubric metadata) and exposed via API.
000172: 3. **Invitation model** (token, jobId, stage, expiry, candidate email). Public endpoints for invite acceptance + temporary accounts. ✅ Invitation store + controller with org creation, public preview, and authenticated acceptance.
000173: 4. **Candidate job hub** on the frontend: browse published jobs, apply (resume upload, questionnaire), track status, handle invite deep-links. ✅ New `/jobs` page lists published roles; `/invite?token=` page lets candidates review and accept invites (application form still TODO in later phases).

000191:    - Post-interview status + feedback page tied to the job pipeline rather than practice analytics. _TODO_
000192: 
000193: ### Phase 4 – Glue & Quality

000195: 2. **Documentation & onboarding** – publish guides that explain each role and how data flows across the system. ✅ This document now reflects Phase 4 completion, serving as the canonical onboarding reference for every role.

000001: # Security Implementation Guide
000002: 
000003: This document describes the security measures implemented in the InterviewAI Pro application following OWASP best practices.
000004: 
000005: ## Table of Contents
000006: 
000007: 1. [Rate Limiting](#rate-limiting)
000008: 2. [Input Validation and Sanitization](#input-validation-and-sanitization)
000009: 3. [API Key Management](#api-key-management)
000010: 4. [HTTP Security Headers](#http-security-headers)
000011: 5. [Security Monitoring](#security-monitoring)
000012: 
000013: ---
000014: 
000015: ## Rate Limiting
000016: 
000017: ### Overview
000018: 
000019: Rate limiting is implemented using `express-rate-limit` with endpoint-specific configurations to prevent abuse and protect against denial-of-service attacks.
000020: 
000021: ### Configuration
000022: 
000023: Rate limits are defined in `server/src/middleware/rateLimiter.middleware.js`:
000024: 
000025: | Endpoint Type | Window | Max Requests | Notes |
000026: |--------------|--------|--------------|-------|
000027: | General API | 15 min | 100 | Baseline for all API endpoints |
000028: | Authentication (Login) | 15 min | 10 | Stricter limit, skips successful requests |
000029: | Registration | 1 hour | 5 | Prevents mass account creation |
000030: | Email Check | 1 min | 10 | Prevents email enumeration |
000031: | Email Verification | 1 hour | 5 | Prevents verification abuse |
000032: | Interview Creation | 1 hour | 10 | Prevents resource abuse |
000033: | Public Endpoints | 15 min | 200 | Higher limit for read-only |
000034: | Newsletter | 1 hour | 3 | Prevents subscription spam |
000035: | Contact Form | 1 hour | 5 | Prevents spam messages |
000036: | File Upload | 15 min | 20 | Prevents upload abuse |
000037: | Admin Bootstrap | 24 hours | 3 | Very strict for one-time setup |
000038: | Team Invitations | 1 hour | 20 | Prevents invitation spam |
000039: | Job Applications | 1 hour | 10 | Prevents application spam |
000040: 
000041: ### 429 Response Format
000042: 
000043: All rate limit responses follow this format:
000044: 
000045: ```json
000046: {
000047:   "success": false,
000048:   "error": "Too many requests. Please try again later.",
000049:   "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
000050:   "retryAfter": 900,
000051:   "retryAfterMs": 900000
000052: }
000053: ```
000054: 
000055: The `Retry-After` header is also set for HTTP compliance.
000056: 
000057: ---
000058: 
000059: ## Input Validation and Sanitization
000060: 
000061: ### Overview
000062: 
000063: Input validation is implemented in `server/src/middleware/inputValidation.middleware.js` using `express-validator` with schema-based validation.
000064: 
000065: ### Validation Features
000066: 
000067: 1. **Type Checking**: All inputs are validated for correct types
000068: 2. **Length Limits**: String inputs have maximum length limits
000069: 3. **Pattern Validation**: Regex patterns for emails, phones, URLs, etc.
000070: 4. **Enum Validation**: Whitelist of allowed values for enums
000071: 5. **Sanitization**: HTML escaping to prevent XSS attacks
000072: 6. **Field Whitelisting**: Unexpected fields are stripped from requests
000073: 
000074: ### Length Limits
000075: 
000076: | Field Type | Max Length |
000077: |------------|------------|
000078: | Name | 100 |
000079: | Email | 254 |
000080: | Phone | 20 |
000081: | Short Text | 100 |
000082: | Medium Text | 500 |
000083: | Long Text | 2,000 |
000084: | Very Long Text | 5,000 |
000085: | URL | 2,083 |
000086: | ID | 128 |
000087: | Token | 512 |
000088: 
000089: ### Usage Example
000090: 
000091: ```javascript
000092: import { 
000093:   validateRequest, 
000094:   stripUnexpectedFields,
000095:   validationSchemas,
000096: } from '../middleware/inputValidation.middleware.js';
000097: 
000098: router.post(
000099:   '/contact',
000100:   stripUnexpectedFields(validationSchemas.contact.submit.allowedFields),
000101:   validationSchemas.contact.submit.validators,
000102:   validateRequest,
000103:   ContactController.submit,
000104: );
000105: ```
000106: 
000107: ### Validation Error Response
000108: 
000109: ```json
000110: {
000111:   "success": false,
000112:   "error": "Validation failed",
000113:   "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
000114:   "errors": [
000115:     {
000116:       "field": "email",
000117:       "message": "Valid email address is required"
000118:     }
000119:   ]
000120: }
000121: ```
000122: 
000123: ---
000124: 
000125: ## API Key Management
000126: 
000127: ### Overview
000128: 
000129: Secure configuration is managed in `server/src/config/secureConfig.js` with environment variable validation.
000130: 
000131: ### Required Environment Variables
000132: 
000133: | Variable | Service | Sensitive |
000134: |----------|---------|-----------|
000135: | FIREBASE_DATABASE_URL | Firebase | No |
000136: | FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT | Firebase | Yes |
000137: | EMAIL_VERIFICATION_CODE_SECRET | Auth | Yes |
000138: 
000139: ### Optional Environment Variables
000140: 
000141: | Variable | Service | When Required |
000142: |----------|---------|---------------|
000143: | SENDGRID_API_KEY | Email | When EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid |
000144: | SMTP_PASS | Email | When EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp |
000145: | SIGHTENGINE_USER/SECRET | Moderation | For image moderation |
000146: 
000147: ### Key Rotation Guidelines
000148: 
000149: 1. **Firebase Service Account**
000150:    - Rotate in Firebase Console > Project Settings > Service Accounts
000151:    - Generate new private key, update environment, revoke old key
000152: 
000153: 2. **SendGrid API Key**
000154:    - Generate new key in SendGrid Dashboard > Settings > API Keys
000155:    - Update environment variable
000156:    - Revoke old key after confirming new key works
000157: 
000158: 3. **SMTP Password (Gmail)**
000159:    - Generate new App Password at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords
000160:    - Update environment variable
000161: 
000162: ### Best Practices
000163: 
000164: - Never commit secrets to version control
000165: - Use different secrets for development, staging, and production
000166: - Rotate keys every 90 days
000167: - Use strong, randomly generated secrets: `openssl rand -base64 32`
000168: 
000169: ---
000170: 
000171: ## HTTP Security Headers
000172: 
000173: ### Overview
000174: 
000175: Security headers are configured using Helmet in `server/src/middleware/security.middleware.js`.
000176: 
000177: ### Headers Applied
000178: 
000179: | Header | Value | Purpose |
000180: |--------|-------|---------|
000181: | Content-Security-Policy | Restrictive policy | Prevents XSS |
000182: | X-Frame-Options | DENY | Prevents clickjacking |
000183: | X-Content-Type-Options | nosniff | Prevents MIME sniffing |
000184: | X-XSS-Protection | 1; mode=block | XSS filter |
000185: | Strict-Transport-Security | max-age=31536000 | Forces HTTPS |
000186: | Referrer-Policy | strict-origin-when-cross-origin | Limits referrer info |
000187: | X-Download-Options | noopen | IE security |
000188: | X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies | none | Flash/PDF policy |
000189: 
000190: ### CORS Configuration
000191: 
000192: - Only configured frontend URL is allowed
000193: - Credentials are allowed
000194: - Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
000195: - Rate limit headers are exposed
000196: 
000197: ---
000198: 
000199: ## Security Monitoring
000200: 
000201: ### Logging
000202: 
000203: Security events are logged with Winston:
000204: 
000205: 1. **Rate Limit Violations**: IP, path, method, user ID
000206: 2. **Validation Failures**: Path, method, IP, failed fields
000207: 3. **Suspicious Requests**: Pattern matches for attacks
000208: 
000209: ### Suspicious Pattern Detection
000210: 
000211: The following patterns are monitored:
000212: 
000213: - Path traversal: `../`
000214: - XSS attempts: `<script`, `javascript:`, event handlers
000215: - SQL injection: `union.*select`, `'.*or.*'`
000216: 
000217: ### Audit Trail
000218: 
000219: For admin operations, the following are logged:
000220: - Organization approval/rejection
000221: - System settings changes
000222: - User management actions
000223: 
000224: ---

000001: # Quick Fix: SendGrid Sender Verification
000002: 
000003: ## The Problem
000004: SendGrid is rejecting emails because `noreply@interviewai.pro` is not verified.
000005: 
000006: **Error**: "The from address does not match a verified Sender Identity"
000007: 
000008: ## Solution: Verify Your Sender Email
000009: 
000010: You have two options:
000011: 
000012: ### Option 1: Use Your Real Email (Easiest - Recommended)
000013: 
000014: 1. **Use the email address you used to sign up for SendGrid** (or any email you own)
000015: 
000016: 2. **Update your `.env` file**:
000017:    ```env
000018:    FROM_EMAIL=your-actual-email@gmail.com
000019:    FROM_NAME=InterviewAI Pro
000020:    ```
000021: 
000022: 3. **Verify it in SendGrid**:
000023:    - Go to [SendGrid Dashboard](https://app.sendgrid.com)
000024:    - Click **Settings** → **Sender Authentication**
000025:    - Click **"Verify a Single Sender"**
000026:    - Enter your email address
000027:    - Fill in the form (name, company, address, etc.)
000028:    - Click **"Create"**
000029:    - Check your email inbox and click the verification link
000030:    - Wait for verification (usually instant)
000031: 
000032: 4. **Restart your server**
000033: 
000034: 5. **Test again** - emails should now send!
000035: 
000036: ### Option 2: Use Domain Authentication (If You Own interviewai.pro)
000037: 
000038: If you actually own the `interviewai.pro` domain:
000039: 
000040: 1. Go to SendGrid Dashboard → **Settings** → **Sender Authentication**
000041: 2. Click **"Authenticate Your Domain"**
000042: 3. Follow the DNS setup instructions
000043: 4. This takes longer but allows you to use any email from that domain
000044: 
000045: ## Quick Steps (Option 1 - Recommended)
000046: 
000047: 1. **Find your email** - Use the email you signed up for SendGrid with, or any Gmail/Outlook you own
000048: 
000049: 2. **Update `.env`**:
000050:    ```env
000051:    FROM_EMAIL=your-email@gmail.com
000052:    ```
000053: 
000054: 3. **Verify in SendGrid**:
000055:    - Dashboard → Settings → Sender Authentication
000056:    - Verify a Single Sender
000057:    - Enter your email
000058:    - Complete the form
000059:    - Verify via email link
000060: 
000061: 4. **Restart server**
000062: 
000063: 5. **Done!** ✅
000064: 
000065: ## Why This Happens
000066: 
000067: SendGrid requires sender verification to prevent spam. You must verify:
000068: - Either a single email address (quick, easy)
000069: - Or your entire domain (more complex, but more flexible)
000070: 
000071: For development/testing, verifying a single sender is the fastest solution.
000072: 
000073: 
```

000001: # SME Calibration Workflow
000002: 
000003: ## Overview
000004: 
000005: This document describes the SME (Subject Matter Expert) calibration workflow implemented to satisfy **FR8** and the contextual report: comparison of AI scores with SME ratings, calibration, and override mechanisms.
000006: 
000007: ## Features
000008: 
000009: 1. **Comparison of AI vs SME scores** – Side-by-side view of AI evaluation and SME (reviewer) ratings.
000010: 2. **Override semantics** – SME can choose to use their overall score as the final score (override AI).
000011: 3. **Traceability** – Each review stores AI overall score at review time, SME overall score, and override flag.
000012: 4. **Final score** – Interview document has `finalOverallScore` and `finalScoreSource` ('AI' | 'SME').
000013: 
000014: ## Data Model
000015: 
000016: ### Interview (Firestore `interviews`)
000017: 
000018: - **existing:** `overallScore`, `evaluation`, `readinessLevel`
000019: - **added:** `finalOverallScore` (number, when SME override used), `finalScoreSource` ('AI' | 'SME')
000020: 
000021: When no SME override exists, downstream code should use `overallScore` as the effective score. When `finalScoreSource === 'SME'`, use `finalOverallScore`.
000022: 
000023: ### Review (Firestore `interviewReviews`)
000024: 
000025: - **existing:** `interviewId`, `reviewerId`, `reviewerRole`, `score`, `decision`, `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `notes`
000026: - **added for calibration:**
000027:   - `rating` (0–10, SME overall)
000028:   - `technicalScore`, `communicationScore`, `problemSolvingScore`, `culturalFitScore` (0–10 each)
000029:   - `recommendation` (STRONG_YES, YES, MAYBE, NO, STRONG_NO, UNDECIDED)
000030:   - `aiOverallScoreAtReview` (snapshot of interview.overallScore when review was submitted)
000031:   - `smeOverallScore` (0–100, derived from rating or category average)
000032:   - `overrideOverall` (boolean – use SME score as final)
000033: 
000034: ## API
000035: 
000036: ### GET `/api/reviews/:interviewId/me`
000037: 
000038: Returns the current user's review for the interview (single review or `{ success: true, review: null }`).
000039: 
000040: ### POST `/api/reviews/:interviewId`
000041: 
000042: Submit or update review. Body can include:
000043: 
000044: - `rating`, `technicalScore`, `communicationScore`, `problemSolvingScore`, `culturalFitScore` (0–10)
000045: - `notes`, `recommendation`
000046: - `overrideOverall` (boolean)
000047: 
000048: When `overrideOverall === true` and `smeOverallScore` is present, the backend updates the interview with `finalOverallScore` and `finalScoreSource: 'SME'`.
000049: 
000050: ## Frontend
000051: 
000052: - **Company Dashboard → Interview Review** (`InterviewReviewEnhanced.jsx`):
000053:   - **AI vs SME** tab: side-by-side AI evaluation vs SME review scores and agreement (difference in overall score).
000054:   - **AI Evaluation** tab: rubric-tied explainability — Technical Skills, Communication Skills, Problem Solving, Cultural Fit (score + feedback per criterion), plus Strengths, Areas for Improvement, Recommendations, and Detailed Feedback. Raw JSON is available in a collapsible section.
000055:   - **My Review** tab: category scores, recommendation, notes, and **Use my overall score as the final score (override AI)** checkbox.
000056:   - Info bar shows **Final Score** and “SME override” when applicable.
000057: - **apiClient:** `getReviewForInterview(interviewId)`, `submitReview({ interviewId, ...payload })` including `overrideOverall`.
000058: 
000059: ## Backward compatibility
000060: 
000061: - Existing reviews (no calibration fields) still load; missing fields default to 0 or null.
000062: - `ReviewerPanel` and other callers that use `reviews.submit(interviewId, { score, decision, notes })` continue to work; new fields are optional.
000063: - Interviews without `finalOverallScore` / `finalScoreSource` behave as before (effective score = `overallScore`).
000064: 
000065: ---
000066: 
000067: *Implemented: January 2026. Aligns with FR8 and contextual report Section 2.7.3 (calibration of SMEs, review and override mechanisms).*
000068: 
```

000001: # Supervisor Tasks Implementation - January 2026

000020: ---
000021: 
000022: ## Task 1: LLM Interview Dataset Collection
000023: 
000024: ### What Was Implemented
000025: 
000026: A complete system for collecting, storing, and exporting interview conversation data for LLM fine-tuning.

000078: 
000079: ## Task 2: MediaPipe Face-Mesh and Posture Data Library
000080: 
000081: ### What Was Implemented
000082: 
000083: A comprehensive reference data library with ideal posture and facial landmark values, plus detection hooks that compare real-time data against these references.
000084: 
000085: ### Files Created
000086: 
000087: | File | Purpose |
000088: |------|---------|
000089: | `src/config/mediapipeReferenceData.js` | Reference values for ideal posture and face-mesh |
000090: | `src/hooks/useFaceMeshDetection.js` | Face-mesh detection hook (468 landmarks) |
000091: | `src/hooks/useInterviewAnalytics.js` | Combined pose + face detection with scoring |
000092: | `src/components/ui/InterviewAnalyticsPanel.jsx` | Enhanced UI showing all metrics |
000093: 
000094: ### Reference Data Library Contents
000095: 
000096: #### 1. Pose Landmarks (33 points)
000097: ```javascript
000098: POSE_LANDMARKS = {
000099:   NOSE: 0,
000100:   LEFT_SHOULDER: 11,
000101:   RIGHT_SHOULDER: 12,
000102:   LEFT_HIP: 23,
000103:   RIGHT_HIP: 24,
000104:   // ... all 33 landmarks
000105: }
000106: ```
000107: 
000108: #### 2. Face-Mesh Landmarks (478 points)
000109: ```javascript
000110: FACE_LANDMARKS = {
000111:   LEFT_EYE: [263, 249, 390, ...], // 16 points
000112:   RIGHT_EYE: [33, 7, 163, ...],   // 16 points
000113:   LEFT_IRIS: [474, 475, 476, 477],
000114:   RIGHT_IRIS: [469, 470, 471, 472],
000115:   LIPS_OUTER: [...],              // 20 points
000116:   // ... all 478 landmarks
000117: }
000118: ```
000119: 
000120: #### 3. Ideal Posture Values
000121: ```javascript
000122: POSTURE_REFERENCE = {
000123:   shoulder: {
000124:     maxSlopeThreshold: 0.03,      // Good posture
000125:     moderateSlopeThreshold: 0.06, // Acceptable
000126:     poorSlopeThreshold: 0.10,     // Needs improvement
000127:   },
000128:   spine: {
000129:     maxForwardHeadThreshold: 0.05,
000130:     // ...
000131:   },
000132:   head: {
000133:     maxTiltThreshold: 0.025,
000134:     // ...
000135:   },
000136:   hands: {
000137:     fidgetingThreshold: 0.05,
000138:     // ...
000139:   }
000140: }
000141: ```
000142: 
000143: #### 4. Ideal Face Values
000144: ```javascript
000145: FACE_REFERENCE = {
000146:   eyes: {
000147:     openEyeEARMin: 0.20,     // Eye Aspect Ratio
000148:     blinkThreshold: 0.18,
000149:     // ...
000150:   },
000151:   orientation: {
000152:     maxYawThreshold: 15,     // degrees
000153:     maxPitchThreshold: 10,
000154:     maxRollThreshold: 10,
000155:     // ...
000156:   }
000157: }
000158: ```
000159: 
000160: #### 5. Scoring Weights
000161: ```javascript
000162: SCORING_WEIGHTS = {
000163:   posture: { weight: 0.30 },     // 30% of overall score
000164:   attention: { weight: 0.40 },   // 40% of overall score
000165:   bodyLanguage: { weight: 0.20 }, // 20% of overall score
000166:   expression: { weight: 0.10 },   // 10% of overall score
000167: }
000168: ```
000169: 
000170: ### Metrics Calculated
000171: 
000172: | Category | Metrics |
000173: |----------|---------|
000174: | **Posture** | Shoulder alignment, spine alignment, head position, slouching detection |
000175: | **Eye Contact** | Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), blink count, attention score |
000176: | **Face Orientation** | Yaw (left/right), Pitch (up/down), Roll (tilt) |
000177: | **Body Language** | Fidgeting detection, hand movement, overall stability |
000178: | **Expression** | Eyebrow position (neutral/raised/furrowed) |
000179: 
000180: ### How the Comparison Works
000181: 
000182: 1. **Real-time Detection**: Every 100ms, the system captures pose and face landmarks
000183: 2. **Reference Comparison**: Each metric is compared against ideal values
000184: 3. **Score Calculation**: Weighted scores are calculated
000185: 4. **Feedback Generation**: Contextual feedback messages are generated
000186: 
000187: ```javascript
000188: // Example: Shoulder alignment scoring
000189: if (shoulderSlope > POSTURE_REFERENCE.shoulder.poorSlopeThreshold) {
000190:   shoulderScore = 40;
000191:   shoulderStatus = 'poor';
000192: } else if (shoulderSlope > POSTURE_REFERENCE.shoulder.moderateSlopeThreshold) {
000193:   shoulderScore = 70;
000194:   shoulderStatus = 'fair';
000195: }
000196: ```
000197:

000001: # Verify Your Email in SendGrid - Step by Step
000002: 
000003: ## Current Issue
000004: Your `.env` file is set to use `akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com`, but:
000005: 1. This email needs to be verified in SendGrid first
000006: 2. Your server needs to be restarted to pick up the new .env value
000007: 
000008: ## Steps to Fix (Do This Now)
000009: 
000010: ### Step 1: Verify Email in SendGrid (5 minutes)
000011: 
000012: 1. **Go to SendGrid Dashboard**:
000013:    - Open: https://app.sendgrid.com
000014:    - Log in with your SendGrid account
000015: 
000016: 2. **Navigate to Sender Authentication**:
000017:    - Click **"Settings"** in the left sidebar
000018:    - Click **"Sender Authentication"**
000019: 
000020: 3. **Verify Single Sender**:
000021:    - Click the **"Verify a Single Sender"** button
000022:    - Fill in the form:
000023:      - **From Email**: `akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com`
000024:      - **From Name**: `InterviewAI Pro`
000025:      - **Reply To**: `akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com` (same as from email)
000026:      - **Company**: Your company name (e.g., "InterviewAI Pro")
000027:      - **Address**: Your address
000028:      - **City**: Your city
000029:      - **State**: Your state
000030:      - **Zip**: Your zip code
000031:      - **Country**: Your country
000032:    - Click **"Create"**
000033: 
000034: 4. **Check Your Email**:
000035:    - Go to your Gmail inbox for `akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com`
000036:    - Look for an email from SendGrid
000037:    - Click the verification link in the email
000038:    - You should see "Sender Verified" confirmation
000039: 
000040: ### Step 2: Restart Your Server
000041: 
000042: After verifying the email, restart your server:
000043: 
000044: ```bash
000045: # Stop your current server (Ctrl+C)
000046: # Then restart it:
000047: cd server
000048: npm run dev
000049: ```
000050: 
000051: ### Step 3: Test Again
000052: 
000053: 1. Go to your admin dashboard
000054: 2. Reject an organization
000055: 3. Check server logs - you should see:
000056:    ```
000057:    ✅ Email sent via SendGrid to user@example.com - Status: 202
000058:    ```
000059: 4. Check the recipient's email inbox
000060: 
000061: ## Verification Checklist
000062: 
000063: - [ ] Email `akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com` is verified in SendGrid
000064: - [ ] Server has been restarted after .env change
000065: - [ ] Server logs show "✅ SendGrid API key initialized successfully" on startup
000066: - [ ] Test rejection shows success in logs
000067: 
000068: ## If You Still Get Errors
000069: 
000070: 1. **Check SendGrid Dashboard**:
000071:    - Go to Settings → Sender Authentication
000072:    - Make sure `akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com` shows as "Verified" (green checkmark)
000073: 
000074: 2. **Check Server Logs**:
000075:    - Look for the FROM_EMAIL being used
000076:    - Should show: `📤 SendGrid: Preparing to send email from akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com`
000077: 
000078: 3. **Double-check .env**:
000079:    - Make sure `FROM_EMAIL=akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com` (no typos)
000080:    - Make sure there are no extra spaces
000081: 
000082: 4. **Wait a few minutes**:
000083:    - Sometimes SendGrid verification takes a minute to propagate
000084: 
000085: ## Quick Test
000086: 
000087: After verification and restart, the logs should show:
000088: ```
000089: 📤 SendGrid: Preparing to send email from akiyoshiyapa@gmail.com to user@example.com
000090: ✅ Email sent via SendGrid to user@example.com - Status: 202
000091: ✅ Rejection email sent successfully to user@example.com
000092: ```
000093: 
000094: If you see this, it's working! 🎉
000095: 
000096:

### 13.2.59 `README.md`

```text
000001: # 🤖 InterviewAI Pro
000002: 
000003: AI-first mock interview coach that blends live video practice, real‑time analytics, and personalized study plans into a single experience. The platform pairs a React/Vite front-end with an Express/Firebase backend, plus local LLM + Whisper pipelines for zero-cost coaching.
000004: 
000005: ---
000006: 
000007: ## ✨ Highlights
000008: 
000009: - **Candidate + Company Dashboards** – Personalized insights, progress tracking, and quick actions for both sides of the hiring loop.
000010: - **Live AI Interview Session** – Real-time question flow, pose analysis, interviewer chat, and feedback panel.
000011: - **AI Career Assistant** – Context-aware chat assistant that can analyze sessions, generate study plans, or answer follow-up questions (text + mic).
000012: - **Voice + Pose Intelligence** – Local Whisper transcription, Ollama-powered scoring, and MediaPipe pose coaching.
000013: - **Secure Backend APIs** – Express server with JWT auth, Firebase integrations, rate limiting, validation, and Socket.IO.
000014: 
000015: ---
000016: 
000017: ## 🧱 Architecture Snapshot
000018: 
000019: | Layer | Responsibilities | Key Tech |
000020: | --- | --- | --- |
000021: | Frontend (`src/`) | Vite/React SPA, dashboards, live interview UI, AI assistant, pose overlays | React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide, MediaPipe |
000022: | Backend (`server/`) | Auth, analytics, interview orchestration, Firebase + Supabase adapters, sockets | Node.js, Express, Firebase Admin, Socket.IO, Winston |
000023: | AI/ML Services | Local inference with zero API spend | Ollama (LLM), Whisper server (Python), MediaPipe |
000024: | Deployment | Static app via GitHub Pages + API hosted separately | GitHub Actions Pages workflow, ENV-based API URL |
000025: 
000026: ---
000027: 
000028: ## 🧰 Tech Stack
000029: 
000030: - **Core**: React 18, Vite 5, Tailwind CSS, Redux Toolkit, React Hook Form
000031: - **3rd Party UI/Dev**: Framer Motion, Lucide, Radix Slot, D3/Recharts
000032: - **Server**: Express 4, Firebase Admin, JWT, CORS/Helmet, Socket.IO, Winston
000033: - **AI + Realtime**: Local Ollama, Faster-Whisper server, MediaPipe Tasks Vision
000034: - **Tooling**: ESLint (CRA base), npm, GitHub Actions (Pages), Nodemon
000035: 
000036: ---
000037: 
000038: ## 📁 Project Structure
000039: 
000040: ```
000041: .
000042: ├── src/                     # React + Vite SPA
000043: │   ├── components/          # Shared UI + layout pieces
000044: │   ├── pages/               # Route-based feature modules
000045: │   ├── services/            # API, LLM, audio, pose helpers
000046: │   ├── hooks/contexts/      # State + feature hooks
000047: │   └── styles/              # Tailwind + global CSS
000048: ├── server/                  # Express API + socket server
000049: │   ├── src/                 # Config, controllers, middleware, routes
000050: │   ├── prisma/              # (placeholder for DB schema)
000051: │   └── whisper_server.py    # Optional local Whisper endpoint
000052: ├── public/                  # Static assets + manifest
000053: ├── .github/workflows/       # GitHub Pages deploy pipeline
000054: └── README.md                # You are here
000055: ```
000056: 
000057: ---
000058: 
000059: ## 🚀 Getting Started
000060: 
000061: ### Prerequisites
000062: 
000063: - Node.js 18+ and npm 9+
000064: - Python 3.10+ (if running the optional `whisper_server.py`)
000065: - Ollama installed locally for free LLM inference ([docs](https://ollama.ai))
000066: 
000067: ### 1. Clone & Install
000068: 
000069: ```bash
000070: git clone https://github.com/Akiyoshi02/InterviewAI-Pro.git
000071: cd InterviewAI-Pro
000072: npm install                 # Frontend dependencies
000073: 
000074: cd server
000075: npm install                 # Backend dependencies
000076: cd ..
000077: ```
000078: 
000079: ### 2. Environment Variables
000080: 
000081: Create a root `.env` for the Vite app:
000082: 
000083: ```bash
000084: VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
000085: VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY=...
000086: VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=...
000087: VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=...
000088: VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=...
000089: VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=...
000090: VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID=...
000091: VITE_OLLAMA_URL=http://localhost:11434
000092: VITE_OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b-instruct
000093: # Optional: Set VITE_LOCAL_WHISPER_URL if you are running a local Whisper server
000094: ```
000095: 
000096: Copy `server/.env.example` to `server/.env` and populate the values (Firebase Admin, Sightengine keys, Ollama, Whisper, etc.).
000097: 
000098: ### 3. Run Locally
000099: 
000100: ```bash
000101: # Terminal 1 – API + sockets
000102: cd server
000103: npm run dev
000104: 
000105: # Terminal 2 – Frontend
000106: cd ..
000107: npm run dev
000108: # default Vite port: 4028 (configured in vite.config.mjs)
000109: ```
000110: 
000111: Optional services:
000112: 
000113: - **Ollama**: `ollama run qwen2.5:7b-instruct --keepalive 1h` (or your chosen model)
000114: - **Local Whisper**: `python server/whisper_server.py`
000115: 
000116: ### Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Configuration
000117: 
000118: 1. `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b-instruct` (≈5.4 GB, runs well on 12 GB GPUs).
000119: 2. Set `VITE_OLLAMA_MODEL` and `OLLAMA_MODEL` to `qwen2.5:7b-instruct`.
000120: 3. The app automatically sends an optimized preset for Qwen: 8K context (`num_ctx=8192`), `gpu_layers=999`, `num_batch=256`, `top_k=40`, `top_p=0.9`, `temperature=0.65`, `repeat_penalty=1.08`, and generous `num_predict` limits. Override via the helper options only if you need different behavior.
000121: 
000122: ---
000123: 
000124: ## 📜 Available Scripts
000125: 
000126: | Location | Command | Description |
000127: | --- | --- | --- |
000128: | `/` | `npm run dev` | Launch Vite dev server |
000129: | `/` | `npm run build` | Production build to `build/` |
000130: | `/` | `npm run serve` | Preview built assets |
000131: | `/server` | `npm run dev` | Nodemon hot reload server |
000132: | `/server` | `npm start` | Start Express server |
000133: 
000134: ---
000135: 
000136: ## 🚢 Deployment (GitHub Pages + API)
000137: 
000138: - Static site is deployed via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. Every push to `main` builds the Vite app and publishes the `build/` folder to GitHub Pages.
000139: - Set the backend URL via `VITE_API_URL` to point to your hosted Express instance (e.g., Render, Railway, Fly.io, Supabase Edge Functions).
000140: - Remember to enable GitHub Pages → “GitHub Actions” in repo settings after the first successful workflow run.
000141: 
000142: ---
000143: 
000144: ## 🤝 Contribution Flow
000145: 
000146: 1. Branch from `main` using `feature/<kebab-description>` or `fix/<kebab-description>`.
000147: 2. Make focused changes + write conventional commits (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, etc.).
000148: 3. Open a PR back into `main` with a concise summary + testing notes (see project workflow memory).
000149: 4. Merge via GitHub UI; the Pages deploy workflow will run automatically.
000150: 
000151: ---
000152: 
000153: ## 📮 Support
000154: 
000155: Have questions or find a bug? Open an issue or ping in the PR comments and include:
000156: 
000157: - What you tried (screenshots/logs appreciated)
000158: - Whether you were running the local backend/LLM services
000159: - Steps to reproduce
000160: 
000161: Happy interviewing! 🎤💼
000162: 
000163:

000001: import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, jest } from '@jest/globals';

000238:   findActiveByJobAndEmail: jest.fn(async (organizationId, jobId, email) => {
000239:     const invitation = [...state.invitations.values()].find((item) => (
000240:       item.organizationId === organizationId
000241:       && item.jobId === jobId
000242:       && String(item.email || '').toLowerCase() === String(email || '').toLowerCase()

000246:   }),
000247:   claimForAcceptance: jest.fn(async (token, userId) => {
000248:     const invitation = [...state.invitations.values()].find((item) => item.token === token);
000249:     if (!invitation) {
000250:       return { status: 'NOT_FOUND', invitation: null };
000251:     }
000252:     if (invitation.status === 'PENDING') {
000253:       if (invitation.acceptanceInProgress) {
000254:         return { status: 'IN_PROGRESS', invitation: clone(invitation) };
000255:       }
000256:       const accepted = {
000257:         ...invitation,
000258:         status: 'ACCEPTED',
000259:         candidateUserId: userId,
000260:         acceptedAt: invitation.acceptedAt || nowIso(),
000261:         acceptanceInProgress: true,
000262:         acceptanceStartedAt: nowIso(),
000263:         updatedAt: nowIso(),
000264:       };
000265:       state.invitations.set(accepted.id, accepted);
000266:       return { status: 'CLAIMED', invitation: clone(accepted) };
000267:     }
000268:     if (invitation.status === 'ACCEPTED' && invitation.acceptedInterviewId) {
000269:       return { status: 'ALREADY_COMPLETED', invitation: clone(invitation) };
000270:     }
000271:     if (invitation.acceptanceInProgress) {
000272:       return { status: 'IN_PROGRESS', invitation: clone(invitation) };
000273:     }
000274:     return { status: 'UNAVAILABLE', invitation: clone(invitation) };
000275:   }),
000276:   finalizeAcceptance: jest.fn(async (invitationId, { interviewId = null, applicationId = null } = {}) => {
000277:     const invitation = state.invitations.get(invitationId);
000278:     if (!invitation) return null;
000279:     const updated = {
000280:       ...invitation,
000281:       status: 'ACCEPTED',
000282:       acceptanceInProgress: false,
000283:       acceptanceStartedAt: null,
000284:       acceptedInterviewId: interviewId || invitation.acceptedInterviewId || null,
000285:       acceptedApplicationId: applicationId || invitation.acceptedApplicationId || null,
000286:       updatedAt: nowIso(),
000287:     };
000288:     state.invitations.set(invitationId, updated);
000289:     return clone(updated);
000290:   }),
000291:   releaseAcceptanceLock: jest.fn(async (invitationId, options = {}) => {
000292:     const invitation = state.invitations.get(invitationId);
000293:     if (!invitation) return null;
000294:     const revertToPending = options?.revertToPending === true;
000295:     const updated = {
000296:       ...invitation,
000297:       ...(revertToPending
000298:         ? {
000299:           status: 'PENDING',
000300:           candidateUserId: null,
000301:           acceptedAt: null,
000302:           acceptedInterviewId: null,
000303:           acceptedApplicationId: null,
000304:         }
000305:         : {}),
000306:       acceptanceInProgress: false,
000307:       acceptanceStartedAt: null,
000308:       updatedAt: nowIso(),
000309:     };
000310:     state.invitations.set(invitationId, updated);
000311:     return clone(updated);
000312:   }),
000313: };

000322:   }

000324:   lines.push('## General Rotation Best Practices');

000448:           : 'fail',
000449:     details:
000450:       missingRequired.length === 0
000451:         ? 'All core identity and registration fields are present.'
000452:         : `Missing: ${missingRequired.join(', ')}`,
000453:   });
000454: 
000455:   if (!companyEmail) {
000456:     checks.push({
000457:       id: 'company-email',
000458:       label: 'Company contact email',
000459:       status: 'fail',
000460:       details: 'No dedicated company contact email was provided.',
000461:     });
000462:   } else if (!companyEmailDomain) {
000463:     checks.push({
000464:       id: 'company-email',
000465:       label: 'Company contact email',
000466:       status: 'warn',
000467:       details: `Company email "${companyEmail}" is not in a valid format.`,
000468:     });
000469:   } else if (FREE_EMAIL_DOMAINS.has(companyEmailDomain)) {
000470:     checks.push({
000471:       id: 'company-email',
000472:       label: 'Company contact email',
000473:       status: 'warn',
000474:       details: `Company email uses a public provider (${companyEmailDomain}) instead of a business domain.`,
000475:       evidence: { companyEmailDomain },
000476:     });
000477:   } else {
000478:     checks.push({
000479:       id: 'company-email',
000480:       label: 'Company contact email',
000481:       status: 'pass',
000482:       details: `Company email domain (${companyEmailDomain}) looks business-owned.`,
000483:       evidence: { companyEmailDomain },
000484:     });
000485:   }
000486: 
000487:   if (!websiteDomain || !companyEmailDomain) {
000488:     checks.push({
000489:       id: 'domain-alignment',
000490:       label: 'Email and website domain alignment',
000491:       status: 'warn',
000492:       details: 'Provide both website and company email to validate domain ownership.',
000493:       evidence: { websiteDomain, companyEmailDomain },
000494:     });
000495:   } else if (websiteDomain === companyEmailDomain) {
000496:     checks.push({
000497:       id: 'domain-alignment',
000498:       label: 'Email and website domain alignment',
000499:       status: 'pass',
000500:       details: 'Website and company email share the same domain.',
000501:       evidence: { websiteDomain, companyEmailDomain },
000502:     });
000503:   } else {
000504:     checks.push({
000505:       id: 'domain-alignment',
000506:       label: 'Email and website domain alignment',
000507:       status: 'fail',
000508:       details: `Website domain (${websiteDomain}) does not match company email domain (${companyEmailDomain}).`,
000509:       evidence: { websiteDomain, companyEmailDomain },
000510:     });
000511:   }
000512: 
000513:   if (!registrationNumber) {
000514:     checks.push({
000515:       id: 'registration-number',
000516:       label: 'Business registration number',
000517:       status: 'fail',
000518:       details: 'No business registration number was provided.',
000519:     });
000520:   } else if (insights && registrationMentionMatched) {
000521:     checks.push({
000522:       id: 'registration-number',
000523:       label: 'Business registration number',
000524:       status: 'pass',
000525:       details: 'Provided registration number appears in uploaded proof document.',
000526:     });
000527:   } else if (insights && registrationMentionPartial) {
000528:     checks.push({
000529:       id: 'registration-number',
000530:       label: 'Business registration number',
000531:       status: 'warn',
000532:       details: 'Document includes a similar registration number, but exact value was not matched.',
000533:       evidence: { extractedRegistrationCount: registrationMentions.length },
000534:     });
000535:   } else if (insights && registrationMentions.length > 0) {
000536:     checks.push({
000537:       id: 'registration-number',
000538:       label: 'Business registration number',
000539:       status: 'warn',
000540:       details: 'Document includes registration numbers, but exact provided value was not matched.',
000541:       evidence: { extractedRegistrationCount: registrationMentions.length },
000542:     });
000543:   } else if (insights) {
000544:     checks.push({
000545:       id: 'registration-number',
000546:       label: 'Business registration number',
000547:       status: 'warn',
000548:       details: 'Document analysis did not extract a registration number to cross-check.',
000549:     });
000550:   } else {
000551:     checks.push({
000552:       id: 'registration-number',
000553:       label: 'Business registration number',
000554:       status: 'info',
000555:       details: 'Registration number was provided, but document analysis is unavailable for comparison.',
000556:     });
000557:   }
000558: 
000559:   if (!owner?.companyVerificationUrl) {
000560:     checks.push({
000561:       id: 'verification-document',
000562:       label: 'Verification document quality',
000563:       status: 'fail',
000564:       details: 'No verification document is attached.',
000565:     });
000566:   } else if (!insights) {
000567:     checks.push({
000568:       id: 'verification-document',
000569:       label: 'Verification document quality',
000570:       status: 'warn',
000571:       details: 'Verification document exists, but extracted insights are unavailable.',
000572:     });
000573:   } else if (insights.countryMatchStatus === 'mismatch') {
000574:     checks.push({
000575:       id: 'verification-document',
000576:       label: 'Verification document quality',
000577:       status: 'fail',
000578:       details: 'Detected document jurisdiction does not match provided company location.',
000579:       evidence: {
000580:         expectedCountry: insights.expectedCountry || null,
000581:         detectedCountries: insights.detectedCountries || [],
000582:       },
000583:     });
000584:   } else if (authorityMentions.length > 0 && (registrationMentions.length > 0 || addressMentions.length > 0)) {
000585:     checks.push({
000586:       id: 'verification-document',
000587:       label: 'Verification document quality',
000588:       status: 'pass',
000589:       details: 'Document includes authority, registration, and/or address signals typically found in official records.',
000590:       evidence: {
000591:         authorityMentions: authorityMentions.length,
000592:         registrationMentions: registrationMentions.length,
000593:         addressMentions: addressMentions.length,
000594:       },
000595:     });
000596:   } else {
000597:     checks.push({
000598:       id: 'verification-document',
000599:       label: 'Verification document quality',
000600:       status: 'warn',
000601:       details: 'Document is attached but has weak official signals. Manual review is recommended.',
000602:       evidence: {
000603:         authorityMentions: authorityMentions.length,
000604:         registrationMentions: registrationMentions.length,
000605:       },
000606:     });
000607:   }
000608: 
000609:   const companyNameScore = typeof insights?.companyNameScore === 'number' ? insights.companyNameScore : null;
000610:   if (companyNameScore == null) {
000611:     checks.push({
000612:       id: 'company-name-match',
000613:       label: 'Company name found in document',
000614:       status: insights ? 'warn' : 'info',
000615:       details: insights
000616:         ? 'Document analysis could not confidently score company name matching.'
000617:         : 'Company name matching skipped because insights are unavailable.',
000618:     });
000619:   } else if (companyNameScore >= 0.6) {
000620:     checks.push({
000621:       id: 'company-name-match',
000622:       label: 'Company name found in document',
000623:       status: 'pass',
000624:       details: `Company name match score is ${(companyNameScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%.`,
000625:     });
000626:   } else if (companyNameScore >= 0.35) {
000627:     checks.push({
000628:       id: 'company-name-match',
000629:       label: 'Company name found in document',
000630:       status: 'warn',
000631:       details: `Company name match score is ${(companyNameScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%, verify manually.`,
000632:     });
000633:   } else {
000634:     checks.push({
000635:       id: 'company-name-match',
000636:       label: 'Company name found in document',
000637:       status: 'fail',
000638:       details: `Company name match score is ${(companyNameScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%, likely mismatch.`,
000639:     });
000640:   }
000641: 
000642:   const recentDocumentDate = toIsoDate(insights?.mostRecentDate);
000643:   if (!insights) {
000644:     checks.push({
000645:       id: 'document-recency',
000646:       label: 'Document recency',
000647:       status: 'info',
000648:       details: 'Recency not scored because document insights are unavailable.',
000649:     });
000650:   } else if (!recentDocumentDate) {
000651:     checks.push({
000652:       id: 'document-recency',
000653:       label: 'Document recency',
000654:       status: 'warn',
000655:       details: 'Document date could not be extracted. Consider requesting a clearer copy.',
000656:     });
000657:   } else {
000658:     const ageYears = yearsSince(recentDocumentDate);
000659:     if (ageYears != null && ageYears <= 3) {
000660:       checks.push({
000661:         id: 'document-recency',
000662:         label: 'Document recency',
000663:         status: 'pass',
000664:         details: 'Document appears recent (within approximately 3 years).',
000665:         evidence: { mostRecentDate: recentDocumentDate },
000666:       });
000667:     } else {
000668:       checks.push({
000669:         id: 'document-recency',
000670:         label: 'Document recency',
000671:         status: 'warn',
000672:         details: 'Document appears older than 3 years. Confirm the company is currently active.',
000673:         evidence: { mostRecentDate: recentDocumentDate },
000674:       });
000675:     }
000676:   }
000677: 
000678:   const footprintSignals = [
000679:     Boolean(website),
000680:     Boolean(organization?.linkedinUrl || owner?.companyLinkedinUrl),
000681:     Boolean(organization?.address || owner?.companyLocation),
000682:   ];
000683:   const footprintCount = footprintSignals.filter(Boolean).length;
000684:   checks.push({
000685:     id: 'public-footprint',
000686:     label: 'Public footprint',
000687:     status: footprintCount >= 2 ? 'pass' : 'warn',
000688:     details:
000689:       footprintCount >= 2
000690:         ? 'Website plus at least one additional public signal is available.'
000691:         : footprintCount === 1
000692:           ? 'Only one public signal is available. Collect more evidence if needed.'
000693:           : 'No public website, social profile, or address signal is available.',
000694:   });
000695: 
000696:   const summary = checks.reduce(
000697:     (acc, check) => {
000698:       const status = normalizeCheckStatus(check.status);
000699:       acc[status] += 1;
000700:       acc.total += 1;
000701:       return acc;
000702:     },
000703:     { pass: 0, warn: 0, fail: 0, info: 0, total: 0 },
000704:   );
000705: 
000706:   const riskFlags = [];
000707:   if (summary.fail > 0) {
000708:     riskFlags.push('At least one critical verification check failed.');
000709:   }
000710:   if (missingRequired.length > 0) {
000711:     riskFlags.push(`Missing core fields: ${missingRequired.join(', ')}.`);
000712:   }
000713:   if (companyEmailDomain && FREE_EMAIL_DOMAINS.has(companyEmailDomain)) {
000714:     riskFlags.push('Company contact uses a public email provider.');
000715:   }
000716:   if (websiteDomain && companyEmailDomain && websiteDomain !== companyEmailDomain) {
000717:     riskFlags.push('Company website and email domain mismatch.');
000718:   }
000719:   if (insights?.countryMatchStatus === 'mismatch') {
000720:     riskFlags.push('Document country does not match provided company location.');
000721:   }
000722:   if (!owner?.companyVerificationUrl) {
000723:     riskFlags.push('No verification document attached.');
000724:   }
000725: 
000726:   let recommendationLevel = 'ready';
000727:   let recommendationLabel = 'Ready for approval';
000728:   let recommendationReason = 'All critical identity checks passed with limited risk.';
000729: 
000730:   if (summary.fail > 0) {
000731:     recommendationLevel = 'high_risk';
000732:     recommendationLabel = 'High risk - require clarification';
000733:     recommendationReason = 'One or more critical checks failed. Request additional evidence before approval.';
000734:   } else if (summary.warn >= 3 || summary.info >= 2) {
000735:     recommendationLevel = 'caution';
000736:     recommendationLabel = 'Needs manual review';
000737:     recommendationReason = 'No critical failures, but multiple warnings require manual verification.';
000738:   }
000739: 
000740:   return {
000741:     summary,
000742:     recommendation: {
000743:       level: recommendationLevel,
000744:       label: recommendationLabel,
000745:       reason: recommendationReason,
000746:     },
000747:     checks: checks.map((check) => ({
000748:       ...check,
000749:       status: normalizeCheckStatus(check.status),
000750:     })),
000751:     riskFlags,
000752:     domainSignals: {
000753:       websiteDomain,
000754:       companyEmailDomain,
000755:       ownerEmailDomain,
000756:       ownerEmailIsPublic: ownerEmailDomain ? FREE_EMAIL_DOMAINS.has(ownerEmailDomain) : null,
000757:     },
000758:     organizationProfile: {
000759:       legalName: organization?.name || null,
000760:       displayName: organization?.displayName || null,
000761:       industry: organization?.industry || owner?.industry || null,
000762:       companySize: organization?.companySize || owner?.companySize || null,
000763:       companyType: owner?.companyType || null,
000764:       hiringVolume: owner?.hiringVolume || null,
000765:       website: website || null,
000766:       location: owner?.companyLocation || null,
000767:       address: organization?.address || owner?.companyLocation || null,
000768:       description: organization?.description || null,
000769:       establishedYear: owner?.establishedYear || null,
000770:       registrationNumber: registrationNumber || null,
000771:       socialLinks: {
000772:         linkedin: organization?.linkedinUrl || owner?.companyLinkedinUrl || null,
000773:         facebook: organization?.facebookUrl || null,
000774:         youtube: organization?.youtubeUrl || null,
000775:       },
000776:     },
000777:     ownerProfile: owner
000778:       ? {
000779:         id: owner.id,
000780:         fullName: owner.fullName || null,
000781:         email: owner.email || null,
000782:         phoneNumber: owner.phoneNumber || null,
000783:         jobTitle: owner.jobTitle || null,
000784:         department: owner.department || null,
000785:         companyEmail: owner.companyEmail || null,
000786:         companyLocation: owner.companyLocation || null,
000787:         hiringVolume: owner.hiringVolume || null,
000788:         accountCreatedAt: owner.createdAt || null,
000789:       }
000790:       : null,
000791:     evidence: {
000792:       companyLogoUrl: organization?.logo || owner?.companyLogoUrl || null,
000793:       verificationDocumentUrl: owner?.companyVerificationUrl || null,
000794:       verificationDocumentName: owner?.companyVerificationOriginalName || null,
000795:       verificationDocumentHash: owner?.companyVerificationHash || null,
000796:       verificationInsights: insights,
000797:     },
000798:   };
000799: };
